A Ward that leaves lasting memory behind: use it on yourself and you are held safe from Rewind for good. Made on the Antibody Bench, after Immune Memory.
pages.title: Lasting Rewind Ward

pages.text: Made in $(item)Clonal Selector$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Immune Memory.

Two sheets of fat molecules, tails inward, heads out to the water: the skin of every cell, five nanometres thick and self-sealing. Made on the Patch-Clamp Rig from egg yolk lecithin.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Macrophage (Inner Space (Tumour, Bloodstream, Lymph Node ...)).
pages.title: Lipid Bilayer

pages.text: Made in $(item)Patch-Clamp Rig$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Macrophage.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bsl4 Field Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Membranes.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cell Membrane, Ion Channel Membrane, Living Cell, Perfused Tissue.
An enzyme in a living cell that remakes it as fast as it wears: a catalyst that never quite runs down while it is fed. Used as a catalyst, it heals its own wear. Made on the Gene Circuit Loom.
pages.title: Living Catalyst

pages.text: Made in $(item)Gene Circuit Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Gene Circuits.

A membrane holding a working machine inside: ribosomes, enzymes and a charge across its skin, burning sugar for its living. The first piece of the Tree of Life. It dies if carried about too long. Made on the Patch-Clamp Rig.
pages.title: Living Cell

pages.text: Made in $(item)Patch-Clamp Rig$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Respiration.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Circadian Culture, Living Catalyst, Miniaturiser, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Mirror Cell, Perfused Tissue, Tree of Life.

The clear jelly of a brine jelly's bell, still faintly glowing: almost all water, held in a web of collagen. Dropped by Brine Jellies in Titan's hidden ocean. It lights membranes, and the Chemical Reactor draws a gel from it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Brine Jelly (Titan's Hidden Ocean (Subsurface Ocean, Hydrothermal Vents)).
pages.title: Luminous Mesoglea

pages.text: $(thing)Dropped by$(): Brine Jelly.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bioluminescent Membrane.

Packed lymphocytes and the mesh that holds them, where invaders are shown to the cells that will fight them. Found on the surface of Inner Space's Lymph Node. The Antibody Bench raises Memory Cells from it; matrix and a memory cell make more.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Inner Space.
pages.title: Lymph Tissue

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Germinal Centre chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Memory Cell.

Collagen, the rope that holds a body together: three chains wound round each other into a fibre stronger than steel for its weight. Found in collagen seams in Inner Space's tissue. The Regeneration Tank spins more from tissue and bone.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Collagen Seam in Inner Space (Bloodstream, Lymph Node, Tissue); dropped by the Macrophage (Inner Space (Tumour, Bloodstream, Lymph Node ...)).
pages.title: Matrix Fibre

pages.text: Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Collagen Seam$(), in veins through the rock.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Macrophage.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Ribosome Workshop chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Collagen Seam, Extracellular Matrix, Grown Organ.
An antibody bred over many rounds of selection, each round keeping only the clones that bind best, until it fits its target a thousand times more tightly. Made in the Clonal Selector.
pages.title: Matured Antibody

pages.text: Made in $(item)Clonal Selector$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Affinity Maturation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Lasting Fracture Ward, Lasting Grey Goo Ward, Lasting Hollowing Ward, Lasting Metastasis Ward, Lasting Rewind Ward, Metastasis Ward.

A lymphocyte that has met an invader once and never forgets it: years later it wakes and answers in hours. Dropped by T Cells and kept in the Germinal Centres of Inner Space's Lymph Node; the Antibody Bench raises more from lymph tissue.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the T Cell (Inner Space (Tumour, Nucleus, Lymph Node)).
pages.title: Memory Cell

pages.text: Made in $(item)Antibody Bench$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): T Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Germinal Centre chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antibody, CAR-T Cell Culture, Lymph Tissue, Matured Antibody.

A working copy of one gene, read off the DNA to be carried to a ribosome: the message between the genome and the protein. Made on the Ribosome Assembler.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Polymerase (Inner Space (Nucleus)).
pages.title: Messenger RNA

pages.text: Made in $(item)Ribosome Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Polymerase.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Nuclear Pore, Ribosome Workshop chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Transcription.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Engineered Enzyme, Folded Protein Crystal, Gene Circuit, Gene Circuit Loom, Living Cell.

CH₄, the simplest hydrocarbon: the cloud's carbon, the Fuel Cell's fuel, and a Cracking Tower's feed.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the caches of Abandoned Refinery structures in Titan (Ontario Lacus Basin, Kraken Mare).
pages.title: Methane

pages.text: Made in $(item)Fractionation Spire$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Fermentation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hydrogen Cyanide, Methane, Tholin, Water.

A ring of lenses round a capsule, after the 1966 film Fantastic Voyage: it shrinks whoever stands in it until a body's cells are the size of houses, and sets them down inside one. Used in the Overworld it takes you into Inner Space; used there, it brings you back out.
pages.title: Miniaturiser

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Pharmacokinetics.

An antibody built mirror-handed, the one shape that fits a mirror microbe. Use it on yourself: held safe from the Mirror Plague of the Antiverse's Mirror Microbes for three in-game days (no other ward holds it). Made in the Mirror Culture Vat.
pages.title: Mirror Antibody

pages.text: Made in $(item)Mirror Culture Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mirror Life.

A cell built left-handed where life is right, and right where life is left: its own mirror image. Nothing alive can eat it, and it can eat nothing alive. It dies if carried about too long. Made in the Mirror Culture Vat.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Mirror Microbe.
pages.title: Mirror Cell

pages.text: Made in $(item)Mirror Culture Vat$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Mirror Microbe.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mirror Life.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Mirror Antibody.

$(thing)Mirror Microbe$(): A bacterium built mirror-handed, as everything in the Antiverse is. Nothing alive can digest it, and nothing in a body can grip it: its touch gives the Mirror Plague, which no Anomaly Ward holds. Only a Mirror Antibody wards it. Found drifting in the Antiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Chiral Crystal, Mirror Cell.
pages.title: Mirror Microbe

pages.text: Every signal an embryo listens to, in one vial. A Breached Anomaly Engine spends one on every creature it grows.
pages.title: Morphogenic Serum

pages.text: Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity.
Penicillium, the blue-green mould on old bread. Fleming saw it kill the bacteria around it in 1928. It dies if carried about too long. Made on the Mycelium Bed.
pages.title: Mould Culture

pages.text: Made in $(item)Mycelium Bed$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Bsl4 Field Station chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Mycology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Antibiotic, Physarum Culture.

A pea-sized brain grown in a dish: real neurons, folded and connected, with no body around them. Its electrical activity has started to look like the patterns of a sleeping brain. I try not to think about what it might be dreaming about.
pages.title: Neural Organoid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brain organoids are a real technology. I grew stem cells around a thought matrix with a room-temperature superconductor for wiring and fed them synaptic fluid. Within days the electrodes recorded coordinated waves.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neurobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Boltzmann Brain, Cognitive Singularity, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Superintelligence Core, Xenobot Swarm.

A sugar, a phosphate and one of four bases: a single letter of the genetic code. Found in nucleotide clusters in the Nucleus of Inner Space; the Fermenter draws more out of yeast.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Nucleotide Cluster in Inner Space (Nucleus); dropped by the Polymerase (Inner Space (Nucleus)).
pages.title: Nucleotide

pages.text: Made in $(item)Fermenter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Nucleotide Cluster$(), in veins through the rock.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Polymerase.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Nuclear Pore chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chromatin, Messenger RNA, Nucleotide Cluster.
Found in Inner Space, between Y 8 and 200. Gives Nucleotide when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Nucleotide Cluster

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Inner Space.

A warm, rich medium for growing cells. Sugar provides energy, bone meal provides minerals, and a zeolite catalyst keeps the chemistry steady. It smells faintly sweet. Left uncovered for even a moment, it clouds with whatever life drifts into it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the caches of Bsl4 Field Stations.
pages.title: Nutrient Broth

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Life needs food. In the Bioreactor, I combined sugar, bone meal and water with a zeolite catalyst, and the broth supported growth.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Molecular Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor, Engineered Enzyme, Folded Protein Crystal, Immortal Cell Line, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum and more.

One genome that can build any creature in any dimension; carbon or silicon, DNA or not. It is a coiled, shifting helix that seems to shift as I watch. Every living thing I have met is a sentence it can write.
pages.title: Omnicellular Genome

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed the Evolution Engine a panspermia seed, a silicon life spore, a neural organoid, recombinant DNA and Xenoplasm and let it evolve a single code that could express all of them. It took less time than I thought.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Simulacrum, Bubble Universe, Omnilex Seal, Pocket Universe, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

A seed packed with life designed to survive the trip between universes. Tardigrade toughness, a spark of life and unbihexium shielding, all sealed in a capsule that seems to hold a small universe of its own. It is light and very still.
pages.title: Panspermia Seed

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Panspermia supposes life travels between worlds. I wanted it to travel between universes. The Abiogenesis Crucible sealed a spark of life with tardigrades, Xenoplasm and primordial soup inside a bubble universe shielded by unbihexium.
Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Panspermia.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnicellular Genome, Omnilex Seal, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

A figure forever meeting its own past. It acts out the grandfather paradox, flickering whenever its history stops adding up.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Paradox Residue, Chronon Capacitor, Closed Timelike Curve.
pages.title: Paradox Echo

pages.text: A sheet of living cells kept alive by a network of fine channels carrying nutrient and oxygen to every one, as blood does. It dies if carried about too long. Made on the Perfusion Rig.
pages.title: Perfused Tissue

pages.text: Made in $(item)Perfusion Rig$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Circulation.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Grown Organ, Matrix Fibre, Miniaturiser, Stem Cell Culture, Symbiont Lining.

A single yellow cell the size of a plate, with millions of nuclei. Set oat flakes out as cities and it links them with the shortest network it can: it once laid out Tokyo's railways. It dies if carried about too long. Made on the Mycelium Bed.
pages.title: Physarum Culture

pages.text: Made in $(item)Mycelium Bed$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Slime Moulds.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Network Map.

The chemical mixture from which life arose. Morphogens, chiral crystals and superacids give it the ingredients for self-replication. It is warm and bubbles slowly. Miller and Urey made amino acids in a flask of sparks; this goes much further.
pages.title: Primordial Soup

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis needs the right chemistry. In the Chemical Reactor, I combined a Turing Morphogen with chiral crystal, clathrate and superacid, and the soup began to organise itself.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Panspermia Seed, Spark of Life.

A lining of harmless bacteria that hold every surface, so nothing harmful finds room to grow. Fitted to a Biology console, it is never contaminated again. One upgrade per machine. Made in the Fermenter.
pages.title: Probiotic Seal

pages.text: Made in $(item)Fermenter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Probiotics.

A double helix spliced together from more than one creature, its pieces joined by enzymes that cut and paste at precise sequences. It looks no different from any other DNA, yet does things no single creature's DNA could.
pages.title: Recombinant DNA

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Restriction enzymes cut genomes at precise points; ligases stitch them back. I let engineered enzymes splice two samples together in a nutrient broth, and the Gene Sequencer read back a genome that had never existed before.

Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apoptosis Trigger, CAR-T Cell Culture, Chronoplastic Gasket, Folded Protein Crystal, Minimal Synthetic Cell, Morphogenic Serum, Omnicellular Genome, Stem Cell Culture.
$(thing)Antibodies$()$(br2)A tip that fits one shape alone, out of billions the body can make. Bound to an invader, it marks it for clearing, or blocks the key it uses to get in.
pages.title: Antibodies

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 130$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Adaptive Immunity.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Antibody.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Antibody at level L binds a target with dissociation constant K. Write the share B of targets bound.
$(thing)Biomineralisation$()$(br2)Some bacteria grow chains of magnetite crystals and steer by the Earth's field. Kept short of air, they mine iron for you. Unlocks bacterial Magnetite.
pages.title: Biomineralisation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Microbiology, Ferromagnetism.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Bacterial Culture, 8 Iron Nugget.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A chain of n magnetite crystals, each of moment m, lines up in a field B against the jostling of heat, kT. Write the share A it lines up by, for a weak field, m·n·B over three kT.
$(thing)Circulation$()$(br2)The heart pushes blood through vessels that branch finer and finer; the flow in each follows the fourth power of its radius. Unlocks Perfused Tissue.
pages.title: Circulation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Physiology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Living Cell, 4 Redstone.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Flow through a vessel goes as the fourth power of its radius (Poiseuille). A vessel of radius r carries a base flow; write the flow Q for radius r, from a constant c.
$(thing)Extremophiles$()$(br2)Life at the edges: boiling vents, frozen vacuum, radiation. Unlocks tardigrade cultures.
pages.title: Extremophiles

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Genomics, Cryogenics, Microbiology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A reaction proceeds only when molecules reach a short-lived activated complex at the top of the energy barrier. Treat that complex as in equilibrium with the reactants and let it fall apart at the universal frequency kB·T/h, with a transmission coefficient κ. Write the rate constant in terms of the activation enthalpy and activation entropy (molar).
$(thing)Immune Memory$()$(br2)Memory cells that outlive the fight and answer at once the next time, for years. Unlocks lasting Wards, held safe for good.
pages.title: Immune Memory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 180$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Immunisation, Directed Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Fracture Ward, 1 Telomerase Complex.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Memory falls off slowly, by a half-life T. Write the share S still protected after a time t.
$(thing)Immunisation$()$(br2)Show the body a harmless trace of an invader and it is ready for the real one. Unlocks an Anomaly Ward for each of the Anomaly's infections.
pages.title: Immunisation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 140$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Antibodies.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Antibody, 2 Fractured Essence.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A disease spreads at R0. Write the share H that must be held safe so each case makes less than one more (herd immunity).
$(thing)Innate Immunity$()$(br2)The body's first answer, the same for every invader: cells that engulf what does not belong, and inflammation that walls it off. Unlocks Antibodies.
pages.title: Innate Immunity

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Microbiology, Respiration.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Bacterial Culture, 1 Living Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A phagocyte clears invaders at a rate proportional to how many are left: dN/dt = -cN. Write how many remain, M, after time t, from a start of N.

$(thing)Inner Space$()$(br2)A body, seen from the inside at the scale of its cells. Unlocks the Miniaturiser that takes you there, and the materials of its five regions: plasma, matrix fibre, memory cells, nucleotides and tumour specimens. In its Tumour, a Metastatic Spore calls the Tumour Hydra.
pages.title: Inner Space

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 160$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Circulation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Perfused Tissue, 2 Living Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A body of size l moves at speed u through a fluid of density p and viscosity m. Write the ratio R of its inertia to the fluid's stickiness, which says whether inertia or stickiness wins.
$(thing)Lysogeny$()$(br2)Some phages do not burst their host at once: they write themselves into its genome and wait. A way to deliver genes. Unlocks cheap Recombinant DNA.
pages.title: Lysogeny

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Viruses.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Bacteriophage.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): c cells are infected; a share f of them burst at once, each releasing B phages. Write how many new phages, P, come out.
$(thing)Membrane Potential$()$(br2)Let potassium leak out through its channels and the inside of the cell goes negative, until the voltage holds it back: Nernst. Unlocks Ion Channel Membranes.
pages.title: Membrane Potential

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Membranes, Galvanic Cells.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Lipid Bilayer.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Ions of charge z are at c outside and q inside. Write the voltage E (in mV, at body heat) that holds them in balance.
$(thing)Metabolism$()$(br2)A cell is a chemical network: hundreds of enzymes in chains and cycles, each feeding the next. Unlocks the Fermenter.
pages.title: Metabolism

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Membranes, Enzyme Kinetics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Assayed Enzyme.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A chain of n enzymes each passes on a share f of what it is given. A amount of sugar goes in; write the amount Y that reaches the end.
$(thing)Microbiology$()$(br2)Most life is too small to see, and doubles every twenty minutes while the food lasts. Unlocks Bacterial Cultures.
pages.title: Microbiology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Fermentation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Yeast Culture, 4 Bone Meal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Bacteria double every g minutes. Starting from N cells, write how many there are, M, after t minutes.
$(thing)Morphogenesis$()$(br2)How a blob of identical cells paints itself into a body: reaction and diffusion. Unlocks Turing morphogens.
pages.title: Morphogenesis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Complex Analysis, Reaction and Diffusion.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Minimal Synthetic Cell.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An activator molecule a spreads by diffusion, catalyses its own production (in proportion to a² and inhibited by a second molecule h, with saturation κ at high a), decays at rate μ, and is also produced at a small basal rate. Write the rate of change of the activator concentration.
$(thing)Neurobiology$()$(br2)Grow a brain in a dish and ask it what it thinks. Unlocks neural organoids.
pages.title: Neurobiology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Artificial General Intelligence.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Stem Cell Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Ions of valence z and concentration C(x) cross a cell membrane. They drift down their concentration gradient with diffusion constant D, and are also pushed by the electric field from the membrane potential V(x). Write the ion flux j as the sum of both effects, using the thermal energy per mole RT and the charge per mole zF.
$(thing)Panspermia$()$(br2)Life carried between worlds, and between universes. Unlocks panspermia seeds and the omnicellular genome.
pages.title: Panspermia

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 450$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Abiogenesis, The Multiverse, The Island of Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Spark of Life.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Spores ride inside a rock between worlds for time t. Radiation at dose rate R is attenuated by the rock (absorption coefficient μ, depth x), and a spore dies only when all m of its sensitive targets are hit, each target surviving a dose D with probability exp(−D/D0). Write the surviving fraction after the journey.
$(thing)Predator and Prey$()$(br2)More prey feed more predators, more predators eat more prey, and so it cycles, round and round. Unlocks Stable Ecosystems and the Symbiont Lining.
pages.title: Predator and Prey

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 160$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Ecology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Algae Culture, 2 Bacterial Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Prey settle at the level where predators neither grow nor shrink: predator death g against gain d per prey. Write that prey level X.
$(thing)Probiotics$()$(br2)Fill every surface with harmless bacteria and nothing harmful finds room: competitive exclusion. Unlocks the Probiotic Seal.
pages.title: Probiotics

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Microbiology, Sterile Technique.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Bacterial Culture, 2 Sterile Pack.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A harmful strain grows at rate r, but only into the room the friendly ones leave: N of a capacity K is already taken. Write its growth rate G.

$(thing)Respiration$()$(br2)With air, a cell burns sugar all the way to carbon dioxide and gets fifteen times as much from it, pumping protons across a membrane to drive its turbine. Unlocks the Living Cell.
pages.title: Respiration

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Metabolism, Membrane Potential.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Ion Channel Membrane, 2 Yeast Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A proton gradient of p pH units and a voltage V (mV) drive the turbine together. Write the total push F, in mV, 59 mV for each pH unit.

$(thing)Slime Moulds$()$(br2)Physarum is one cell that spreads toward food and keeps only the tubes that carry most: a network that solves shortest paths. Unlocks Physarum Cultures and cheap Network Maps.
pages.title: Slime Moulds

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Mycology, Networks.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Mould Culture, 1 Network Map.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A tube of conductance D carries flow along a pressure drop p over a length L. Write the flow Q.
$(thing)Stem Cells$()$(br2)A cell that can become any other, waiting to be told which. The seed of every organ, and of regrowing one. Unlocks the Regeneration Tank.
pages.title: Stem Cells

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 130$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Physiology, Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Stem Cell Culture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A culture of stem cells doubles every d days. Write how many, M, there are after t days, from a start of N.
$(thing)Tolerance$()$(br2)The body must also know not to attack itself: regulatory cells that call off the response. Reality has them too, and a breach is read as self. Law Wraiths leave you be.
pages.title: Tolerance

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 160$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Adaptive Immunity.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Antibody, 1 Crystallised Law.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Effector cells of number E are held down by regulatory cells R, each damping by g. Write the net drive D they have left.

$(thing)Translation$()$(br2)The ribosome reads the message three letters at a time and strings the amino acids together: the genetic code. Unlocks cheap Engineered Enzymes and a new Synthetic Cell route.
pages.title: Translation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Transcription.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Messenger RNA, 4 Amino Acid Mixture.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A ribosome gets each of L codons wrong with chance ε. Write the share Y of chains with no mistake at all.

$(thing)The Tree of Life$()$(br2)Every living thing on one branching tree from a single root, four billion years deep. The five pieces of life, from the cell to the biosphere, make one endgame catalyst that never wears.
pages.title: The Tree of Life

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 300$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Predator and Prey, Gene Circuits, Immune Memory, Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Living Cell, 1 Grown Organ, 1 Stable Ecosystem.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A branching tree doubles its tips at each of g levels. Write how many tips T it ends with, from one root.
$(thing)Xenobiology$()$(br2)Life in other dimensions does not use DNA. Unlocks xenogenome work, Xenoplasm and silicon life.
pages.title: Xenobiology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 130$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Synthetic Biology, Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An alien genome is a string of L letters drawn from an alphabet of b chemically distinct bases, base j appearing with probability p_j. Write the information it can store, in bits: the length times the average surprise per letter, built from the probabilities and their logarithms, converted from natural units to bits.

A spore built on silicon instead of carbon; a speculative chemistry that only works in the strange physics of the Bulk. It is glassy, faceted and very slightly warm, and it ticks quietly, as though growing at the pace of crystal.
pages.title: Silicon Life Spore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Silicon life has always been a thought experiment. In the Bulk, where chemistry runs differently, I seeded a minimal cell with a xenogenome and Xenoplasm on a bulk crystal. The spore that grew was neither carbon nor stone.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm.

A small bright point that is the moment chemistry crossed into biology; self-replication, metabolism and a boundary, all arriving at once. It flickers unsteadily. Holding it feels like holding a match that might become a forest.
pages.title: Spark of Life

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Abiogenesis is the unsolved step. I put primordial soup, stellar plasma and the omega point in the Abiogenesis Crucible with telomerase, a minimal cell and quantum chlorophyll, and caught the instant it all started to copy itself.

Made in $(item)Abiogenesis Crucible$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abiogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omnilex Seal, Omniscience Catalyst, Ontological Junction, Panspermia Seed, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.
A substance metered out so its level in the body stays steady, between too little to work and enough to harm: the pharmacist's art. Made on the Dosing Pump.
pages.title: Stable Dose

pages.text: Made in $(item)Dosing Pump$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Pharmacokinetics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Miniaturiser.

A sealed world in balance: producers, grazers and hunters whose numbers rise and fall around each other without ever crashing or exploding. The fifth piece of the Tree of Life. It dies if carried about too long. Made in the Ecosphere.
pages.title: Stable Ecosystem

pages.text: Made in $(item)Ecosphere$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Predator and Prey.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Tree of Life.

A mix of ways to behave that, once common, nothing else can invade: Maynard Smith's answer to why animals mostly fight by display. Recorded at the Strategy Table. The Bioreactor grows Tardigrade Cultures cheaply with one.
pages.title: Evolutionarily Stable Strategy

pages.text: Made in $(item)Strategy Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Evolutionary Games.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Tardigrade Culture.

Swabs, wipes and a fresh filter, sealed and steamed in the Autoclave until not one spore in a trillion is left alive. Use it on a Biology machine to bring it back to fully sterile and clear any contamination. Made in the Autoclave.
pages.title: Sterile Pack

A living skin of helpful microbes grown to line a machine, repairing and renewing its catalysts as they work. Fitted to a machine, its catalysts wear 40% slower. One upgrade per machine. Made in the Ecosphere.
pages.title: Symbiont Lining

pages.text: Made in $(item)Ecosphere$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Predator and Prey.

A culture of water bears, tiny eight-legged animals that survive vacuum, radiation and freezing by drying out and simply pausing being alive. In the jar they wander slowly through moss. Dried, they will wait for centuries.
pages.title: Tardigrade Culture

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Extremophiles taught me that life could survive almost anything. I used engineered enzymes to boost a tardigrade genome's repair genes, gave them moss to live in and froze a culture in superfluid helium. It woke up.
Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Extremophiles.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Chronoplastic Gasket, Panspermia Seed, Telomerase Complex.

An enzyme that rebuilds telomeres; the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides. Cells that have it do not age. The complex is small, pale and oddly cold, as if keeping time for itself.
pages.title: Telomerase Complex

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Telomerase is real; most adult cells have switched it off. The Evolution Engine ran a million generations of stem cells and tardigrades with Turing morphogens and Xenoplasm, while an arrow of time shard kept the clock running fast.

Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Directed Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Immortal Cell Line, Omnilex Seal, Ontological Junction, Spark of Life, Transfinite Lattice Bolt.

Every living thing, from the first cell to the whole biosphere, on one branching tree from a single root. As a catalyst it never wears. The keystone of Biology. Made in the Ecosphere from the five pieces of life.
pages.title: Tree of Life

pages.text: Made in $(item)Ecosphere$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Tree of Life.

Riftia: worms two metres long with no mouth and no gut, living on the bacteria inside them, which live on the vent's sulfide. Their red plumes are full of haemoglobin. Found round the vents of Titan's hidden ocean, where they spread by themselves near a black smoker. The Fermenter grows Bacterial Cultures from their symbionts.
pages.title: Giant Tube Worms

pages.text: $(thing)Used in$(): Bacterial Culture.

$(thing)Tumour Hydra$(): A mound of overgrown tissue as wide as a house, with heads on long necks growing out of every side. Its body only walks to keep the heads in reach; the heads bite. Strike a head or anywhere along its neck: every 30 damage cuts that head off (a blow to the body is mostly soaked up). The stump stays where the head was, open for five seconds: seal it with fire, or strike it with a CAR-T Cell Culture or an Apoptosis Trigger, and that head is gone for good; leave it, and it grows back with another beside it. With no heads left, blows to the body land in full and it can be killed. Its bite carries Metastasis. Called with a Metastatic Spore on open ground in the Tumour of Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tumour Specimen, Immortal Cell Line, Metastatic Spore.
pages.title: Tumour Hydra

Living machines a millimetre across, built from cells arranged in shapes no animal ever had. They walk, push, heal and even assemble copies of themselves from loose cells. They twitch in the jar, busy.
pages.title: Xenobot Swarm

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobots were real: frog cells arranged by an evolutionary algorithm. I gave a general AI core stem cells and nanites to design with, and the Bioreactor built whatever shape it picked. Some of them built more of themselves.
Made in $(item)Evolution Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Synthetic Biology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Symbiont Culture, Xenobot Swarm.

A vial of something that is clearly a genome but is not DNA. The molecule folds the wrong way, uses letters I do not recognise and carries information more densely than any terrestrial code. It glows faintly in the dark.
pages.title: Xenogenome Sample

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I sampled a creature from another dimension expecting DNA and found something else. Life evolved under different physics, with a different chemistry of inheritance, and it was still readable.
Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Silicon Life Spore, Xenobot Swarm, Xenoplasm.

Life fluid from another dimension. It does not use DNA, and its chemistry is foreign. It is warm, iridescent and moves on its own. Its molecules are built on a backbone no terrestrial cell would recognise, and their handedness alternates in ways that should be unstable. Somehow it thrives on that instability.
pages.title: Xenoplasm

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Xenobiology studies life without DNA. In the Bioreactor, I combined a Xenogenome Sample with foam substrate and nutrient broth, and the culture grew as no Earth life could.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Xenobiology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metastatic Spore, Omnicellular Genome, Panspermia Seed, Silicon Life Spore, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid.

Photosynthesis moves energy through its antenna with near-perfect efficiency by trying every path at once, coherently. A robin feels north through a pair of electrons entangled in a protein in its eye.

From these: $(item)Quantum Chlorophyll$() and the $(item)Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor$(), which Psionic Crystals now need. $(item)Tardigrade Cultures$() come from the extremophiles: animals that survive vacuum by pausing life itself.
Photosynthesis moves energy by trying every path at once, coherently.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().
The protein in a robin's eye that feels Earth's field through entangled radical pairs.$(br2)Made in $(item)Gene Sequencer$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Quantum Chlorophyll$(): Spark of Life$(li)$(item)Cryptochrome Magnetoreceptor$(): Psionic Crystal$(li)$(item)Tardigrade Culture$(): Chronoplastic Gasket, Panspermia Seed, Telomerase Complex
Biology from the bottom up: the cell, its skin, its chemistry and its protein factory. Everything alive is made of these.

$(thing)Contamination$(): Biology machines do not explode, they catch things. Each run handles the culture and costs 4% sterility; below half, a run may bring something in, and the machine stops until it is cleaned. A $(item)Sterile Pack$() (from the $(item)Autoclave$()) always cleans it. An $(item)Antibiotic$() is cheaper, but each dose on the same machine selects for what survives it, so the n-th works only one time in n.

$(thing)Living cultures$(): yeast, algae and cells are alive. Carried loose or dropped they die off (half in a few days of carrying); machines and chests keep them. A dead culture is no use to any recipe.

$(thing)Membranes$(): the $(item)Patch-Clamp Rig$() sets the ions on each side of a membrane; the voltage, Nernst's E = (RT/zF) ln(c_out/c_in), must land in the recipe's window. Lipid Bilayers sit at potassium's −90 mV, Ion Channel Membranes at sodium's +60, and a $(item)Living Cell$() ($(thing)Respiration$()) at a resting −70.

$(thing)Fermentation$(): the $(item)Fermenter$() grows yeast with air and ferments without it; too much sugar holds it back. Yeast makes Nutrient Broth cheaply, and rotten flesh rots to biogas (methane). $(thing)Photosynthesis$(): the $(item)Photobioreactor$() grows algae that make oxygen and a far cheaper Quantum Chlorophyll; too bright and they bleach.

$(thing)Transcription$() and $(thing)Translation$(): the $(item)Ribosome Assembler$() reads messages. Faster is sloppier, and a chain is right only if every codon is. Messenger RNA makes Engineered Enzymes cheaply, and with a Living Cell, a Synthetic Cell. $(thing)Protein Folding$(): the $(item)Folding Chamber$() holds a chain below its melting point until 95% of it folds.
Life too small to see: bacteria, the viruses that eat them, and the fungi that feel their way through the ground.

$(thing)Microbiology$(): the $(item)Fermenter$() grows $(item)Bacterial Cultures$() with air. $(thing)Biomineralisation$(): magnetotactic bacteria, kept short of air (1 to 10%), grow $(item)Magnetite$() from iron nuggets. $(thing)Probiotics$(): lactobacilli, with no air at all, make the $(item)Probiotic Seal$(), an upgrade that keeps a Biology console from ever being contaminated.

$(thing)Viruses$(): the $(item)Phage Lab$() sets how many phages each cell meets. The share hit is 1 − e^(−MOI), and each bursts after its latent period; too many phages burst the cells from outside. $(thing)Lysogeny$(): phages that write themselves into a genome deliver genes, a cheap Recombinant DNA.

$(thing)Mycology$(): the $(item)Mycelium Bed$() grows mould from old bread: growth peaks at its temperature and wants damp, but too wet and bacteria take the bed. Mould gives $(item)Antibiotics$(): cheap cleaning for a contaminated machine, but each dose on the same machine works less often. That is resistance, made by selection.
$(thing)Slime Moulds$(): $(item)Physarum$() links food sources with the shortest network it can, and makes Network Maps cheaply: Mathematics' graphs, alive.
The body is attacked all the time, and answers: first the same for every invader, then learned, and remembered. The Anomaly is an invader like any other, and now you can be ready for it.

$(thing)Infections$(): the creatures a failed machine releases now leave a lasting mark when they hit you. A $(thing)Destabilised Husk$() gives $(thing)Fracture$() (you slip a few blocks through space); a $(thing)Nanite Swarm$(), $(thing)Grey Goo$() (your food burns away); a $(thing)Paradox Echo$(), $(thing)Rewind$() (back where you stood ten seconds ago); a $(thing)Void Wraith$(), $(thing)Hollowing$() (six less health). They run their course.

$(thing)Innate$() and $(thing)Adaptive Immunity$(): the $(item)Antibody Bench$() grows a trace of an invader and measures the body's answer, a Hill curve in the dose, raised by the adjuvant. Too much of both and it resonates. It makes $(item)Antibodies$() and, from what each creature drops, an $(item)Anomaly Ward$().

$(thing)Immunisation$(): use a Ward on yourself and its infection cannot touch you for three in-game days. Renew it too soon (more than half its time left) and the imprint overloads: a Ward Overload. After $(thing)Immune Memory$() (you must have studied $(thing)Directed Evolution$()), a lasting Ward holds for good.

$(thing)Tolerance$(): the body must also know not to attack itself, and so must reality. The $(item)Law Wraiths$() that pour from a dimensional breach are reality's own antibodies, striking the breach and whoever stands by it. Study Tolerance and you are read as self: they leave you be.
Life at the scale of organs: how the body feeds itself, grows itself, and keeps time.

$(thing)Physiology$() and $(thing)Circulation$(): the $(item)Perfusion Rig$() pushes nutrient through vessels. The flow is Poiseuille's, the fourth power of the vessel's radius, so narrow vessels need far more pressure; too much and the vessel tears. It makes $(item)Perfused Tissue$() and a cheaper Stem Cell Culture.

$(thing)Stem Cells$() and $(thing)Regeneration$(): the $(item)Regeneration Tank$() sets up a morphogen gradient, c = c0.e^(-x/lambda), and cells read it to know where they are (the axolotl's trick). The gradient must still carry to the organ's far end. It grows $(item)Grown Organs$() (the fourth piece of the Tree of Life) and mends worn gear.

$(thing)Chronobiology$(): the $(item)Circadian Incubator$() keeps the world's day, and its cultures work hardest in their active hours. $(thing)Pharmacokinetics$(): the $(item)Dosing Pump$() meters a substance so its level stays between what works and what harms, C = (D/V).e^(-kt).
Life above the single creature: whole populations, their evolution, life built to a plan, and life built backwards. And the keystone that ties the branch together.

$(thing)Ecology$(): the $(item)Ecosphere$() holds a world in balance. Stock predator and prey near their Lotka-Volterra balance point and the cycle holds; stock too far off and it swings until one side crashes. It makes $(item)Stable Ecosystems$() and the $(item)Symbiont Lining$() (catalysts wear 40% slower).

$(thing)Population Genetics$(): the $(item)Selection Chamber$() breeds a trait in. A useful one fixes with chance (1 - e^(-2s)) / (1 - e^(-4Ns)): too weak and drift loses it, too strong and the culture dies. It feeds the Evolution Engine cheaply. $(thing)Gene Circuits$(): the $(item)Gene Circuit Loom$() wires genes into switches (bistable only when the cooperativity is over one) and makes the $(item)Living Catalyst$(), which heals its own wear while fed.

$(thing)Mirror Life$(): the $(item)Mirror Culture Vat$() grows cells built the wrong way round, on mirror food (natural food poisons them). Their $(item)Mirror Antibodies$() are the only answer to the Antiverse's Mirror Microbes.

$(thing)The Tree of Life$(): the five pieces of life, one from each phase, a $(item)Living Cell$(), a Pure Culture, a $(item)Grown Organ$(), an $(item)Antibody$() and a $(item)Stable Ecosystem$(), together make the $(item)Tree of Life$(): an endgame catalyst that never wears, the keystone of the branch.

Each chapter of the Anomaly storyline now has something to meet, not only to read. $(thing)Abnormality & Infection$(): the containment-failure creatures infect (Fracture, Grey Goo, Rewind, Hollowing). $(thing)Broken Symmetry$(): the Destabilised Husk's Fracture. $(thing)Molecules That Copy Themselves$() and $(thing)Self-Reference$(): the Nanite Swarm's Grey Goo. $(thing)Pathological Objects$(): the Paradox Echo's Rewind.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Tumour Nodule in Inner Space (Tumour); dropped by the Tumour Hydra.

$(thing)Oncogenesis$(): the Tumour of Inner Space, its oncogenic field, and the Tumour Hydra. $(thing)Evasion$(): Metastasis, which plain wards miss. $(thing)Clonal Evolution$(): resistance, as each antibiotic dose on a machine selects what survives it. $(thing)The Microenvironment$(): Inner Space's inflammation and its macrophages.

$(thing)Epidemics$(): infections pass between players. Each second an infected player passes theirs on, one time in fifty, to anyone within four blocks who is not warded: the SIR model played out, and a ward is herd immunity. $(thing)Where Anomaly Meets Normality$(): the Law Wraiths, reality's own antibodies (Tolerance makes them leave you be). $(thing)Symbiosis$(): the Probiotic Seal and the Symbiont Lining.
$(thing)Containment$() and $(thing)Targeted Therapy$(): the Containment Ward, and the CAR-T Cell Culture that seals the Tumour Hydra's stumps. $(thing)Resolution$(): the Resolution Engine, as before.

Late anomalies learn to hide, as tumours do: they shed the markers a ward is made against. The $(thing)Tumour Hydra$()'s bite carries $(thing)Metastasis$(): every ten seconds the growth spreads somewhere new (weakness, hunger or slowness), and no plain Anomaly Ward holds it.

The $(item)Clonal Selector$() matures antibodies as a germinal centre does. Each round of selection multiplies their binding by (1 + s), but culls the line: its diversity falls as 100.e^(-n.s/3), and below 10% it collapses to a single clone. Set the rounds and the stringency to bind tightly enough while keeping enough variety.

$(item)Matured Antibodies$() make the $(item)Metastasis Ward$() (three days, as the others) and, after Immune Memory, the lasting one. They also make the other four lasting wards far more cheaply than before.

Pleroma is everything at once, and that includes every fluid of every mod installed. First, every mod's fluids are distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$() into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$(): one fluid that stands for all of them.

Each distillation takes up to twelve of one mod's fluids (16,000 mB of each) and gives 1,000 mB of Essence. A mod with more fluids is distilled in parts, and the parts (4,000 mB of each) into the whole Essence. JEI lists every mod's distillations; new mods' fluids join in by themselves. Only fluids that fit in a bucket count, and a server can leave fluids or mods out (essenceBlacklist).

Then the Essences go on, in the same Distillery, into $(fluid)Anima Mundi$(), the soul of the world: water, lava, Basaltic Magma and Deep Brine (16,000 mB of each) and 4,000 mB of every mod's whole Essence, twelve at a time, in parts if there are more. Anima Mundi is one of the five fluids of Pleroma. Essences live in tanks and pipes only: a containment cell cannot remember whose Essence it held.

Found hanging from the ice of Titan's hidden ocean, and growing longer by itself. The Chemical Reactor melts it to concentrated brine.
pages.title: Brinicle

pages.text: $(thing)Used in$(): Concentrated Brine.

Sixty carbon atoms bonded into the shape of a football, twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons, with a hollow centre big enough to trap one more atom. It is round, slippery and perfectly symmetrical, and the hollow seems to be waiting for something.
pages.title: Buckyball Cage

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Heating graphene with blaze powder, I expected soot. Instead the sheets curled into closed spheres, and cooled in superfluid helium they stayed that way; the same cages Kroto and Smalley found in vaporised graphite.

pages.title: Carbon Nanotube Bundle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graphene curled on its own along the edges of an orbital lattice, so I gave it more lattice and an ionic liquid to roll in. The tubes came out closed and clean, and twisted into rope as they dried.

pages.title: Carborane Superacid

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Carborane acids are a million times stronger than sulfuric. Electrolysing an Electride Crystal with chiral crystal and ionic liquid, I made one strong enough to protonate anything.

A crystal that comes in only one hand. Like my left and right palms, its mirror image cannot be rotated to match it. Living things use left-handed amino acids and right-handed sugars, and nobody fully knows why. This one twists light passing through it, always the same way.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Mirror Microbe.
pages.title: Chiral Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Molecular orbitals let me predict which hand a molecule would take. Seeding an orbital lattice with amethyst and a quantum dot in supercritical solvent, I found the crystals all came out with the same handedness. I stopped calling it an accident after the tenth batch.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Muon-catalysed fusion was known in the 1950s; its problem is that muons are short-lived and get stuck. Using a noble gas clathrate to hold the fuel, quark-gluon plasma to make muons and a monopole to free them, I got the catalyst to work cycle after cycle.

Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
A melt spun onto a cold wheel: cooled fast enough, its atoms freeze in an order that never repeats.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.

Set the cooling rate (as a power of ten, K/s) and the alloy's aluminium fraction. Five-fold order forms only between 10² and 10⁴ K/s, near 63% aluminium; slower, an ordinary crystal grows.

Every machine has a $(thing)catalyst slot$(), the gold slot under its progress arrow. It holds one catalyst at a time, and is filled by hand (shift-click puts a catalyst there first); pipes and ME networks do not reach it.$(br2)A catalyst that wears or decays only works from the catalyst slot, so it is always the one there that wears. A catalyst that never wears still works from an input slot too, as it always did.
When the catalyst in the slot wears out, it moves to the output slots (where pipes and the ME network can take it away to be restored), and the slot is free for the next one.

Chemistry grew into fourteen branches in 1.2. These are the ones built so far, and their machines; each has its own entries in this chapter.$(li)$(thing)Kinetics & Equilibrium$(): $(item)Haber-Bosch Reactor$(), $(item)Ostwald Converter$(), $(item)Contact Process Tower$(), $(item)Air Separation Unit$()$(li)$(thing)Acids, Bases & Solutions$(): $(item)Titration Bench$(), $(item)Buffer Tank$(), $(item)Brine Evaporator$(), $(item)Reverse Osmosis Cell$()$(li)$(thing)Thermochemistry$(): $(item)Bomb Calorimeter$(), $(item)Heat-Pack Reactor$()

$(li)$(thing)Electrochemistry, extended$(): $(item)Fuel Cell$(), $(item)Electroplating Bath$()$(li)$(thing)Analytical Chemistry and the nebula gases$(): $(item)Chromatography Column$(), $(item)Mass Spectrometer$(), $(item)Cloud Siphon$()$(li)$(thing)Catalysis & Surfaces$(): $(item)Catalyst Formulator$()$(li)$(thing)Organic Synthesis & Polymers, and Frameworks & Porous Materials$(): $(item)Cracking Tower$(), $(item)Polymeriser$(), $(item)Synthesis Bench$(), $(item)Framework Assembler$(), $(item)Quasicrystal Furnace$()

$(li)$(thing)Inorganic & Coordination Chemistry, Spectroscopy, Materials & Solid-State$(): $(item)Coordination Reactor$(), $(item)Chelation Column$(), $(item)Infrared Spectrometer$(), $(item)NMR Spectrometer$(), $(item)Phase Diagram Kiln$(), $(item)Doping Furnace$(), $(item)Sintering Press$()$(li)$(thing)Titan, Saturn's largest moon$(): $(item)Lake Pump$()$(li)$(thing)Titan's creatures, its ruins, and Photochemistry$(): $(item)Photochemical Reactor$()$(li)$(thing)The last of the branch, and the Alkahest$(): $(item)Asymmetric Reactor$(), $(item)Oscillator Vessel$(), $(item)Alkahest Still$()

The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() has an $(thing)Operation$() console now, like the big physics machines. Set two things: the $(thing)heater temperature$() and the $(thing)residence time$(); how long each batch is held.$(br2)A reaction goes at the rate constant k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) (Arrhenius): hotter is faster, and the higher its activation energy Eₐ, the more heat it needs.

A batch held for τ reaches the conversion X = 1 − e^(−kτ). Each recipe needs its own conversion (the recipe page shows it); until the readout reaches it the reactor waits, $(thing)Out of Window$().$(br2)A shorter residence time runs more batches (60 s is the normal pace, down to a quarter of it), so heat it up, then shorten τ until X just reaches the target.

Two limits: the vessel is rated to 850 K, and a recipe with a $(thing)catalyst$() has the catalyst's sintering temperature (700 K). A catalyst lowers Eₐ, the same reaction runs at a much lower temperature, but run it above 700 K and it wears ten times as fast.

Technetium-99m loses half of itself every six hours, on the scaled clock, every 15 seconds. Carried loose, or dropped on the ground, a vial is spent within a minute.$(br2)Anywhere it is stored it waits instead: in a machine, an ME network, a chest or a $(item)Chronostatic Vault$().

To move it around, carry it in a $(item)Lead Pig$(): right-click the pig with vials on the cursor to put them in (up to 64), and right-click it with an empty hand to take them out. Vials put in at different times share one age, the average of theirs.

Nothing a machine holds on to lasts for ever. A $(thing)catalyst$() speeds a reaction and is not used up by it, but its pores clog and its surface is poisoned, a little each time. Lenses scratch, magnets lose their field, crystals crack and chips burn out.$(br2)Each time one of these serves as a recipe's catalyst it uses a run of its life: ten runs when the machine is pushed past a $(thing)wear$() limit of its physics. Its tooltip and the bar under it show what is left.

$(li)Living Catalyst: 128 runs, but each run that feeds it sugar or broth heals one$(li)Zeolite Catalyst, Platinum-Rhodium Gauze, Nickel Catalyst: 256 runs, then restored in the $(item)Regeneration Kiln$()$(li)Muonic Catalyst: 150 runs, then used up$(li)Photonic Lens, Cosmic String Lens, Tesseract Lens, Dark Matter Lens, Moissanite Lens, Einstein Ring Lens, Schmidt Corrector Plate, Echelle Grating, Apochromatic Objective: 256 runs, then restored in the $(item)Optical Workshop$()$(li)Neodymium Magnet, Ferrite Magnet, Samarium-Cobalt Magnet: 256 runs, then restored in the $(item)Magnetizer$()$(li)Perfect Crystal Interferometer: 512 runs, then restored in the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$()$(li)Iron Catalyst, Vanadium Bed: 512 runs, then restored in the $(item)Regeneration Kiln$()$(li)Quantum Random Number Chip, Boundary CFT Chip, Quantum Processor: 1024 runs, then used up

A worn-out catalyst comes out of the machine marked $(thing)worn$(), and no longer works until restored. Chips cannot be mended.$(br2)Mathematical, abstract and endgame catalysts never wear: a proof does not get tired.

Radioactive sources $(thing)decay$(): their activity halves with each half-life of their isotope, on the same clock as the Decay Chamber, wherever they are, in a chest, a machine or an ME network (all but Technetium-99m: see Carrying Technetium-99m). Below a sixteenth of its first activity a source is $(thing)spent$() and no longer works. It also gives off less radiation as it goes.$(br2)A $(item)Chronostatic Vault$() holds time still: a source kept in it stops decaying, and goes on where it left off when taken out.

Burn sulfur (or gunpowder) in oxygen for $(fluid)Sulfur Dioxide$(). Over vanadium, 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃; exothermic again, so the equilibrium falls back as it heats, but the $(item)Vanadium Bed$() only lights off near 670 K.

The $(item)Contact Process Tower$() cools the gas between its three beds. Set the bed temperature and the oxygen excess; a pass must convert 95%. The sulfur trioxide is absorbed into $(fluid)Sulfuric Acid$(). Above 873 K the bed sinters. Iron ore carries a little vanadium: eight raw iron make a bed.

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives out heat, and turns four volumes of gas into two. So $(thing)ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS$() climbs as it gets hotter and the equilibrium constant $(thing)K = e^(−ΔG°/RT)$() falls: cold and pressed makes the most ammonia. But the iron catalyst is sluggish when cold.

The $(item)Haber-Bosch Reactor$() sets the bed temperature, the pressure and the H₂ : N₂ ratio. A pass needs 15% ammonia; how much comes out follows the yield times the rate. The classic answer is about 720 K and 200 atm, 3 : 1. Above 823 K the $(item)Iron Catalyst$() sinters and wears ten times as fast; the vessel is rated to 300 atm.

A reaction goes at the rate constant $(thing)k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$() (Arrhenius): ten degrees warmer and many go twice as fast. The Chemical Reactor's console runs on it.$(br2)The feeds for heavy chemistry: the $(item)Air Separation Unit$() boils liquid air apart into $(fluid)Nitrogen$() and $(fluid)Oxygen$(); coal and steam in the Chemical Reactor give $(fluid)Hydrogen$() (C + H₂O → CO + H₂), as does water in the Electrolytic Cell.

Every one of these is shared with the pack's other mods: a recipe that asks for the mod's Hydrogen takes Mekanism's or NuclearCraft's as readily (anything in the c:hydrogen tag), and the same for nitrogen, oxygen, ammonia, the acids and sulfur dioxide.

On white-hot platinum, ammonia burns to nitric oxide: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. Too cool, or too long on the gauze, and it burns to plain nitrogen instead. The $(item)Ostwald Converter$() sets the gauze temperature and the contact time: hot (about 1100-1200 K) and brief (a millisecond or two) for 90% selectivity. The nitric oxide is absorbed into $(fluid)Nitric Acid$().
The $(item)Platinum-Rhodium Gauze$() loses platinum above 1250 K. Iron meteorites carry the platinum metals: dissolve the iron away in sulfuric acid and they are left behind.

chemistry/r60_acids.title: Acids, Bases and the Purity Tag

pages.text: An acid gives up a proton, a base takes one; $(thing)pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]$(). On the $(item)Titration Bench$() a standard runs into the sample until the indicator turns: at the endpoint the pH jumps six units in a drop. Set the titrant so the pH sits between 4 and 10 and the reagent comes out $(thing)assayed$().

Assayed reagents carry the $(thing)purity tag$(). The chemical catalysts, Zeolite, Iron, Vanadium and the Platinum-Rhodium Gauze, are poisoned by impurities: each run on an acid, base or sulfur dioxide feed that has $(l)not$() been assayed costs them five runs of life. Pipes and ME networks keep the tag; a containment cell does not. An assayed fluid says so in its name ("Ammonia (Assayed)") and shows a bright hatched border round its icon, in a tank and in an ME terminal alike.

A weak acid and its salt hold a pH set by their ratio: $(thing)pH = pKa + log₁₀([A⁻]/[HA])$(). The $(item)Buffer Tank$() mixes them: $(fluid)Phosphate Buffer$() at the pH of blood, 7.4, from bone meal and sulfuric acid; $(fluid)Ammonia Buffer$() at 9. Too far from a ratio of 1 and there is nothing left to buffer with.

Water crosses a membrane toward the saltier side, pulled with the osmotic pressure $(thing)π = iMRT$(): about 30 bar for a brine. The $(item)Reverse Osmosis Cell$() pushes harder; water comes through fresh, and what stays behind is $(fluid)Concentrated Brine$(), which dries to halite sooner. The membrane is rated to 80 bar.

A salt dissolves until its ions' product reaches the $(thing)solubility product K_sp$(). Drive the water off a brine and its salts come out in order: in the $(item)Brine Evaporator$(), $(item)Gypsum$() at four times the strength, $(item)Halite$() at ten to twenty, and $(item)Lithium Carbonate$() from the bittern beyond thirty.
Set the pan temperature and the water driven off. Hotter is faster, but above about 335 K the crystals grow too fast and trap the other salts: the purity must stay above 80%.

In the $(item)Bomb Calorimeter$() a weighed sample burns in pure oxygen inside a steel bomb, under water. The heat q = m·ΔH_c warms the water by $(thing)ΔT = q/C$(). Size the sample so the rise is readable (1.5 to 3 K) and give it oxygen enough to burn it all: each burn writes a $(item)Thermochemical Data Card$() and gives Insight.

Heat is a state function, so the heat of any reaction can be added up from steps already measured (Hess). The $(item)Heat-Pack Reactor$() runs reactions for their heat: ammonia and nitric acid neutralise to $(item)Ammonium Nitrate$(), giving heat out; mixed too fast it runs away. Dissolving it again takes heat in: $(fluid)Cold Pack Solution$() at 268 K. Salt and ice make $(fluid)Eutectic Brine$() at 252 K.
Both cold packs are $(thing)coolants$(): pour them into a physics machine's coolant loop to hold it below room temperature; colder than water, though they carry less heat.

Split a reaction in two and make its electrons go round by a wire, and its free energy comes out as a voltage: $(thing)ΔG = −nFE$(). The Nernst equation says how the voltage moves with the reactants: $(thing)E = E° − (RT/nF)·ln Q$().

The $(item)Fuel Cell$() burns Hydrogen (or Ammonia) with Oxygen as a current. Drawing more current costs voltage, so the power, V·i, peaks part-way, near 1 A/cm². Too little current and it floods; too much and it starves.

The $(item)Vanadium Flow Battery$() stores 50 million FE in two tanks of vanadium electrolyte. Its voltage follows its charge, and right-clicking it reads both; it stops taking charge at 95%. Salt water through the Electrolytic Cell gives $(fluid)Chlorine$() and $(item)Caustic Soda$(); lithium carbonate gives back lithium.

A current through a metal salt lays the metal down on the cathode: $(thing)m = MIt/(nF)$() (Faraday). Nitric acid takes the nickel out of meteoric iron as $(fluid)Nickel Sulfate Solution$(); the $(item)Electroplating Bath$() puts it back on iron. Set the current and time for a coat 20 to 50 µm thick; above 8 A/dm² it burns. $(item)Nickel-Plated Iron$() makes $(item)Corrosion-Proof Casings$().

A mixture carried down a packed column comes apart: each part sticks to the packing for its own time. The bands spread as they go, the $(thing)plate height H = A + B/u + C·u$() (van Deemter) is smallest at a middling flow, and two parts come out clean when the resolution $(thing)Rs$() reaches 1.5.

The $(item)Chromatography Column$() is a tower: every storey adds a metre of column and more plates, for harder splits. Set the carrier flow and the oven temperature. It splits $(fluid)Molecular Cloud$() gas into water and ammonia, methane and hydrogen cyanide, and the dust clouds' medium into $(item)PAH Soot$().

Gases that come off it pure are $(thing)assayed$(): Hydrogen, Nitrogen, Oxygen, Methane and Carbon Monoxide. From now on these, like the acids, poison a chemical catalyst when fed in unassayed (five runs each).

An ion accelerated through V and bent by a field B moves on $(thing)r = √(2mV/q)/B$(). The $(item)Mass Spectrometer$()'s detector sits at 0.5 m: set the field for the mass you want. Cold clouds concentrate deuterium in their molecules thousands of times; a cheaper deuterium than heavy water. Lithium-6 can be picked out of lithium the same way.

The Frontier's clouds are a gas field Earth's air cannot match. A $(item)Cloud Siphon$() touching a Hydrogen, Oxygen or Dust Cloud draws its gas for ever; the cloud is not used up. The Fractionation Spire, run cold, parts out $(fluid)Hydrogen$() and $(fluid)Carbon Monoxide$().

Carbon monoxide and hydrogen make $(fluid)Methanol$(); methane runs the Fuel Cell; hydrogen cyanide and ammonia with a little sugar make an $(item)Amino Acid Mixture$() (the Strecker route); PAH soot makes graphene more cheaply than coal.

A catalyst holds a molecule on its surface just long enough to change it. Too weakly and nothing sticks, too tightly and nothing leaves: plotted against the binding energy, the activity is a $(thing)volcano$() (Sabatier). The coverage of a surface follows $(thing)θ = KP/(1 + KP)$() (Langmuir).

The $(item)Catalyst Formulator$() makes the catalysts more cheaply than the Chemical Reactor: set the metal loading and the calcination temperature so the binding sits at the volcano's peak, but calcine too hot and the metal sinters. It also makes the $(item)Nickel Catalyst$(), for hydrogenation.
The $(item)Regeneration Kiln$() now has a console too: burn the coke off hot enough and with air enough, but below about 900 K, where the metal starts to sinter. 90% must come back.

A framework is a crystal of nodes and struts, mostly empty. On the $(item)Framework Assembler$() the linker sets the pore: it must fit the target molecule, and the solvent must be dried out slowly or the pores collapse. $(item)MOF Gas Sorbent$() fills a $(item)MOF Gas Storage Cell$(), which holds 256,000 mB of one gas; sixteen tanks' worth, because the framework holds gas on its inner surface (Langmuir). $(item)Silica Aerogel$() is ninety-nine parts air.

Clay digested in caustic soda gives $(item)Alumina$() (Bayer); electrolysed, $(item)Aluminium$() (Hall-Héroult). In the $(item)Quasicrystal Furnace$() an aluminium-copper-iron melt quenched at 10² to 10⁴ K/s, near 63% aluminium, freezes into a $(item)Quasicrystal Plate$(): order without repetition.

Coal and hydrogen under pressure make $(fluid)Synthetic Crude$() (Bergius); the pack's crude oil will do as well. In the $(item)Cracking Tower$() its long chains break into short ones: hotter gives more $(fluid)Ethylene$() (about 1100 K), cooler more $(fluid)Propylene$() (1000 K). Each needs a 60% share. Above 1150 K coke fouls the Zeolite Catalyst; steam keeps it down.

When a fraction p of the ends have reacted, chains average $(thing)1/(1 − p)$() units (Carothers): a thousand-unit polyethylene needs p = 0.999. The $(item)Polymeriser$() makes $(item)Polymer Sheet$() from ethylene, $(item)Nylon Fibre$() from propylene, ammonia and nitric acid, and $(item)Aramid Fibre$() from PAH soot spun out of sulfuric acid. Above 420 K it runs away.

A route of n steps keeps $(thing)yⁿ$() of its material: every step costs. On the $(item)Synthesis Bench$(), choose the shortest route the target allows; it has a least number of steps, and no route is shorter. $(item)Fine Reagents$() are what later recipes ask for by name.

Ligands split a metal's d orbitals by $(thing)Δ$(); against the pairing energy $(thing)P$(), that decides high spin or low. The $(item)Coordination Reactor$() sets the ligand field: $(item)Prussian Blue$() and the $(item)Porphyrin Oxygen Carrier$() are low spin, the $(item)Copper Ammine Complex$() high. The porphyrin is haem: it holds oxygen and lets it go.
$(item)EDTA$() grips a metal with six bonds. In the $(item)Chelation Column$() it pulls rare earths out of brine, and cleans spent fuel salt back into fuel, so long as the flow does not saturate it.

At its $(thing)eutectic$() an alloy melts all at once: the $(item)Phase Diagram Kiln$() makes Superconducting Solder from lead and copper more cheaply. The $(item)Doping Furnace$() diffuses a dopant into a wafer for a working junction (10¹⁶ to 10¹⁸ carriers); a $(item)Doped Wafer$() goes through the Lithographer at twice the yield.
The $(item)Sintering Press$() fires alumina dense without growing its grains: $(item)Alumina Ceramic Plates$(), and with aramid behind them, $(item)Ceramic Armour Plates$().

Each bond absorbs infrared at its own vibration, $(thing)ν = √(k/μ)/2π$(). The $(item)Infrared Spectrometer$() must scan across the band, narrowly enough to resolve it: a $(item)Structure Card$(). With one in its catalyst slot, the Synthesis Bench knows its target and takes a shorter route.

The $(item)NMR Spectrometer$() listens to nuclei in a superconducting magnet: they resonate at $(thing)f = γB/2π$(). Keep it below 10 K (superfluid helium in its coolant loop) and the field under 22 T, or it quenches. Its readings are worth Insight.

On Titan, methane does what water does on Earth: it rains, runs in rivers, pools in seas and evaporates again. At 94 K its vapour pressure is about a sixth of an atmosphere (Clausius-Clapeyron); enough to make clouds and rain.

The $(item)Lake Pump$() draws from a lake it touches on Titan: $(fluid)Liquid Methane$() from the seas and lakes, $(fluid)Cryolava$() from the cryovolcanoes' lakes. The Fractionation Spire boils liquid methane off into $(fluid)Methane$() gas, with the $(fluid)Nitrogen$() dissolved in it, and splits cryolava into $(fluid)Ammonia$() and water.

Where a lake dries, what it had dissolved is left as a crust. $(item)Organic Evaporite$(), co-crystals of benzene and ethane, acetylene and butane, hydrogenated over a Nickel Catalyst gives $(fluid)Ethylene$(). It can be made again, as Titan makes it: liquid methane boiled down in the Brine Evaporator leaves its evaporites (20 to 50 times concentrated). Evaporite Crust dissolved in methanol gives them up too, and Cryolava Rock remelts into cryolava in the Chemical Reactor. Two Packed Ice, chilled hard, make Water-Ice Bedrock.

A photon absorbed breaks one bond; what follows can make several molecules of product; the quantum yield Φ. How much of the light is absorbed is the $(thing)Beer-Lambert law$(): the absorbance is A = εcl, and the cell takes a fraction 1 − 10^(−A).

The $(item)Photochemical Reactor$() (a console) makes Titan's own haze chemistry: $(item)Tholin$() and $(fluid)Hydrogen Cyanide$() from methane and nitrogen, and $(fluid)Hydrogen$() from water. Set the path length so the mixture absorbs 90% to 99.9% of the light (A between 1 and 3): thinner and the light goes through, thicker and only a skin by the window reacts. Brighter is faster, up to 400 W/m².

The alchemists searched for the $(thing)alkahest$(), a universal solvent that would dissolve anything. It is distilled here from all of Chemistry at once, in the $(item)Alkahest Still$(), in four stages, each with its own boiling point. Purity must reach 95% (a reflux ratio of 5 or more); hotter is faster, but 150 K over the boiling point boils over.

$(fluid)Tincture of Balance$(): ammonium nitrate, nickel-plated iron, sulfuric acid and ammonia; kinetics, equilibrium, acids, heat and current. $(fluid)Tincture of Form$(): a Structure Card, Fine Reagents, a quasicrystal and ethylene; spectra, synthesis, frameworks and chains.

$(fluid)Tincture of Chirality$(): Enantiopure Reagents, a Chemical Clock, tholin and Ammonia Buffer; handedness, time, and Titan. $(fluid)Alkahest$(): a Porphyrin Oxygen Carrier, a Copper Ammine Complex and a Doped Wafer, with the Kekule Ring in the catalyst slot.
Alkahest dissolves any ore: four raw iron, gold or copper and a little Alkahest give twelve ingots. It is $(thing)Chemistry's unifying fluid$(), and one of the five fluids Pleroma is distilled from.

Many molecules come in two mirror-image forms, like hands. Living things use only one: the wrong hand of a drug can be useless, or a poison. A $(thing)chiral catalyst$() lowers the barrier to one hand by ΔΔG‡ more than to the other, so that one forms $(thing)s = e^(ΔΔG‡/RT)$() times faster; the enantiomeric excess is ee = (s − 1)/(s + 1).

The $(item)Chiral Ligand$() is made at the Synthesis Bench with the Ouroboros's $(item)Kekule Ring$() in its catalyst slot (the ring never wears). In the $(item)Asymmetric Reactor$()'s catalyst slot it makes $(item)Enantiopure Reagent$() from Fine Reagent and hydrogen. Run it cold enough for ee ≥ 0.9: colder is purer, and slower.

Two routes, by choice: the reactor is $(thing)fast but random$() (60% of runs give the reagent); the Chromatography Column $(thing)resolves$() two Fine Reagents into one, slowly, every time; it separates the two hands and throws one away.

In 1951 Boris Belousov found a mixture that turned from yellow to clear and back, again and again. Nobody believed him. The $(thing)Brusselator$() shows how: one species makes more of itself from another and is used up again, and past a threshold $(thing)B > 1 + A²$() the steady mixture can no longer stay still.

The $(item)Oscillator Vessel$() makes $(item)Chemical Clocks$() from redstone and sulfuric acid. Set the feeds so that B is at least 0.2 past the threshold and the beat (about 2π/A seconds) falls between 3 and 8 seconds.
A furnace that burns the coke and poisons out of a worn catalyst's pores, and gives it back like new.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 1$() machine.

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry, and JEI, show the pattern.

When a particle meets its antiparticle, both vanish and all of their rest mass becomes energy, mostly gamma rays, via E = mc^2. Fission releases under 0.1% of the mass; annihilation releases 100%. One gram of antimatter matches dozens of kilotons of TNT.

Fuel log: it burns $(item)Antimatter Pellets$() (with a $(item)Dilithium Crystal$() as regulator) at 131,072 FE/t, or a full $(item)Annihilation Core$() at 524,288 FE/t.$(br2)It needs superfluid helium cooling. Do not skip this.

pages.text: Neutrinos are near-massless leptons that feel only the weak force (and gravity). A light-year of lead would stop only about half of them. Real detectors use kilotons of water or ice and catch a handful a day. The $(item)Neutrino Condenser$() is, frankly, cheating.

Why it matters: a neutron star packs more than a Sun's mass into a city-sized sphere. Gravity crushes electrons into protons, leaving neutrons held up only by degeneracy pressure. Deeper in, neutrons may dissolve into free quarks. A teaspoon would weigh about a billion tonnes.

A controlled matter-antimatter reaction inside a box. Matter and antimatter meet and convert entirely into energy, the most efficient fuel possible. Dilithium slows the reaction so it releases steadily rather than all at once. It glows white-hot, but the box stays cool.
pages.title: Annihilation Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Antimatter Penning Trap I let antimatter seep through Dilithium Crystal into a superfluid helium bath. Instead of a crater, it gave me a steady glow I could tap for power.
Made in $(item)Antimatter Penning Trap$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Annihilation Power.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Neutrino Flux.
One extra quark in every billion pairs. Everything that was not annihilated grew out of that one part in a billion.
pages.title: Baryon Asymmetry Crystal

pages.title: Bounce Core

A slab of neutronium that should, by rights, explode back into a cloud of free neutrons the moment it leaves a star. The spacetime-alloy frame keeps the pressure on, so the plate stays degenerate: neutrons packed shoulder to shoulder, refusing by the Pauli principle to be squeezed any further.
pages.title: Degenerate Armour Plate

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Neutronium decompresses violently outside a star, so I tried caging a block in spacetime alloy and letting the Casimir Vacuum Press hold the vacuum around it. The neutrons stayed locked. Anything that can survive a compact star's interior can survive me.
Made in $(item)Casimir Vacuum Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stellar Containment Plate, Theoretical Notes II.
Walls built to hold a region where escape velocity reaches light speed. Nothing leaves through a horizon; the walls are for what has not fallen in yet.
pages.title: Horizon Containment

pages.title: Kilonova Ash

pages.text: Made in $(item)Reflecting Telescope$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Kilonovae.

A fragment of a magnetar, a neutron star with a magnetic field a thousand trillion times stronger than Earth's. Near it, atoms are stretched into needles and empty space becomes birefringent. It would wipe a credit card from the Moon, and it pulls iron from across the room.
pages.title: Magnetar Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Through the Einstein-Rosen Bridge Projector I reached toward a magnetar and caught a shard. Dilithium Crystal and Sterile Neutrino kept the field from tearing it apart on the way back.

Hydrogen compressed until it becomes a metal. At pressures found in the cores of gas giants, the electrons break free and conduct like copper. It flows silvery and heavy, and may be a room-temperature superconductor.
pages.title: Liquid Metallic Hydrogen

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wigner and Huntington predicted metallic hydrogen in 1935. Crushing degenerate matter with superfluid helium in the Neutron Star Forge, I found hydrogen that conducted like a metal.
Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Metallic Hydrogen Ingot.

Hydrogen compressed until its electrons are shared freely, like a metal. In the cores of Jupiter and Saturn it is the dominant form. It is probably metastable at ordinary pressure, and conducts electricity and heat beautifully. The ingot is mirror-bright and surprisingly light.
pages.title: Metallic Hydrogen Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Bose-Einstein Condenser, I pressed Liquid Metallic Hydrogen between Casimir Plates and cooled it. When the pressure was released, it held its metallic state. Probably. I have kept an eye on it.
Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compact Stars.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Room-Temperature Superconductor, Theoretical Notes III.

A stream of ghost particles, trillions of which pass through me every second. They barely interact with anything, so the flux is invisible, weightless and almost impossible to stop. Only rarely does one leave a blue flash.
pages.title: Neutrino Flux

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pauli predicted the neutrino to save energy conservation. The Neutrino Condenser caught the rare few that interacted with its Cherenkov quartz, and slowly accumulated them into a flux.

Made in $(item)Matter-Antimatter Annihilation Reactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Gold Ingot, Lepton Triplet, Magnetar Shard, Pulsar Timing Crystal, R-Process Cluster, Standard Model Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

A cube of compacted neutronium, matter in which electrons and protons have been crushed together into neutrons. It is almost impossibly dense for its size, and dropping it on a floor would be a mistake. The surface is a smooth, dull grey.
pages.title: Block of Neutronium

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Storing loose neutronium ingots wasted space, so I pressed nine together. The block holds its shape with nothing but the strong force, and it makes a convenient compact supply.

A crystal that ticks with the precision of a millisecond pulsar, the most regular natural clocks known. Its pulses are so stable that any drift reveals a passing gravitational wave. It flashes a faint blue on every beat, and I set my watches by it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Pulsar Timing Ore in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field); dropped by the Pulsar Wisp (the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field)).
pages.title: Pulsar Timing Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge I spun a Magnetar Shard up inside quartz, with a Chronon Capacitor to stabilise the rhythm. Neutrino Flux synchronised it with the stars, and the beat matched to the nanosecond.

The heart of a star too dense even for neutrons, where the neutrons have dissolved into free quarks. Strange matter may be stable here. It is the densest thing short of a singularity, and holding it makes my wrist ache even through the containment.
pages.title: Quark Star Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge, I compressed a Block of Neutronium with strange matter and supernova remnants, until the neutrons broke apart into quarks. Quark-Gluon Plasma bonded the result together.

$(thing)Kilonovae$()$(br2)When two neutron stars merge, a few hundredths of a solar mass of neutron-rich matter is flung out, and in a second it captures neutrons up to gold and platinum. Its radioactive glow fades over days.
