pages.title: Holographic Encoder

pages.text: The holographic principle: the most information a region can hold grows with its surface area, not its volume; a black hole's entropy is a quarter of its horizon area in Planck units. So a volume can, in principle, be written onto its own boundary. This machine does exactly that.
$(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry, and JEI, show the pattern.

pages.title: Maxwell's Demon Sorter

pages.text: By the books it should not work: sorting particles lowers entropy, and someone always pays. See my notes on Maxwell's Demon. For now I just watch it sort.

A crystal containing the maximum information a region of space can hold, the Bekenstein bound: proportional to the area of its surface, not its volume. Add one more bit and it would become a black hole. It is warm, glassy and dense with stored meaning.
pages.title: Bekenstein Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wrote a Holographic Matrix's information onto Hawking radiation in the Holographic Encoder, pushing it until the crystal reached its limit. Any further and it would have collapsed into a black hole.

A mixer that visits every state there is, given time, so its average over time is its average over all of them.
pages.title: Ergodic Mixer Core

A three-dimensional object stored entirely on its two-dimensional boundary, just as the holographic principle says all the information in a volume is encoded on its surface. The matrix is a cube whose faces hold everything inside it. Looking through it, the interior shifts when I tilt the surface.
pages.title: Holographic Matrix

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Holographic Encoder, I recorded the interior of a Metamaterial Sheet onto its surface using a Quantum Processor and a condensate. Then I deleted the interior. Nothing changed. The surface held everything.

A container of order. Inside, entropy flows backwards: heat moves from cold to hot and mixed gases unmix themselves. A Maxwell's demon chip does the sorting and pays for it by erasing its memory elsewhere, as Landauer said it must. The cell is cold and very quiet.
pages.title: Negentropy Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I set a Maxwell's Demon Chip inside a neutronium shell with a Bose-Einstein Condensate in the Maxwell's Demon Sorter. The demon sorted the condensate atoms by speed, and order accumulated inside.

Armour for working at the smallest length that means anything. Neutronium plate gives it unyielding density, Planck shards set its grain to the scale of quantum gravity, and a spacetime casing core keeps the inside from bubbling away into foam.
pages.title: Planck Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My first harvester rig dissolved into fizz at the Planck scale. Bonding Planck shards onto neutronium over a spacetime casing produced walls fine-grained enough that the foam could not slip between them.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Thermodynamics of Information.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester.

A fragment one Planck length across, about 1.6 times ten to the minus thirty-five metres, the scale at which the concept of length stops meaning anything. It cannot be cut smaller because there is no smaller. It looks like a point of light that is somehow also a solid edge.
pages.title: Planck Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Sorting through Spacetime Slag in the Maxwell's Demon Sorter, I asked the demon to pick out the smallest pieces. It returned these, and could go no further: the demon itself admitted there was nothing smaller to sort.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Thermodynamics of Information.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Planck Area Tile, Planck Casing, Planck Diver, Resonance Probe, Vacuum Fluctuation Harvester.

$(thing)AdS/CFT Correspondence$()$(br2)A theory of gravity in a curved space and a quantum field theory on its boundary, without gravity, are the same theory in two languages. The universe as a hologram, made exact.
pages.title: AdS/CFT Correspondence

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 400$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): The Holographic Principle, Page Curve and Islands.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Page Curve Record, 1 Island Fragment, 1 Holographic Matrix.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Gravity in a three-dimensional anti-de Sitter space of radius L, with gravity's constant G, is the same as a two-dimensional conformal field theory whose central charge C counts its degrees of freedom. Write C.

A handheld instrument that reads the four virtual-particle resonances of the Quantum Foam where you stand. It hums at different pitches depending on what the vacuum is doing, and its needle never settles.
pages.title: Resonance Probe

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Foam I needed to know which virtual particles were bubbling up where. A spectral analyzer tuned by a qubit and a Planck shard gave me a probe that could read the foam's resonances.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Thermodynamics of Information.

Quark matter made of up, down and strange quarks in roughly equal numbers. Some physicists suspect it is more stable than ordinary nuclei, which would make it contagious: ordinary matter that touches it may convert. The pellet is heavy, faintly warm and sits in a container I never open twice.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Destabilised Husk.
pages.title: Strange Matter Pellet

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Fractured Essence from a Destabilised Husk keeps some strange quarks in its splinters. A Maxwell's Demon Sorter, cooled by superfluid helium, sorted those quarks from the rest one at a time until a pellet of pure strange matter remained.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Destabilised Husk.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Thermodynamics of Information.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Matter Singularity, Glueball Core, Hyperon Crystal, Kugelblitz Seed, Magnetar Shard, Magnetic Monopole, Pentaquark Shard, Quark Star Core and more.

Void lattice shards compacted into a block; a crystal of empty sites that is rigid even though there is nothing in it. Looking at it feels like looking at a hole in the world with very clean edges. It weighs almost nothing.
pages.title: Void Lattice Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pressing void lattice shards together made a block that still had nothing in it but held its shape anyway. It is the strangest building material I have, and it stacks neatly.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Thermodynamics of Information.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Void Lattice Shard.

A splinter of the scaffolding that sits between branes, the structure the Bulk uses to keep separate universes apart. It has edges but no obvious inside, and light that enters it takes a long time to come back out. Held close to the ear it hums at a pitch just below hearing.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Void Lattice Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef); dropped by the Void Wraith; dropped by the Moduli Crawler (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes)); dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)); and elsewhere.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The first shards fell from a Void Wraith I fought near a bulk monolith, still crackling. Later I found them in derelict station lockers and learned to break them out of Void Lattice Blocks directly, which is quieter than fighting for them.

Calculus is the art of the infinitely small. $(item)Infinitesimals$() come from the reals. With a $(item)Function Graph$() they become $(item)Derivative$() and $(item)Integral Operators$(); rates of change and sums of slices.
Together those make $(item)Differential Manifolds$(); curved spaces smooth enough to do calculus on. They are the stage relativity is written on.

Complex analysis gives $(item)Fractal Sets$(); its own study, Fourier Series, gives $(item)Fourier Series$() (any wave as a sum of pure tones).$(br2)Number theory needs $(item)Prime Shards$(), mined in the Platonic Realm, or sieved slowly from naturals, for $(item)Modular Forms$() and the $(item)Riemann Zeta Crystal$(). Riemann's zeros still guard the primes.

Set the block length n and the parity bits r. A Hamming code with r parity bits covers blocks of up to 2^r − 1 bits and corrects one flipped bit in each; a block fails if two flip, about (nε)²/2 of the time, which must be under the tolerance. Longer blocks carry more data per bit.

The Platonic Realm is self-similar: big islands low down, smaller ones above them, smaller still at the top. Its landmarks are mathematical objects built exactly to their definitions.

Landmarks I have charted:$(li)$(thing)Menger sponges$() with Euclid's Vault at their heart$(li)$(thing)Sierpinski tetrahedra$()$(li)$(thing)Mandelbulbs$()$(li)$(thing)Cantor dust$()$(li)$(thing)recursive trees$()$(li)the $(thing)Hilbert Archive$(), a corridor that walks a Hilbert curve to its treasure.

Two natives guard it. The $(thing)Fractal Wyrm$(), a serpent made of smaller copies of itself. And the $(thing)Axiom Sentinel$(), an icosahedron that spends two seconds proving you wrong; break its line of sight. I learned that the hard way.

Set the junctions V and the links L. A network needs at least V − 1 links to join them all; each one more is a spare route. Start from nothing, literally. Start from $(item)Axiom Schemas$() and the $(item)Empty Set$() (Void Essence, or plenty of Void Lattice). Von Neumann built every number out of empty sets nested inside each other; I am doing the same.
Proofs, $(item)Power Sets$(), $(item)Aleph-Null$(), the $(item)Continuum$() and the $(item)Axiom of Choice$() follow. Choice is what Banach and Tarski needed to double a sphere.

Category theory sits on top: $(item)Category Lattices$(), $(item)Functor Bridges$() and finally the $(item)Topos$(); a universe of mathematics with its own logic. Category theory studies not things, but the arrows between them.
The rules you agree to before you prove anything.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Axiom Sentinel (the Platonic Realm).

The set of all subsets. Always strictly bigger than what you started with.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
From every set of sets you may pick one of each. Accept it and spheres can be doubled.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
Objects and arrows, and nothing else. All of mathematics fits inside.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
A map between categories that keeps every arrow pointing the right way.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().

Absolute Infinity is no longer a shortcut. To build it I have to build mathematics itself, one branch at a time.

The branches: $(thing)numbers$(), $(thing)analysis$(), $(thing)number theory$(), $(thing)topology$(), $(thing)logic$(), $(thing)sets$() and $(thing)categories$(), each with its own machine and its own symbols.

The $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$() builds number systems, the $(item)Analytic Continuator$() does calculus and analysis, the $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() does logic, set theory and category theory, and the $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$() takes it all to infinity.
Finally, whole stacks of every branch are compressed into a $(item)Mathematics Singularity$(), which, with Surreal Numbers, Toposes and Continuum Shards, becomes $(item)Absolute Infinity$().
One, two, three... Peano built all of arithmetic from zero and "the next one".$(br2)Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().

Glass whose clarity has a cardinality. It holds countably many points of light in a perfectly ordered grid, yet every sliver of it still contains as many points as the whole. Looking through it, scale stops meaning much.
pages.title: Aleph Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cantor showed some infinities are larger than others. In the ordinal lands I found panes of glass in which a small piece held just as many reflections as the whole. A one-to-one map onto itself.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Hopf Fibration, Ordinal Recursor, Power Set.

The next size of infinity after the countable one: the cardinality of omega-one. Whether it equals the size of the real line is independent of the standard axioms. The token is dense and unbearably large for something that fits in a hand.
pages.title: Aleph-One

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Measuring omega-one with cardinal shards in the Ordinal Recursor, I found the next infinity after the countable one. Synaptic fluid helped me hold the concept in mind long enough.
Made in $(item)Ordinal Recursor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Inaccessible Cardinal, Transcendent Cache.

An Engineered Enzyme with its Michaelis constant and top speed measured, so it is always fed exactly as much substrate as it can use. Made on the Enzyme Assay Bench; Bioculture wastes far less with it.

Given any collection of non-empty sets, you may choose one element from each, even when no rule tells you which. It seems harmless, yet it implies that a sphere can be cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two spheres. The token feels decisive.
pages.title: Axiom of Choice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to choose a point from each piece of the continuum and it could not without an extra axiom. I wrote one in and it immediately proved Banach-Tarski.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Set Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Banach-Tarski Sphere.

The starting assumptions of a system, written out as patterns that stand for infinitely many individual axioms. Change one and you change what can be proved. The slate is plain and heavy, and every line carved on it is accepted without proof.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Axiom Sentinel (the Platonic Realm).
pages.title: Axiom Schema

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found my first schemas in Euclid's vault and among the debris of Axiom Sentinels. Building my own meant encoding natural number rules into a qubit until the Formal Proof Assistant would accept them as given.

Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Axiom Sentinel.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Euclids Vault, Hilbert Archive, Liars Vault, Proof Stairs chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes III, Axiom of Choice, Category Lattice, Empty Set, Formal Proof Tree, Platonic Compass, Proof Certificate.
$(thing)Axiom Sentinel$(). Lives in: Platonic Realm.$(br)Drops: Proof Fragment, Axiom Schema, Prime Shard.
pages.title: Axiom Sentinel

pages.text: Pale, smooth stone that seems to be made of definitions. Each block holds its shape because it has been told to. It is cool and faintly humming, like a theorem being proved. Its surface is unmarked except for faint, regular lines, like ruled paper for a proof yet to be written.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.
pages.title: Axiom Stone

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the realm of axioms, everything rests on this stone. I mined a piece to see what it was and found it underlay both the natural numbers and the axiom schemas I had been studying.

Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Axiom Schema, Fractal Lattice Block, Koch Crystal, Natural Number Lattice, Prime Shard, Proof Fragment, Transcendent Stone, Transcendental Crystal.

A piece of how many there are, even when there are infinitely many. Cardinals measure the size of a set rather than its order. The shard is uniform and solid and feels like a count without a sequence.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Cardinal Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Ordinal Hound (the Platonic Realm).
pages.title: Cardinal Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ordinal Hounds dropped these, and I found more in Hilbert's Hotel and the Ordinal Spire. They measured how big a set was, regardless of how it was ordered.

Made in $(item)Ordinal Recursor$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Cardinal Ore$(), in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Ordinal Hound.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Hilbert Hotel, Ordinal Spire chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Aleph-One, Inaccessible Cardinal, Omega-One.

Objects connected by arrows, with the only rule being that arrows compose. Numbers, spaces, groups and programs all form categories, and theorems about one often transfer to the others. The lattice looks almost bare: dots and arrows, and nothing else.
pages.title: Category Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I noticed that function graphs, power sets and axiom schemas all had the same shape: things and maps between them. The Formal Proof Assistant abstracted that shape into a lattice of objects and arrows.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Category Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Conceptual Containment Casing, Functor Bridge, Theoretical Notes III.

The real line, with the imaginary unit laid at right angles across it, forming a flat sheet of numbers. On this plane every polynomial has all its roots, multiplication is rotation and scaling, and smooth functions become astonishingly rigid. It feels like a perfectly flat, perfectly thin pane of glass.
pages.title: Complex Plane

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)With i in hand, the obvious step was to cross it with the real continuum. The Analytic Continuator held the two at right angles in a condensate until they fused into one field of numbers, two dimensions wide.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Fourier Series, Fractal Set, Mathematics Singularity, Modular Form, Quaternion Crystal, Riemann Zeta Crystal, Turing Morphogen and more.

A machine's outputs, sampled so many times that their odds are known to the last digit, and the settings that favour the good ones. Fitted to a machine, every chance product comes out halfway closer to certain. One upgrade per machine. Made in the Statistics Engine.
pages.title: Confidence Seal

pages.text: Made in $(item)Statistics Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Statistics.

Between any two grains of it there is another: a stone with no gaps, and no smallest piece. Found in the Continuum (the Platonic Realm, Y 880 to 1040). The Analytic Continuator draws Transcendental Crystals out of it, and makes more from cobblestone and Epsilon Dust.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.
pages.title: Dense Stone

pages.text: Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Real Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transcendental Crystal.

Take a function, look at it on a smaller and smaller scale until it looks straight, and record the slope. That is the derivative, and this operator does it at every point at once. It feels like a lens: everything seen through it is reduced to how fast it is changing.
pages.title: Derivative Operator

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dividing a function graph's rise by its run over an infinitesimal step gave exactly the instantaneous slope I wanted. Newton and Leibniz argued over credit; the Analytic Continuator just does it.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Christoffel Symbol, Differential Manifold, Hamiltonian Operator, Metric Tensor, Optimised Pathway, Optimiser, Riemann Curvature Tensor.

A space that looks flat if you look closely enough, though it may curve in any way overall. Calculus works on each small flat patch, and the patches stitch together smoothly. Einstein wrote relativity on exactly this kind of stage. The object folds and flexes in the hand without ever creasing.
pages.title: Differential Manifold

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted calculus on a curved surface, so I glued derivative and integral operators onto a topological insulator patch by patch. The condensate smoothed the seams until no point could tell it was anywhere special.

Made in $(item)Topology Kiln$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Calabi-Yau Manifold, Dimensional Residue, Functor Bridge, Klein Bottle, Minkowski Lattice, Quantum Field Lattice, Tensor Calculus Engine.
Two hundred and forty roots, each touching the same number of neighbours, packed so tightly in eight dimensions that no sphere could be added anywhere. Viazovska proved it optimal in 2016.
pages.title: E8 Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Octonions and the Hopf fibration kept pointing at the same structure, so I fed both into the Tesseract Assembler with a G2 manifold and a little exotic matter. The lattice that came out was the one every symmetry I had studied was secretly a shadow of.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes II, Theory of Everything.

The set with nothing in it. From it alone, by taking sets of sets, you can build every number and every structure in mathematics. It is surprisingly heavy for something containing nothing, and the eye slides off it.
pages.title: Empty Set

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A Void Wraith leaves behind a kind of absence. Feeding that essence to the Formal Proof Assistant, I asked it to collect every element present. It returned a set and confirmed that it was empty.
Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Liars Vault chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Power Set, Unity, Zero.

A slim instrument with a dial that sets which entangled channel a transceiver listens on. Entanglement cannot carry a message by itself, but it can share a key and a correlation; the tuner makes two devices agree on which pair of photons they share. It clicks softly between settings.
pages.title: Entanglement Tuner

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)My transceivers kept pairing with whichever partner was nearest. I mounted an entangled photon pair and a quantum dot on a neutronium plate as a reference, so every device I tune shares the same correlated source and stays on one channel.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Cryptography.

For every epsilon there is a delta: grains as small as anyone asks, and smaller. Found in Epsilon Ore in the Continuum (the Platonic Realm, Y 880 to 1040), and dropped by Fourier Wisps. The Analytic Continuator builds Real Continua and Infinitesimals from it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Epsilon Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Fourier Wisp (the Platonic Realm).
pages.title: Epsilon Dust

pages.text: $(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Epsilon Ore$(), in veins through the rock.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Fourier Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dense Stone, Infinitesimal, Real Continuum.

Omega to the omega to the omega, forever: the first ordinal that equals omega raised to itself. It is still countable, which feels absurd. The token has an endlessly recursive pattern, each layer like the last.
pages.title: Epsilon-Naught

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Raising omega to itself in the Ordinal Recursor, with power sets and ordinal shards, I reached a fixed point. Dark energy kept it from collapsing. I also found these in the Ordinal Spire.

Made in $(item)Ordinal Recursor$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Ordinal Spire chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Notes III, Absolute Singularity, Mathematics Singularity, Omega-One.

e^(iπ) + 1 = 0: the five most important numbers, from five fields of mathematics, in one line. Proved on the Formal Proof Assistant. A proof written so carefully that every step cites the rule that justifies it, branching back to axioms at the leaves. Machines check these line by line; mathematicians tend to trust them and move on. The tree is cool and heavy and it never contradicts itself.
pages.title: Formal Proof Tree

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mathematicians skip steps; I wanted a proof with none. Feeding an axiom schema and a function graph into a quantum processor, and wetting it with synaptic fluid, gave me a tree where every leaf was an axiom.

Hold it to your ear and it hums every frequency at once, so quietly that it sounds like silence.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Fourier Wisp (the Platonic Realm).

Grit with the same structure at every scale: each grain is made of smaller grains arranged exactly like the whole pile. Its dimension is not a whole number, somewhere between a scattering of points and a line. It sifts strangely, never quite settling, as if there is always more of it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Fractal Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Fractal Wyrm (the Platonic Realm).

A vein that never resolves. Zoom in on any facet and it repeats itself in smaller copies, edges crinkling like a coastline whose length depends on the ruler you use. It has a fractional dimension somewhere between surface and solid, and it feels faintly rough no matter how finely it is polished.
pages.title: Fractal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chipping at the axiom stone, I hit a seam whose outline kept getting longer the closer I measured it. Self-similarity that deep is not geology; it is a rule being iterated by the rock itself.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Platonic Realm (mine it for its drop).

Iterate z goes to z squared plus c, and colour each point by whether it escapes. The boundary that results is infinitely detailed: zoom in anywhere and new spirals, filaments and tiny copies of the whole appear. Holding it, the edges seem fuzzy, and they never sharpen however closely you look.
pages.title: Fractal Set

Hilbert's Hotel has infinitely many rooms, all full, and still has space for a new guest: everyone just moves up by one. The key is warm, as if someone has only now handed it over.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Hilbert Bellhop (the Platonic Realm).

A number whose square is minus one, which sounds like nonsense until you notice that it simply rotates the number line by a right angle. A tachyon's mass is imaginary, and this tiny bead was distilled from exactly that. It looks perfectly ordinary until you turn it, when it seems to point somewhere sideways.
pages.title: Imaginary Unit

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A tachyon's rest mass squared is negative, so its mass itself must be an imaginary number. I condensed tachyon flux over a tachyon crystal and pinned the result against the real continuum, and the leftover factor was i.

An infinity so large no smaller infinity can build it, by unions or power sets. Its existence cannot be proved from the usual axioms. The token is heavy and remote, as if seen from a great distance. Nothing reaches it.
pages.title: Inaccessible Cardinal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Using a topos, aleph-one and Hilbert's Hotel key in the Cantor Diagonalizer, I tried to build a larger infinity from smaller ones. It refused, and the result was an inaccessible cardinal.
Made in $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Infinity, Absolute Notes III.

Smaller than every positive real, and yet not zero. Leibniz used them freely; Weierstrass banished them; Robinson brought them back rigorously as non-standard analysis. The grain looks like nothing at all, and the closer you look the further away it seems to be.
pages.title: Infinitesimal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted the step size in a derivative to be truly smaller than anything. The Analytic Continuator pressed the real continuum against a quantum dot under superfluid helium, and squeezed out a number below every real but still above zero.

Every natural number paired with its mirror image below zero, closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication. The ring has a satisfying symmetry: turn it over and every number becomes its negative. Being a ring, you can add or multiply any two elements and never fall out of it.
pages.title: Integer Ring

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Subtraction kept breaking the natural numbers; three minus five had nowhere to go. Feeding an antimatter pellet into the engine alongside a natural lattice gave each number an opposite, the way antimatter gives each particle one.

pages.title: Koch Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)First turned up in a chest deep inside a Hilbert archive, wrapped like a specimen. Measuring its perimeter with finer and finer rulers, the number never settled. A border with no length is still a border.

pages.title: Modular Form

Eight-dimensional numbers, built by doubling quaternions once more. Multiplication stops even associating, so the order you group products in matters. Yet every non-zero octonion still has an inverse; they are the last and largest normed division algebra. The crystal is beautiful and slightly unsettling to look at for long.
pages.title: Octonion Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Doubling the quaternions by the Cayley-Dickson trick needed room for eight dimensions, which a Calabi-Yau manifold and some exotic matter provided. A prime shard stabilised the multiplication table. Hurwitz says there is nothing beyond this that still divides.

pages.title: Omega-One

pages.title: Power Set

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I asked the Formal Proof Assistant to list every subset of a natural number lattice, starting with the empty set. A proof tree confirmed what Cantor showed: no list of them could ever be complete.

pages.title: Prime Number Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I mined along a seam in axiom stone and found the veins only at prime intervals. The ore held numbers that could not be divided, and I kept every piece.

A sliver of a number divisible only by one and itself. Primes are the atoms of arithmetic: every whole number factors into them in exactly one way. In the Platonic Realm they grow wild in irregular clusters; out here they must be sieved. Each shard is sharp-edged and refuses to split.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Prime Number Ore in the Platonic Realm; dropped by the Axiom Sentinel (the Platonic Realm).

Hamilton's numbers: one real part and three imaginary units i, j and k, which multiply in a fixed cycle and do not commute. Swap the order and the sign flips. Rotations in three dimensions are just quaternion multiplication, so the crystal turns in the hand with an uncanny smoothness and never gimbal-locks.
pages.title: Quaternion Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Trying to extend the complex plane into three dimensions failed, as it did for Hamilton, until I added a fourth. A magnetic monopole supplied the twist that lets ij differ from ji, and the condensate held it steady.

Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Abstract Algebra.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Empirical Notes II, Hopf Fibration, Minkowski Lattice, Octonion Crystal, Spinor Lattice.

A machine's rate equations, solved ahead of time and printed as a table, so it never waits to work out its next step. Use it on a multiblock's controller (or a console machine) to fit it: +20% products each cycle, on top of what its precision gives, so a perfectly tuned machine goes past perfect. One upgrade per machine.
pages.title: Rate Table

pages.text: Made in $(item)Integrator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Rates as Equations.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Stability Margin.

Every fraction of one integer by another, which is enough to divide by anything except zero. Between any two rationals there is another, so the field is dense everywhere, yet the square root of two is nowhere in it. It shimmers like a fine mesh that hides countless holes.
pages.title: Rational Field

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I needed division, so I let a Casimir plate split the integer ring into finer and finer slices, mimicking how the vacuum between plates is divided into modes. Every ratio appeared, and with them, the unsettling gaps between them.

Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Geometers Ruin, Proof Stairs chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Integers and Rationals.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Analytic Continuator, Clonal Selector, Confidence Seal, Dosing Pump, Enzyme Assay Bench, Evolutionarily Stable Strategy, Gene Circuit Loom, Geometer's Table and more.
$(thing)Abstract Algebra$()$(br2)Quaternions, octonions and spinors: number systems that give up commutativity, then associativity.
pages.title: Abstract Algebra

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 40$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Groups and Symmetry, Modular Arithmetic.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Complex Plane.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Write two four-component numbers as a real part plus a three-vector part, a + u⃗ and b + w⃗, where the three imaginary units square to −1 and anticommute. Multiply them out using vector operations only.
$(thing)Algorithms$()$(br2)A recipe precise enough for a machine. Some take steps in proportion to the input, some its square: sorting a million things can take twenty million steps, or a trillion.
pages.title: Algorithms

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Vectors and Matrices, Combinatorics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Natural Number Lattice.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A good sort of n things compares them about n·log₂ n times. Write that count M.
$(thing)Bifurcations$()$(br2)Turn a setting slowly and, at one value, a steady state turns unstable and the system starts to oscillate: the Belousov reaction's threshold, and a heartbeat's.
pages.title: Bifurcations

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Stability, Oscillating Reactions.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Stability Margin, 1 Chemical Clock.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): In the Brusselator with feeds A and B the steady state turns unstable, and the mixture oscillates, past one value of B. Write that value H.
$(thing)Calculus$()$(br2)Infinitesimals, derivatives and integrals, and manifolds, the spaces calculus lives on.
pages.title: Calculus

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 30$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Real Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Infinitesimal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): The slope of a curve at a point is what the slope of a short chord approaches as the chord shrinks. For the power function x^n, write the slope at x as the limit of rise over run as the step δ goes to zero.
$(thing)Cardinality$()$(br2)How many members a set has. Von Neumann built every number from nothing: zero is the empty set, one is the set holding it. Unlocks Zero and Unity.
pages.title: Cardinality

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 30$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Formal Logic, Combinatorics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Empty Set.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A set has n members. A relation on it says, for every ordered pair of members, whether the pair is related. Write how many different relations there are.
$(thing)Category Theory$()$(br2)Objects and arrows. Functors between categories, and toposes; universes with their own logic.
pages.title: Category Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Set Theory, Geometric Topology, Abstract Algebra, Lie Groups.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Function Graph.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): In the category of finite sets, an arrow into C from a product A × B (or a disjoint union with D) is the same as choosing an element of C independently for every point of the source. Count the arrows from (A × B) + D into C as nested products over the points, using cardinalities |X|.
$(thing)Complex Analysis$()$(br2)Add the square root of minus one and every polynomial has its roots. Fourier series and fractals follow.
pages.title: Complex Analysis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 30$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Real Continuum.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A complex number has modulus r and argument θ, and you want every complex w with wⁿ equal to it. Write the k-th such root in polar form, remembering that the argument is only defined up to whole turns of 2π.
$(thing)Constructions$()$(br2)With only a compass and a straightedge: bisect an angle, draw a perpendicular, divide a line in the golden ratio. Unlocks Golden Ratio Glass on the Geometer's Table.
pages.title: Constructions

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euclid's Elements.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Euclidean Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A right triangle has legs a and b. Write the length D of its long side.
$(thing)Control Theory$()$(br2)Feed back too hard and a machine overshoots and rings; too gently and it drifts. Maxwell worked out where the line is. Unlocks the Governor.
pages.title: Control Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Feedback, Optimisation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Stability Margin, 2 Euclidean Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A controller corrects an error e by a gain k each second. Write how much error E is left after t seconds of smooth correction.
$(thing)Cooperativity$()$(br2)Haemoglobin's four sites help each other: once one holds oxygen, the rest grab it faster. Its curve is an S, not a bend (Hill).
pages.title: Cooperativity

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Enzyme Inhibition.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Assayed Enzyme.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Sites that help each other bind as an S-curve with steepness n. Write the share Y of sites filled at level S, for half-filling at K.
$(thing)Coordinates$()$(br2)Descartes put numbers on the plane: every point a pair, every line an equation, and geometry became algebra.
pages.title: Coordinates

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euclid's Elements, Vectors and Matrices.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Rational Field.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Write how far apart, D, the points (p, q) and (u, v) are on the plane.
$(thing)Cryptography$()$(br2)A secret only stays secret if breaking it takes longer than the secret matters. Unlocks the One-Time Pad.
pages.title: Cryptography

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Error Correction, Modular Arithmetic.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Error-Correcting Code.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A key has b bits, and a machine can try s keys a second. Write the longest time T it can take to find the key by trying them all.

$(thing)Curved Geometry$()$(br2)Drop the fifth postulate and parallel lines may meet, or spread apart: the geometry of a sphere, or of a saddle. Gauss measured mountain triangles to see which one we live in.
pages.title: Curved Geometry

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 40$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euclid's Elements, Cartography.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 π Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A triangle is drawn on a sphere of radius R and covers an area A. Write the sum S of its three angles.
$(thing)Eigenvalues$()$(br2)Some directions a matrix only stretches, never turns. How much it stretches them decides whether a system grows, shrinks or circles.
pages.title: Eigenvalues

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Vectors and Matrices.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Rational Field.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A 2 × 2 matrix has trace T and determinant D. Write the larger of the two amounts L it stretches its own directions by.
$(thing)Enzyme Inhibition$()$(br2)A molecule that sits in the enzyme's pocket without reacting slows it down; more substrate can push it out. How most drugs work. Unlocks a cheaper Stem Cell Culture.
pages.title: Enzyme Inhibition

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Enzyme Kinetics, The Steady-State Approximation.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Assayed Enzyme.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An inhibitor at level I, with constant Q, sits in the enzyme's pocket and makes it seem to need more substrate. Write the apparent constant A, from the enzyme's own K.
$(thing)Error Correction$()$(br2)Add a few check bits, cleverly placed, and a flipped bit can be found and flipped back. Unlocks the Error-Correcting Code.
pages.title: Error Correction

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Information Theory, Modular Arithmetic.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Prime Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A Hamming code uses r check bits on a block of 2^r − 1 bits. Write the share C of the bits that carry data.
$(thing)Euler's Formula$()$(br2)Raise e to an imaginary power and it does not grow: it turns, round a circle, as cos θ + i sin θ. A cheaper way to the Imaginary Unit.
pages.title: Euler's Formula

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): e, Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 e Crystal, 1 π Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): e^(iωt) goes once round the unit circle and back. Write how long one turn takes, the period T.
$(thing)e$()$(br2)Grow by 100% once, and you double. Grow by 1% a hundred times, and you get 2.70... Grow continuously, and you get e. Unlocks the e Crystal.
pages.title: e

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 60$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Rates as Equations.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Rate Table.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Grow by 1/n of the whole, n times in a row. Write the factor G you end up multiplied by.
$(thing)Euler's Identity$()$(br2)e to the power iπ, plus one, is nothing: the constants of growth, of the circle, of the imaginary, of one and of none, in a single line. Unlocks Euler's Identity.
pages.title: Euler's Identity

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 140$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euler's Formula, π, Cardinality.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Imaginary Unit, 1 Zero, 1 Unity.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A point at r·e^(iθ) in the complex plane has turned through θ round a circle of radius r. Write how far up from the axis it is, Y.

$(thing)Evolutionary Games$()$(br2)Let the winners have more offspring and the game plays itself: the mix a population settles into is the one nothing can invade. Unlocks the Evolutionarily Stable Strategy.
pages.title: Evolutionary Games

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Nash Equilibrium, Genomics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Genome Sample.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Fighters win a prize V; when two aggressive ones meet, both risk an injury costing C. When a share P of the population is aggressive, write how much more G an aggressive fighter earns than a timid one.
$(thing)Feedback$()$(br2)Measure what a machine does, compare it with what it should do, and push it back by the difference. Every thermostat works this way.
pages.title: Feedback

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Rate Table.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A machine multiplies what goes in by G; what comes out is scaled by H and taken away from what goes in. Write the overall gain T, out over in.
$(thing)Fixed Points$()$(br2)Where a system stops changing: an equilibrium. Newton found them by guessing, then sliding down the tangent, again and again.
pages.title: Fixed Points

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Rates as Equations, Chemical Equilibrium.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Rate Table.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): To find the square root of a, guess x, then average x with a/x. Write the better guess X.
$(thing)Fourier Series$()$(br2)Any repeating signal is a sum of pure tones. Fourier said so in 1807, and nobody believed him. Unlocks the Fourier Series.
pages.title: Fourier Series

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euler's Formula.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Imaginary Unit.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A signal jumps between +1 and −1 every half period. Write the size A of its n-th odd harmonic.
$(thing)Geometric Topology$()$(br2)Surfaces with one side and bottles with no inside.
pages.title: Geometric Topology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 50$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Calculus, Topological Matter.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Möbius Strip.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A compact orientable surface S with b boundary circles carries Gaussian curvature K, and its boundary curves bend within the surface with geodesic curvature κ. The total curvature integrated over the surface plus along the boundary is 2π times a topological invariant, 2 − 2g − b. Solve that for the number of handles g.
$(thing)Integers and Rationals$()$(br2)Take away more than you have and you need negative numbers; share out fairly and you need fractions. Unlocks Integer Rings and Rational Fields.
pages.title: Integers and Rationals

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 30$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Number Systems.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Natural Number Lattice.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Put a/b and c/m together over the common denominator b·m. Write the top of the result, N.
$(thing)Lie Groups$()$(br2)Groups of symmetries that turn smoothly, by any amount. The forces of the Standard Model are three of them: U(1), SU(2) and SU(3). Unlocks the Lie Group Lattice.
pages.title: Lie Groups

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Groups and Symmetry, Vectors and Matrices, Calculus.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Symmetry Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Write the dimension G of the group SU(n), the number of independent ways it can turn.
$(thing)Vectors and Matrices$()$(br2)Arrows that add, and the grids of numbers that stretch and turn them. Most of physics, and every computer picture, is linear algebra.
pages.title: Vectors and Matrices

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 35$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Number Systems, Euclid's Elements.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Rational Field.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A 2 x 2 matrix has trace T and determinant D. Write its larger eigenvalue λ.

$(thing)Manifolds and Curvature$()$(br2)Spaces that look flat close up but bend overall, in any number of dimensions. Their total curvature is fixed by their topology (Gauss-Bonnet); string theory asks which six-dimensional one the universe hides.
pages.title: Manifolds and Curvature

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Topology of Surfaces, Calculus, Curved Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 π Crystal, 1 Möbius Strip.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A closed surface has g handles. Write its total curvature K, the curvature added up over the whole surface.
$(thing)Markov Chains$()$(br2)A process with no memory: where it goes next depends only on where it is. Run it long enough and it settles into a fixed share of time in each state.
pages.title: Markov Chains

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 70$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Probability Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Dice Set.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A machine breaks with chance a on any day and is mended with chance b. Write the fraction P of days it works in the long run.
$(thing)Modular Arithmetic$()$(br2)Arithmetic on a clock: 9 + 5 is 2 on a twelve-hour dial. Fermat and Euler found its rules, and every cipher that keeps a secret on the open internet runs on them.
pages.title: Modular Arithmetic

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 40$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Primes.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Prime Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): p and q are two different primes. Write φ, how many numbers below pq share no factor with pq.
$(thing)Nash Equilibrium$()$(br2)A set of choices where nobody does better by changing alone. Nash proved every game has one, if chance is allowed.
pages.title: Nash Equilibrium

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Games and Strategy.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Rational Field.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Two firms sell the same thing; its price is A − B·(all they make), and each pays c a unit. Write how much Q each makes when neither can earn more by changing alone.
$(thing)Networks$()$(br2)Join every place to every other with as few links as possible and you have a tree; add one more and it has a loop, a second way round. Unlocks the Network Map.
pages.title: Networks

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Graph Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Integer Ring.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): How many different trees N join n labelled junctions, each link joining two of them, with no loop? Write it.
$(thing)Number Theory$()$(br2)Primes, modular forms and the Riemann zeta function; the hardest problems in mathematics are about whole numbers.
pages.title: Number Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 40$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Primes, Modular Arithmetic, Complex Analysis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 16 Prime Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Every whole number factors into primes in exactly one way. Use that to rewrite the series of 1/nˢ over all positive integers as a product, one factor for each prime p_k, where each factor is the geometric series of all powers of that prime.
$(thing)Numerical Methods$()$(br2)When an equation will not be solved, guess, and improve the guess. Newton's method doubles the correct digits at every step.
pages.title: Numerical Methods

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Fixed Points.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Rate Table.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): To find the square root of S from a guess x, write the next, better guess X (Heron's way).
$(thing)π$()$(br2)The ratio of every circle's circumference to its width, the same for all of them, and never ending or repeating. Archimedes trapped it between polygons. Unlocks the π Crystal.
pages.title: π

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 35$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Euclid's Elements.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Rational Field.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A regular polygon of n sides is drawn inside a circle of diameter 1. Write its perimeter P.

$(thing)Probability Theory$()$(br2)Chance has rules. Count the ways an outcome can happen, divide by all the ways anything can, and the result is exact even when every single trial is not. Unlocks the Dice Set.
pages.title: Probability Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 10$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Number Systems.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Cherenkov Quartz.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An experiment either succeeds, with probability p, or fails. It is repeated n times, independently. Write the probability P of exactly k successes.
$(thing)Projective Geometry$()$(br2)What a painter sees: parallel lines meet at the horizon, and lengths change, but straight lines stay straight.
pages.title: Projective Geometry

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Coordinates, Curved Geometry.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 π Crystal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A camera has its screen a length f behind a pinhole and sees a thing of height H at a range Z. Write how tall its image I is.
$(thing)Proof by Induction$()$(br2)Show it for the first case, and show that each case gives the next: then it holds for all of them, like dominoes. Unlocks the Proof Certificate.
pages.title: Proof by Induction

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 25$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Axiom Schema.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Write the sum S of the first n squares, 1 + 4 + 9 + ... + n², the formula that induction proves.
$(thing)Quantum Field Theory$()$(br2)Particles are excitations of fields. Wave packets, spinors, field lattices and Feynman diagrams.
pages.title: Quantum Field Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 50$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Calculus, Abstract Algebra, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Wave Packet.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A free scalar field is a collection of independent harmonic oscillators, one for every wave vector k. Each oscillator has a lowering operator that destroys a particle and a raising operator that creates one, multiplying a plane wave e^(∓ik·x) of the field's 4-momentum. Write the field operator as an integral over all momenta with the relativistically normalised measure.
$(thing)Regression$()$(br2)Draw the straight line that misses a cloud of points by the least. Turn an enzyme's curve upside down and it becomes one (Lineweaver and Burk).
pages.title: Regression

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Statistics, Enzyme Kinetics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Confidence Seal.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Turn an enzyme's speed upside down: write 1/v, R, as a straight line in 1/S, from its top speed V and constant K.
$(thing)Set Theory$()$(br2)Everything is a set. Power sets, the continuum, and the axiom of choice.
pages.title: Set Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 45$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Formal Logic, Cardinality.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Empty Set.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A set S has n elements. Count its subsets by size with binomial coefficients and add them up. Then the collection of all those subsets is itself a set: count ITS subsets the same way, with the inner count used as the size.
$(thing)Shortest Paths$()$(br2)Dijkstra's idea: settle the nearest unsettled place, then see whether it gives a shorter way to its neighbours. Unlocks routed Photonic Processors.
pages.title: Shortest Paths

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Networks, Algorithms.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Network Map.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Dijkstra settles V junctions over L links, keeping the nearest unsettled one in a heap that takes log₂ V steps per change. Write the work T.
$(thing)Stability$()$(br2)A ball in a bowl comes back when pushed; a ball on a hill does not. Whether a fixed point is a bowl or a hill decides everything. Unlocks the Stability Margin.
pages.title: Stability

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Fixed Points, Eigenvalues.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Rate Table.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Near a fixed point a disturbance x grows or shrinks as dx/dt = λx. Write the disturbance X after a time t, starting from x.
$(thing)The Steady-State Approximation$()$(br2)An enzyme's middle step is made as fast as it is used up: set its rate of change to zero, and the algebra falls out.
pages.title: The Steady-State Approximation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 80$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Enzyme Kinetics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Engineered Enzyme.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): An enzyme catches its substrate at a rate a, lets it go at b and turns it over at c. Write the substrate level K at which it runs at half speed.
$(thing)Stochastic Kinetics$()$(br2)In a cell there may be ten molecules of something: reactions happen one at a time, at random moments. Gillespie simulated them exactly.
pages.title: Stochastic Kinetics

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Statistics, Monte Carlo Methods, Markov Chains.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Microstate Tally.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Reactions fire at a total rate a. With a random number u between 0 and 1, write how long W to wait until the next one.
$(thing)Topology Optimisation$()$(br2)Let the mathematics decide where material goes: fill a cell only if it carries load. Structures come out like bone. Unlocks a cheaper Metamaterial Sheet.
pages.title: Topology Optimisation

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 100$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Optimisation, Metamaterials.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Optimised Pathway.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Each cell of a design holds a share r of material. Write its stiffness Y, from the solid's E and the empty cell's m, with the share raised to a power p, so half-filled cells are not worth keeping.

$(thing)Turing Patterns$()$(br2)A zebra's stripes, a leopard's spots, the ridges of a fingerprint: the same two-chemical sum at different spacings. Unlocks cheaper Turing Morphogens and Morphogenic Serum.
pages.title: Turing Patterns

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Reaction and Diffusion, Morphogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 1 Pattern Template.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A tail of radius R has bands laid round it at a spacing w. Write how many bands N fit along its circumference.

The zeta function encodes the distribution of primes in its zeros. Riemann conjectured that every non-trivial zero has real part exactly one half; nobody has proved it. This crystal grew in a single perfectly straight line, and every zero I have checked sits on it. It is cold and perfectly balanced.
pages.title: Riemann Zeta Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Analytically continuing the sum over primes past where it converges took a modular form, the complex plane and superfluid helium to damp the noise. The crystal that formed grew along the critical line. I keep looking for a zero off it.

Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Number Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Godel Sentence, Mathematics Singularity, Mathesis.

A proof of how far each setting can stray before the machine's working point stops being stable. Fitted to a machine, its precision falls off half as fast, so fine tuning is much easier. One upgrade per machine. Made in the Integrator.
pages.title: Stability Margin

pages.text: Made in $(item)Integrator$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stability.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Governor.

A flask of cells that have not yet decided what to become. Any of them could be a neuron, a muscle, a bone. The broth is warm and cloudy and seems to be thinking about its options. Under the microscope they look identical, and that sameness is exactly the point: every possibility is still open.
pages.title: Stem Cell Culture

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Synthetic biology lets me write life rather than read it. I took a genome sample, spliced in recombinant DNA to undo specialisation and used an engineered enzyme to hold the cells in their undecided state.

Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Enzyme Inhibition.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Anomalous Strain Culture, CAR-T Cell Culture, Grown Organ, Neural Organoid, Regeneration Tank, Telomerase Complex, Tumour Microenvironment Organoid, Xenobot Swarm.

Mathematics starts from almost nothing: a few rules of logic, the empty set, and counting.

$(thing)Primes$(): the $(item)Sieve of Eratosthenes$() crosses out the multiples of each prime and keeps what is left, about N / ln N numbers up to N. Set its limit high enough for the recipe, and a wheel to skip the small primes: less work is faster. It makes $(item)Prime Shards$() from Natural Number Lattices, or from Axiom Stone.

$(thing)Cardinality$(): zero is the empty set and one is the set holding it. The Formal Proof Assistant makes $(item)Zero$() and $(item)Unity$(), two of the five constants of Euler's identity. Physics uses them too: Zero presses a Casimir Plate with half the neutronium, Unity normalises a qubit with half the parts.

Mathematics can start almost at once. After $(thing)Number Systems$() the $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$() is made from quartz, iron, a comparator, a block of redstone and Quantum Dots, and it counts $(item)Natural Number Lattices$() from Cherenkov Quartz and redstone.
From lattices: $(item)Integer Rings$() with a redstone torch (a NOT gate: negation), and $(item)Rational Fields$() from rings with a comparator (which can subtract and compare: a quotient).

After $(thing)Formal Logic$() the $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() is made from early parts too (books, a lattice, quartz, an Entangled Photon Pair, iron and a comparator). It writes $(item)Axiom Schemas$() from lattices, paper and a book, and makes $(item)Empty Sets$() from empty glass bottles: nothing, held in something.
Both are built on the Extreme Assembly Table, like all of the mod's crafting.
Geometry, symmetry and shape: the mathematics of space, and of the extra dimensions Physics needs.

$(thing)Euclid's Elements$(): the $(item)Geometer's Table$() finds π as Archimedes did, from a polygon inside a circle. Set its sides and the care of the straightedge; the error must be under the recipe's tolerance. It makes $(item)π Crystals$(), one of the five constants of Euler's identity. Its calibration: fill a vertex with regular polygons.

$(thing)Groups and Symmetry$(): the $(item)Symmetry Lathe$() turns a blank with k-fold rotation and k mirrors, a group of order 2k that must be the recipe's. $(item)Symmetry Crystals$(), then $(item)Lie Group Lattices$() ($(thing)Lie Groups$()), which make Quaternion Crystals and Gauge Boson Clusters far more cheaply. Its calibration: complete a symmetric pattern. Its indexing head is a $(item)Symmetry Seed$() (crafted).

$(thing)Topology of Surfaces$(): the $(item)Topology Kiln$() fires surfaces with handles and cross-caps. Euler's χ = 2 − 2g − c and one-sidedness must be the recipe's: Möbius strips, Klein bottles, differential manifolds and Calabi-Yau manifolds, by new routes far cheaper than the old ones.
Compactification now needs $(thing)Manifolds and Curvature$(), and Grand Unification needs $(thing)Lie Groups$().
The mathematics of things that change: rate equations, where they settle, and whether they stay there.

$(thing)Rates as Equations$(): the $(item)Integrator$() steps a rate equation forward. Set the step size and the method's order; the error must be under the recipe's tolerance, and too big a step blows up. It makes $(item)e Crystals$() (one of Euler's five constants) and the first machine $(thing)upgrades$().

Upgrades: use one on a multiblock's controller or a console machine to fit it (one per machine; fitting another hands the old one back). The $(item)Rate Table$() adds 20% products each cycle on top of precision: a perfectly tuned machine goes past perfect. The $(item)Stability Margin$() ($(thing)Stability$()) makes precision fall off half as fast.

$(thing)Enzyme Kinetics$(): the $(item)Enzyme Assay Bench$() measures an enzyme. Saturate it to 90% without choking it. $(item)Assayed Enzymes$() make Nutrient Broth and Stem Cell Cultures with far less; $(thing)Inhibition$() and $(thing)Cooperativity$() add a cheaper Stem Cell Culture and a steep S-curve (Porphyrin Oxygen Carriers, like haemoglobin).
$(thing)Euler's Formula$(): the Integrator turns π, e and rationals into the $(item)Imaginary Unit$(), i.
Statistics, information and computation: how sure, how much, and how long.

$(thing)Statistics$(): the $(item)Statistics Engine$() samples until it is sure. Set the sample size and the confidence: the margin z·σ/√n must be under the recipe's tolerance. It makes the $(item)Confidence Seal$() upgrade (every chance product halfway closer to certain). $(thing)Regression$() gives Assayed Enzymes from the statistics alone; $(thing)Stochastic Kinetics$() counts Microstate Tallies in bulk. Its calibration: prove it.

$(thing)Information Theory$(): the $(item)Cipher Loom$() weaves Hamming codes. Set the block length and the check bits: the code must cover the block, and blocks that fail must be rarer than the recipe allows. It makes the $(item)Error-Correcting Code$() upgrade (catalysts wear on only every other run) and, with $(thing)Cryptography$(), $(item)One-Time Pads$(), which tune Entanglement Tuners two at a time. Its calibration: break a cipher.
$(thing)Algorithms$() and $(thing)Computability$(): how much work a recipe takes, and what no machine can ever decide.

The Transfinite Hierarchy is no longer a world of its own. It is the $(thing)Platonic Realm$()'s top layer, the Infinite: above Y 1280, across a wide gap of empty air over the Continuum, ordinal stone begins, and the Hierarchy's four strata rise one above another as they always did, with Hilbert's Hotel, the tesseract frames, the Hopf rings and the ordinal spires.

Up there the Hierarchy's laws still hold: Infinite Regress for anyone without a $(item)Well-Ordering Charm$(). Its creatures live only in the strata. The sky darkens as you climb. (The Codex page The Realm in Layers has the five layers below.)

The $(item)Cantor Key$() takes you to the strata from anywhere (used there, it takes you home); the $(item)Platonic Compass$() to the Realm's own islands (in the strata, sneak and look down to use it: it takes you down to the Continuum). Fall out of the bottom of the Realm and you land in the Quantum Foam.
From an older world: anyone still in the old Transfinite Hierarchy is carried to the same place in the strata. Anything built there stays in the old world, out of reach; bring it out before updating.
The best choice, and the shape of a network.

$(thing)Optimisation$(): the $(item)Optimiser$() walks downhill on a bowl. Set the step and the number of steps: each step multiplies the distance from the bottom by |1 − hλ|, and what is left after n steps must be under the recipe's tolerance. Too short a step crawls; too long overshoots, and past hλ = 2 it runs away. A step of exactly 1/λ lands at once, and the fewer steps, the faster. It makes the $(item)Optimised Pathway$() upgrade (a quarter less power per run) and, with $(thing)Topology Optimisation$(), Metamaterial Sheets from quartz, Quantum Dots and Rational Fields. Its calibration: find the shortest route.

$(thing)Graph Theory$(): the $(item)Graph Loom$() weaves networks. Set the junctions and the links: V − 1 links make a tree, and each one more is a spare route. The network fails only if all of its routes fail at once, and that must be rarer than the recipe allows. It makes $(item)Network Maps$() ($(thing)Networks$()) and, with $(thing)Shortest Paths$(), routes Photonic Processors with fewer dies and no qubits. Its calibration: lay the lightest network that joins every junction.
Both machines are built with Euclidean Shards, from the Elements.
Feedback: measure, compare, correct.

The $(item)Governor$() ($(thing)Control Theory$()) is set against a machine with a console: a multiblock's controller, or a console machine. Once a second, while the machine is short of 75% precision, it moves each setting a fifth of the way toward the recipe's best point; if the machine is not working at all, it sets it there. The machine runs at about 75% precision and stays there, whatever recipe it changes to. It never lowers a machine you have tuned higher.

It never goes all the way: the last quarter, and the extra products it brings, is the console's fine work. A Governor is the way to run many machines well; the console is the way to run one perfectly. On older multiblocks it keeps the tuning dial on its drifting target. It needs 32 FE a tick; right-click it to see what it holds.
When the best choice depends on what others choose.

$(thing)Games and Strategy$(): the $(item)Strategy Table$() plays the Hawk-Dove game. Hawks fight for a prize V and risk an injury C; doves share, or back down from a hawk. With a share p of hawks, a hawk out-earns a dove by (V − pC)/2, so the population settles at p = V/C. Set the hawk share close enough, over enough rounds that luck cannot hide the gap (its noise falls as 1/√n), and the table records an $(item)Evolutionarily Stable Strategy$() ($(thing)Evolutionary Games$()). Its calibration: find the equilibrium in a table of payoffs.
The Bioreactor grows Tardigrade Cultures from half the genomes and moss with one, and without enzymes or sterile neutrinos. Biology (1.4) takes the game further, into selection and genetics.
How an even mixture paints itself into stripes.

$(thing)Reaction and Diffusion$(): the $(item)Pattern Basin$() holds an activator and an inhibitor. Set how many times faster the inhibitor spreads (the ratio r) and the reaction rate k. Below r of about 5.8 nothing happens; above it stripes and spots form, about 2π·r^¼/√k apart, and that spacing must be inside the recipe's window. A faster reaction is quicker but needs a larger ratio for the same spacing. It makes $(item)Pattern Templates$(); with $(thing)Turing Patterns$(), Turing Morphogens from an Assayed Enzyme, Rational Fields and slime, and with both, Bioculture grows Morphogenic Serum cheaply. Its calibration: complete a symmetric pattern.
Wherever something changes in proportion to how much of it there is, e appears. Some of the places it turns up in the mod:

$(li)$(thing)Reaction rates$(): Arrhenius, k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT): every chemical machine's speed.$(li)$(thing)Radioactive decay$(): a source keeps e^(−t/τ) of its activity.$(li)$(thing)Boltzmann$(): a state of energy E is e^(−E/kT) as likely.$(li)$(thing)The Zeno Anchor$(): a system watched often enough never gets the chance to decay away.

$(li)$(thing)Waiting times$(): Gillespie, the next reaction after −ln(u)/a.$(li)$(thing)Control$(): a Governor's error falls as e^(−kt).$(li)$(thing)Statistics$(): the bell curve is e^(−x²/2); precision on a console falls off the same way.$(li)$(thing)The circle$(): e^(iθ) goes round it, and at θ = π reaches −1.

e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Five constants, each made in its own phase: $(item)Zero$() and $(item)Unity$() (Foundations), the $(item)π Crystal$() (the Geometer's Table), the $(item)e Crystal$() and the $(item)Imaginary Unit$() (the Integrator).
On the Formal Proof Assistant, e, i and π prove the $(item)Half Turn$(): e^(iπ) = −1, half a turn round the unit circle. The Half Turn, Unity and Zero then prove $(item)Euler's Identity$().

Billions of photonic neurons joined into a self-organising mesh. Connections that carry useful signals strengthen and the rest fade, so the lattice learns in the same way biological brains do, only far faster. Under light it shimmers with constant, restless activity.

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Photonic Neurons on their own did little. Woven through a Metamaterial Sheet and bathed in Synaptic Fluid in the Neural Synthesizer, they began to wire themselves together, and the network started to learn without instruction.

pages.title: Photonic Neuron

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neural Synthesizer, I arranged quantum dots so their emission depended on the light reaching them, and joined them with quartz waveguides. One dot started firing only when two others did: the first logic of a photonic brain.
