A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it. Near the Earth the effect is tiny; near a spinning black hole, inside its ergosphere, nothing can stand still.
Stand near a running $(item)Penrose Ergosphere$() or $(item)Kugelblitz Chamber$() and you are carried sideways: $(thing)Frame Drag$().

Light climbing out of gravity loses energy. Over a height H the fraction lost is $(thing)gH/c²$(), about 2.5×10⁻¹⁵ up a 22.5-metre tower. In 1959 Pound and Rebka measured it with the gamma ray of iron-57, whose line is so sharp that even this shows.

The $(item)Pound-Rebka Tower$() is built 1 to 8 storeys tall, 7.5 m each. A $(item)Cobalt-57 Source$() sits on a Doppler drive at the foot, the absorber at the top. Move the source up at exactly $(thing)v = gH/c$(), under a micrometre a second, and the climb is cancelled.

Counting decides how sure you are: the line is 190 µm/s wide, and N gamma rays find its centre to 190/√N. Count until the shift stands five times above that error, and set v within two of it. Keep the tower at the air's temperature: each kelvin between source and absorber shifts the line by 0.66 µm/s, as much as the whole effect.

Two black holes spiralling together shake spacetime: a wave passes, stretching space one way and squeezing it the other, by a strain h of 10⁻²¹ when it reaches us. The $(item)Laser Interferometer$() is an L of two long arms with a $(item)Test Mass$() at each end: a laser split between the arms comes back to interfere, and a wave changes the pattern.

Four noises hide the wave. $(thing)Shot noise$(), the graininess of light, falls as the laser power P and the arms' finesse F rise, but $(thing)radiation pressure$(), the photons' kicks on the mirrors, grows with them. Both depend only on F√P; where they are equal is the standard quantum limit.

$(thing)Seismic noise$() falls tenfold with each isolation stage; more stages, slower to lock. Machines running nearby shake the ground; below sea level it is quieter, as at KAGRA. $(thing)Thermal noise$() in the mirrors falls as √T: cool them with your coolant.

A black hole merger, h = 10⁻²¹, needs a signal-to-noise of 8. A neutron star merger is five times fainter: only cold mirrors will do. Its record points a telescope at the $(thing)kilonova$(), where gold and platinum were made, and every detection gives a great deal of Insight. The chirp's parameters are read off by Bayesian inference: the Analyzer takes black hole records as evidence.

In 1975 Colella, Overhauser and Werner split single neutrons with a perfect silicon crystal and joined them again, and tilted the whole thing. One path ran a few centimetres higher than the other; gravity slowed the neutron on it; the two waves came back out of step. Gravity, acting on a quantum wave: $(thing)Δφ = 2πm²gλA·sin α/h²$().

Grow a $(item)Silicon Boule$() (fused silica and coal in the Crystal Growth Furnace), study it for its Laue Pattern, and cut two into a $(item)Perfect Crystal Interferometer$(); three blades still joined at the base, their lattices aligned to a fraction of an atom.

The $(item)Neutron Interferometer$() runs on a radium-beryllium source. Choose the wavelength and tilt it until gravity has turned the phase at least 30 radians and lands it on a bright fringe; count until the phase is known to 0.1 rad. Each record is a great deal of Insight.

Sound in a fluid flowing faster than sound cannot make headway upstream. Where the flow crosses its own speed of sound there is a horizon for sound, and the mathematics of sound near it is the mathematics of light near a black hole. Hawking radiation included.

The $(item)Analog Black Hole$() makes the flow out of $(fluid)Bose-Einstein Condensate$(): it streams toward a laser step, subsonic, and falls over it, thinned and fast, supersonic. Set the density (sound speed grows as its square root), the flow and the step depth so that both hold.

At the horizon phonon pairs appear, one carried off downstream, its partner escaping up: a glow at $(thing)T_H = ħκ/2πk_B$(), a few nanokelvin. The condensate itself must be colder than that to see it, and the correlations summed over many shots. Nothing but Bose-Einstein Condensate is cold enough as the coolant.

Two experiments have put quantum theory and gravity into one equation: gravity bending a neutron's phase, and a horizon glowing with quantum pairs. Both are $(thing)semiclassical$(): the quantum world on a smooth, classical spacetime.

Beyond them, spacetime itself must be quantum. One way to compute it is to sum over every way of building spacetime out of simple pieces, at random. With Semiclassical Gravity, the Monte Carlo Engine runs these $(thing)causal dynamical triangulations$(): four records of each experiment and two Metric Tensors make a $(item)Spin Foam Lattice$().
From here the road leads on to quantum gravity itself, and to the strings and singularities of the Codex's far end.
Clocks deep in a gravity well run slow: by $(thing)1/√(1 − r_s/r)$() at a distance r from a mass with Schwarzschild radius r_s.

The $(item)Time Dilation Chamber$() holds samples round a dense core. Set its mass and how close they sit: at three times dilation it grows Time-Dilated Samples in bulk; radium ages into polonium; at five, liquid spacetime is strained into $(fluid)Strained Spacetime$(). Too close and they fall through the horizon. Each storey (1 to 7) holds more.

A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it: a gyroscope near the Earth turns by $(thing)Ω = 2GJ/(c²r³)$(). A $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() carried in the off hand holds you steady: no Frame Drag, no Tidal Strain.

Tides are the difference between the pull on your two ends: $(thing)2GML/r³$(). Near a small black hole they pull you into spaghetti. Tidal shear crystals, a gyroscope and a micro-singularity knot spacetime into a $(item)Lense-Thirring Vortex Core$().

A falling body follows a $(thing)geodesic$(): the straightest path through curved spacetime. The $(item)Geodesic Compass$() points along one. A mass squeezed inside $(thing)r_s = 2GM/c²$() lets no light out.
Light follows geodesics too, and is bent by $(thing)α = 4GM/(c²b)$(); 1.75″ at the Sun's edge. A mass exactly in front of a star turns it into an Einstein ring.

The $(item)Lensing Concentrator$() aims at a star through a lens mass and turns the focused light into power, at night, under open sky. The magnification $(thing)A = (u² + 2)/(u√(u² + 4))$() grows without limit as the alignment u → 0, but the aim jitters by 0.3 milliarcseconds: choose a massive, near lens so the Einstein radius is big. Above A = 20 it grows an $(item)Einstein Ring Lens$().

Two compact stars spiral in as gravitational waves carry off their orbit; how fast the pitch rises depends only on the $(thing)chirp mass$() (m₁m₂)^(3/5)/(m₁ + m₂)^(1/5). The Binary of the Accretion Frontier drops Chirp Signal Records and Merger Remnants.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by The Binary.

The Laser Interferometer, listening to a chirp with a strain sensor, can hear a $(item)Gravitational Wave Echo$(); repeats after the ringdown, if a horizon is not quite a horizon. Played in the Frontier, an echo summons The Binary just as a Binary Black Hole Merger record does.

Alcubierre found a solution of general relativity that moves a bubble of flat space at any speed: space contracts ahead of it and expands behind. Its wall must be made of $(thing)negative energy$(), from $(item)Negative Energy Lattices$() of Casimir plates.

The $(item)Warp Field Forge$() shapes the bubble. Set its speed, radius and wall sharpness: the negative energy needed grows as v²R²σ, the shear across the wall as vσ (above 5 it tears a passenger apart), and a wall too thick for its bubble (Rσ < 10) leaks. A $(item)Warp Bubble Core$() must be superluminal, with under one solar mass of negative energy.
Use a Warp Bubble Core to anchor where you stand: it becomes an $(item)Anchored Warp Bubble$(). Use that, anywhere, to return there, once. Recipes only take the plain core.

Maldacena and Susskind: two entangled particles are joined by a wormhole too small to cross. The $(item)ER=EPR Weaver$() makes pairs and sends their halves to two mouths. Fidelity falls with the distance and with the weaver's own heat, and every pair heats it. Cold, and close, it weaves an $(item)ER Bridge Thread$().

AdS/CFT: gravity inside a space is a quantum field theory on its boundary. The Holographic Encoder turns a holographic matrix, an island and quantum spacetime condensate into a $(item)Holographic Screen$(), and a screen and Hall bars into a $(item)Boundary CFT Chip$(). For gravity in three dimensions, the boundary theory's central charge is exactly 3L/2G.

A black hole of mass M glows at $(thing)T = ħc³/(8πGMk)$(), radiates power ∝ 1/M², and evaporates in a time ∝ M³. A stellar hole is colder than the sky; one of a billion kilograms, hotter than any star.

The $(item)Micro Black Hole Evaporator$() holds one (a Kugelblitz Seed in a slot) and feeds it dust exactly as fast as it radiates. Feed it less and it shrinks, heats, runs away and explodes; more, and it swells. Below 6×10⁸ kg its gamma rays are too much for the lead. It gives great power and $(fluid)Hawking Radiation$(); above 10¹³ K, $(item)Hawking Quanta$() too.

A black hole has entropy $(thing)S = Ac³/(4Għ)$(), its area in Planck units over four, the most any region can hold: the $(item)Bekenstein Crystal$(). It evaporates; if what comes out is purely thermal, what fell in is gone, and quantum mechanics forbids that.

The $(item)Page Curve Analyzer$() follows Hawking quanta through an evaporation. Firewalls and soft hair are two answers. The third: the radiation's entropy rises, then after the $(thing)Page time$(), when half the hole's entropy is gone, at M/√2, falls back to zero. A $(item)Page Curve Record$() carried in the off hand keeps your hotbar in order (no Information Loss). With an ER bridge, it finds the $(item)Island$() that makes the curve turn.

Loop quantum gravity quantises space: areas come in steps of $(thing)8πγℓₚ²√(j(j+1))$(). The $(item)Spin Network Loom$() weaves Planck Shards into $(item)Planck Area Tiles$(), tiles into $(item)Spin Network Nodes$(), and nodes with liquid spacetime into $(fluid)Quantum Spacetime Condensate$().

Causal set theory scatters events at random and keeps only their order: the Monte Carlo Engine sprinkles a $(item)Causal Set Seed$(). Asymptotic safety follows gravity's coupling to a fixed point instead of infinity: a node and a seed together make a $(item)Fixed-Point Lattice$().
Empty space looks empty only if you are not accelerating. Accelerate at a, and the vacuum glows at $(thing)T = ħa/(2πck)$(); one kelvin needs 2.5×10²⁰ m/s².

The $(item)Unruh Accelerator$() is a storage ring: electrons of Lorentz factor γ bent by a field B feel a = γ²c²/r, with r = γmc/eB. Gently, it calibrates an $(item)Unruh Thermometer$() (1-10 K). Hard, above 5000 K, its bath turns superfluid helium into Hawking radiation. But the beam radiates as γ³B, and the cavities replace only 500 kW.

The $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$() works up from $(item)Lorentz Transforms$() and the $(item)Minkowski Lattice$() to the $(item)Metric$() and $(item)Riemann Curvature Tensors$() and finally the $(item)Einstein Field Core$().

The order follows the physics. First flat $(thing)Minkowski$() spacetime, where the $(thing)Lorentz transform$() says how lengths and times change between moving observers. Then gravity: the $(thing)metric$() measures distance in curved spacetime, the $(thing)Riemann tensor$() measures the curvature, and Einstein's equations tie that curvature to matter.

Why it matters: wormhole throats need an $(item)Einstein Field Core$(), and Alcubierre coils need $(item)metric tensors$(). Kugelblitz chambers can merge black holes into $(item)Gravitational Wave Crystals$(); the ripple of two horizons becoming one, frozen solid.
Lengths shrink and clocks slow as you approach light speed. This crystal is always moving at 0.99c.$(br2)Made in $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$().

Novikov's principle, plainly: if time travel is possible, the only histories allowed are ones that are already consistent. You cannot stop your own birth; something always intervenes.$(br2)Here it is enforced. Closed timelike curves now need a Novikov Crystal: a time loop is only allowed if it can never produce a paradox.

Field notes. It only works in the $(thing)Quantum Foam$(). Each virtual particle has a $(thing)resonance$() (0-100) that changes from place to place. The harvester catches whichever particle its dial is tuned closest to, and the closer the better.

So I take a $(item)Resonance Probe$() to where the harvester stands and read the four values. Then I either move the harvester or retune it, to choose what it makes. Two wasted afternoons before I accepted that the readings are local.

Freeman Dyson, 1960: a civilisation hungry enough for energy would wrap its star in collectors, and we could spot it by its waste heat. I appear to be that civilisation now.$(br2)This controller is too complex for a crafting grid. Build it on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$(); check JEI for the exact parts.

The yield, as I have worked it out:$(br2)Output = base x satellites/50 x (1 + shells/16)$(br2)and doubled again once the sphere is complete. A finished sphere is the brightest thing I have built, and from outside you cannot see it at all.

A curved plate of a shell intended to surround a star completely, capturing all of its output. Stellar iron forms its structure, metamaterial catches the light, and a Higgs field capacitor keeps the mass low enough for the shell to hold itself together. It is warm on its inner face and cold on the outer.
pages.title: Dyson Shell Segment

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A solid shell collapses under its own weight. In the Metamaterial Weaver, with Stellar Plasma, I added a Higgs Field Capacitor to each segment, reducing the mass so the shell could finally hold.

One collector out of millions that together surround a star in a cloud. Each one harvests a sliver of starlight, computes its own position and beams the energy home. It is a small, neat thing, but many of them together can catch a star.
pages.title: Dyson Swarm Satellite

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Solar Statites could hover, but not steer or transmit. In the Metamaterial Weaver I gave each one a Quantum Processor and a superconducting coil, and they began organising themselves into a swarm.
Made in $(item)Metamaterial Weaver$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Dyson Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Array, Von Neumann Probe.

Cosmic neutronium, spacetime alloy, glueballs, hyperons and a superheavy metal, all melted together above the temperature at which matter can still be said to have a melting point. The ingot never cools. Its glow is the afterimage of a collapsing star that the metal seems to remember, and it is warm through any glove.
pages.title: Hypernova Alloy Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Transcendent Plasma Forge finally ran hot enough that the ingredients stopped behaving as separate materials. I dropped in a supernova remnant to seed the melt and an alloy of everything I had came out, still shining long after the forge shut down.

Plasma from the most violent explosions in the universe. Hypernovae release more energy than ordinary supernovae and leave behind black holes. The plasma is hotter and denser than any star's core, and it wants to escape.
pages.title: Hypernova Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Feeding a Hypernova Alloy Ingot and a Quark Star Core into the Transcendent Plasma Forge, the plasma that came out matched the conditions of a hypernova.

Cold, dusty gas from which stars are born. It is mostly hydrogen and helium, drifting in faint clouds that glow when lit by nearby stars. It is light and very cold. Given enough of it and enough time, gravity would gather it into a new sun. It is the raw material of every star.
pages.title: Nebular Gas

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stars form from collapsing nebulae. Sweeping the halo with a metamaterial sheet in the Dark Matter Halo Collector, I gathered the cold gas between the stars.

Made in $(item)Dark Matter Halo Collector$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Distillate of Spacetime, Protostar Core, Stellar Core, Stellar Plasma, Stellar Singularity, Stem Cell Culture.

Gold, platinum and uranium, made in seconds when a supernova or neutron star merger floods nuclei with neutrons faster than they can decay. The cluster is a dense jumble of heavy metal nuggets, gleaming in several colours at once.
pages.title: R-Process Cluster

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Firing neutrino flux and a sterile neutrino at a supernova remnant in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber, I saw nuclei capturing neutrons faster than they could decay. Heavy elements formed in a single flash.

Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Flerovium Ingot, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Nuclide Forge, Stellar Singularity, Theoretical Notes I.

When a star exhausts the hydrogen in its core it swells, and its outer layers expand and cool to a dull red. The Sun will do this in about five billion years. The envelope is enormous and tenuous, a thin, glowing fog that barely seems to weigh anything.
pages.title: Red Giant Envelope

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a stellar core in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber past hydrogen exhaustion, I watched its outer layers puff outward. Separating the swollen envelope from the core left me with this bloated fog.
Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Magnetar Shard, Stellar Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

pages.title: Dyson Sphere

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Dyson Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Higgs Field Capacitor.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): A thin closed shell of radius r surrounds a star and absorbs all of its light. In equilibrium the shell radiates the star's whole luminosity from its outer surface only, as a black body at uniform temperature T. Write that luminosity as the radiated flux integrated over the shell in spherical coordinates.
$(thing)Nucleosynthesis$()$(br2)Every element heavier than helium was made in a star. Iron is where fusion stops; supernovae make the rest.
pages.title: Nucleosynthesis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 90$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 White Dwarf Core.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Inside a star at temperature T, two nuclei of reduced mass μ must tunnel through their Coulomb barrier to fuse. Their cross-section is S(E)/E times a tunnelling factor exp(−√(E_G/E)). Average the cross-section times relative speed over the thermal distribution of energies E.

The light left over when matter goes beyond stellar temperatures. It is a hot, glowing gas that carries the memory of every star that went into it. It moves like a slow, luminous fog. Its glow is the colour of a sky just after a star has set.
pages.title: Residual Starlight

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing a Stellar Core beyond its limits in the Transcendent Plasma Forge, with magnetar and pentaquark shards, the matter gave off a glowing gas. Residual starlight, the afterglow of transcendence.

Made in $(item)Transcendent Plasma Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Cosmic String Segment, Dark Energy, Dimensional Residue, Distillate of Spacetime, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, Horizon Shard and more.

Iron forged in the core of a star, where fusion stops being profitable. Iron has the most tightly bound nucleus, so fusing it or splitting it costs energy. The ingot is dense and dull grey and carries a faint heat that seems to come from somewhere deep inside it.
pages.title: Stellar Iron Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a white dwarf core with ordinary iron in stellar plasma, I drove fusion until it stopped. Iron was where nucleosynthesis ended, and the Chamber left me an ingot of star-forged metal.
Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dyson Shell Segment, Magnetar Shard, Stellar Singularity, Supernova Remnant.

The expanding shell of gas and the collapsed core left when a massive star's core can no longer support itself. The shockwave seeds space with heavy elements. This remnant is a dense nugget wrapped in a faint, glowing haze of debris.
pages.title: Supernova Remnant

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Neutron Star Forge I collapsed a stellar iron core under neutronium pressure and flooded it with neutrinos. The red giant envelope blew outward and left a small, heavy remnant.

Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Nucleosynthesis.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Gold Ingot, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Magnetar Shard, Quark Star Core, R-Process Cluster, Stellar Singularity, Theoretical Notes III and more.

In the forge, above stellar-core temperatures, properties like hardness and conductivity stop being fixed and start being chosen. This ingot is what a metal looks like when someone else chose them. It weighs exactly what the forge decided, and feels faintly as though it might change its mind.
pages.title: Transcendent Metal Ingot

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed the forge a hypernova alloy and things that are barely matter at all: an aleph-null shard, Russell's paradox, a cosmic processor. The processor set the rules, the paradox loosened the old ones, and the metal accepted whatever properties it was given.

Made in $(item)Transcendent Plasma Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Apeiron Ingot, Axiomatic Field Emitter, Omniscience Catalyst, Omnium Ingot, Pleroma Confluence.

Plasma above the temperature where matter has fixed properties. It is no longer any element; it is all of them and none. It glows every colour at once and has no fixed density. Instruments dipped into it return a different reading every time, all of them correct.
pages.title: Transcendent Plasma

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pushing hypernova alloy with an Aleph-Null Shard and a Russell Paradox Set into the Transcendent Plasma Forge, the plasma stopped having fixed properties. Stellar transcendence.

Made in $(item)Transcendent Plasma Forge$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmological Constant, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Heat Death Remnant, Horizon Shard, Inflaton Field, Omnium Ingot, Pocket Universe and more.

A coil of hypernova alloy wound around an aleph-null shard over a cosmic neutronium coil, superconducting at room temperature. It carries a current that never quite finishes counting itself. The windings seem to continue past the point where the coil should end.
pages.title: Transfinite Coil Block

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Above stellar-core temperatures even cosmic neutronium coils fail. I wound hypernova alloy around an aleph-null shard with a room-temperature superconductor and a cosmic processor, and the coil held.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Transcendence.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Pleroma Confluence.

A self-replicating machine that builds copies of itself from whatever material it finds. Send one to a star system and it builds more, which build more, until every star has one. Von Neumann proved such machines were possible. This one is small, neat and patient.
pages.title: Von Neumann Probe

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Nanite Assembler I gave a Dyson Swarm Satellite claytronic catoms and a Quantum Processor, so it could fabricate its own parts. It began printing a copy of itself before I had finished writing the entry.
Made in $(item)Nanite Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Dyson Swarm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Theoretical Notes I.

What remains when a modest star sheds its outer layers: a core of carbon and oxygen about the size of the Earth, held up against gravity only by electron degeneracy pressure. It is fiercely hot and absurdly heavy for its size, and will cool for longer than the universe has existed.
pages.title: White Dwarf Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After the red giant phase, the Nucleosynthesis Chamber left a small, glowing ember behind. Electron degeneracy held it up, exactly as Chandrasekhar described, and it slowly radiated away its leftover heat.
Made in $(item)Tectonic Press$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Stellar Evolution.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Singularity, Stellar Iron Ingot, Stellar Singularity.
Takes a star through its whole life, collapse, ignition, giant phase, death, and keeps the elements it forges.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
pages.title: Nucleosynthesis Chamber

pages.text: Almost every atom heavier than helium in my body was cooked inside a star. This chamber runs that process on a workbench: a gas cloud falls in on itself, fusion lights, the star swells, and it dies. My notes on stellar evolution follow each stage.

A star begins as a cloud. I harvest $(fluid)Nebular Gas$() with the Dark Matter Halo Collector and collapse it into a $(item)Protostar$() in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().

Gravity squeezes until the core reaches millions of degrees and hydrogen fuses. I ignite the protostar into a $(item)Stellar Core$(). When a real star runs low on hydrogen its outer layers balloon outward; mine swells into a $(item)Red Giant$(), and I keep its $(item)White Dwarf$(); the bare, glowing core left behind.

White dwarfs forge $(item)Stellar Iron$(); the end of fusion. Iron's nucleus is among the most tightly bound there is; fusing it costs energy instead of releasing it. Dyson shells are made of stellar iron.

A red giant crushed onto stellar iron goes supernova. Its remnant feeds the $(item)r-process$(), rapid neutron capture, nature's way of making gold and everything heavier, and it is needed for every quark star.

pages.title: Coherence Stabiliser

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Foam I watched my own outline blur into overlapping drafts. I braided an entangled photon pair through a quantum field lattice and a spin foam lattice on a chronosteel frame, so that it carries the decoherence away from me instead.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.

A circuit board laid across a Calabi-Yau manifold, its traces running through six compact dimensions. It holds circuits far larger than its surface, folded through hidden space. Turning it over, I can see the traces continue on the back, and into somewhere else.
pages.title: Cosmic Circuit Board

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Tesseract Assembler, I wrapped a Metamaterial Substrate around a Calabi-Yau Manifold with a Cosmic String Segment, an Attoscale Inductor and Exotic Solder. The traces followed every dimension.
Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Processor, Ontological Processor, Transfinite Processor, Unified Notes II.

A die holding a galaxy-scale computation folded into a square I can pinch between two fingers. Its traces stretch across light-years inside the fold. In the dark it glimmers faintly, like a patch of night sky.
pages.title: Cosmic Die

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Cutting a Cosmic Logic Wafer in the Planck-Scale Cutter, I worried the light-year traces would unfold. Superfluid helium held them still while the cutter separated each die.
Made in $(item)Planck-Scale Cutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Processor, Unified Notes III.

A loop of cosmic string that bends light into perfect focus. The missing wedge of space around the string acts as an ideal lens, with no aberration at all. It is a thin circle of light that hums faintly and never needs replacing.
pages.title: Cosmic String Lens

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the String Resonance Loom, I bent a Cosmic String Segment around a Tesseract Lens with a Graviton Crystal. The loop's conical space focused light more perfectly than any glass could.
Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.

Etched with a lens made from a cosmic string, each trace on this wafer is a light-year long, folded into itself. It holds circuits on a galactic scale in a disc I can carry. The surface is dark, scattered with faint points like distant stars.
pages.title: Cosmic Logic Wafer

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the Quantum Lithographer I engraved a Hyperdimensional Wafer through Quantum-Dot Photoresist, focused by a loop of cosmic string. The string folded each trace across a light-year of space.
Made in $(item)Quantum Lithographer$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Die, Unified Notes I, Warm Helium.

The fifth tier of processor: a computer the size of a galaxy, folded into a chip. Its traces stretch across light-years through the fold, and its computation runs at a cosmic scale. It is dark and starry, and warm with constant thought.
pages.title: Cosmic Processor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the Femtoscale Assembly Line, I placed a Cosmic Die on a Cosmic Circuit Board with a Hyperdimensional Processor and attoscale parts. The resulting chip computed the orbits of a galaxy in seconds.

Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Absolute Pedestal, Autonomous Calibrator, Cantor Diagonalizer, Conceptual Singularity Compressor, Convergence Engine, Cosmic Flux Coupler, Dimensional Residue, Entangled Transceiver and more.

A casing built to contain the birth of a universe. Spin foam lattice, multiverse shard and cosmic neutronium are folded over a hyperlattice frame, around rift frame casing. It is unpleasantly heavy and quietly warm.
pages.title: Cosmogenic Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Universe Forge needed a shell strong enough for a Big Bang. Spin foam is the fabric of quantum spacetime, a multiverse shard is the boundary between universes, and cosmic neutronium held them both.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Inflation Chamber, Reality Lattice Casing, Universe Forge.

A surface on which open strings can end, with its own dynamics and its own charge. Our universe could be a three-dimensional D-brane floating in higher dimensions. The sheet ripples like silk, and strings seem to cling to it.
pages.title: D-Brane Sheet

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stretching quantum strings across metamaterial with brane tension fiber in the Compactification Lathe, I noticed their ends stuck to the sheet. Exotic matter held it rigid enough to keep.
Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, M-Brane.

Space in a higher-energy state than it should be, metastable and fragile. Contained, it looks like perfectly clear liquid, but the energy it stores is the energy of an entire universe waiting to tunnel down. I handle it gently.
pages.title: False Vacuum

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a False Vacuum Membrane through the Bose-Einstein Condenser with superfluid helium, I found the condensate stabilised the metastable state long enough to bottle it. Coleman would not approve.

Made in $(item)Bose-Einstein Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Distillate of Spacetime, Exotic Matter Singularity, False Vacuum Membrane, Foam Substrate, Inflaton Condensate, Metastable Vacuum Lattice, Pocket Universe and more.

Seven curled dimensions with a special holonomy whose symmetry group, G2, is the automorphism group of the octonions. M-theory on such a space gives a four-dimensional world with realistic physics. The manifold is tightly folded and seems to have no inside or outside.
pages.title: G₂ Manifold

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a Calabi-Yau with an extra moduli direction and the octonions' symmetry, the Compactification Lathe produced a seven-dimensional manifold with G2 holonomy, held open by exotic matter.
Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, E8 Lattice, M-Brane, M-Theory Core.

A device that keeps its bearer's worldline intact inside a black or white hole. Without it, tidal forces and causal chaos are lethal within seconds. It is heavy and cool and hums faintly, like a gyroscope.
pages.title: Geodesic Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside a black hole I nearly lost my worldline. Combining a Kerr metric shard, graviton crystal and chronon capacitor in a hyperlattice frame on the Extreme Assembly Table, I built an anchor to keep it.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.

At sufficiently high energy, the electromagnetic, weak and strong couplings run together and meet. Grand unified theories predict magnetic monopoles and proton decay as a consequence. The core is bright and calm, three forces resting in a single symmetry.
pages.title: Grand Unified Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running the Standard Model's couplings upward with superpartners included, I saw them converge. In the Tesseract Assembler, a monopole and a quantum string held the high-energy state long enough to crystallise it.

Made in $(item)Tesseract Assembler$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Grand Unification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Eschaton Core, Standard Model Singularity, Theory of Everything, Transcendent Metal Ingot, Transcendent Plasma.

Gravitons are the hypothetical quanta of gravity, and this crystal holds them frozen in a lattice. It feels heavier than it is: the stored gravitons pull on my hand as well as on the floor. Near it, falling dust curves slightly toward the crystal before reaching the ground.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Graviton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cooled Virtual Gravitons from the quantum foam in Superfluid Helium inside the Graviton Condenser until they could not escape. Graviton Wisps carry them naturally, and I found more in vaults, monoliths and derelict stations.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Anomaly Vault, Bulk Monolith chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tether, Bulk Crystal, Bulk Stone, Compactification Lathe, Cosmic Processor, Cosmic String Lens, False Vacuum, Geodesic Anchor and more.

A web of straps and plates that takes the pull of a crushing field and spreads it through every bone at once, so no single joint bears it. Tidal forces kill by difference, not by strength; the harness erases the difference. Wearing it feels like being hugged by a planet.
pages.title: Graviton Harness

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)A walk through a high-gravity field nearly broke both my ankles. I laid graviton crystals across neutronium plating and added an inertia damper to smooth the gradients, so that the field pulls on all of me equally and none of me in particular.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.

pages.title: Graviton Wisp

pages.text: All that is left of a universe that has reached maximum entropy: no stars, no gradients, nothing to drive any process at all. It is cold, perfectly even and perfectly still, a uniform grey with no texture to catch the light. Holding it feels like holding silence.
pages.title: Heat Death Remnant

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I let a Pocket Universe in the Universe Forge run to its end. Trillions of years compressed into a few minutes, and the bubble came out like this: inert, even, and oddly peaceful. Its stillness is what makes new universes possible.

A two-dimensional membrane from M-theory, the eleven-dimensional framework in which strings are the edges of membranes. A brane like this could host an entire universe on its surface, with gravity alone leaking into the Bulk. It is a sheet of light that ripples when I breathe on it.
pages.title: M-Brane

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wove a D-Brane Sheet with a G2 Manifold and a String Coupling Crystal on the String Resonance Loom, turning the coupling up until the strings fused into a membrane. Eleven dimensions, counted twice to make sure.

Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, Exotic Matter Crystal, Inflaton Field, M-Theory Core, Multiverse Shard, Penteract Display, Theoretical Notes II and more.

Five superstring theories turned out to be limits of one eleven-dimensional theory, whose fundamental objects include membranes as well as strings. Witten called it M-theory, and nobody knows what the M stands for. The core vibrates in more directions than seem possible.
pages.title: M-Theory Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Wrapping an M-brane on a G2 manifold and a compactified circle in the Compactification Lathe, I found all five string theories as limits of one. Exotic matter kept the eleventh dimension open.
Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): M-Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, Theory of Everything.

A one-dimensional vibrating string, the fundamental object of string theory. Its mode of vibration decides what it is: one note an electron, another a photon, another a graviton. In the hand it is a thread of light that hums, changing its tune slightly with my pulse.
pages.title: Quantum String

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The String Resonance Loom stretched a Cosmic String Segment down to the Planck scale, tuned it with a Tachyon Crystal and held it in a Superposition Crystal. When it began to vibrate in discrete modes, I knew it was a string.

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 260$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Quantum Gravity, Set Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Normal Distribution Crystal, 2 Metric Tensor.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Events are scattered at random with density ρ through spacetime. Write the chance P that a region of volume V holds none at all.

$(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$()$(br2)At the end of time only massless things remain, and massless things cannot tell an infinite distance from a finite one. Rescale the dead universe and its infinite future becomes the Big Bang of the next aeon.
pages.title: Conformal Cyclic Cosmology

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 280$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Creation from Nothing, Heat Death, Cosmogenesis.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 De Sitter Horizon Shard.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Light does not care about the size of space, only about its shape: it moves through conformal time, the integral of c dt divided by the scale factor a(t). In a universe that ends in pure vacuum energy, a(t) = a₀ e^{Ht} grows exponentially forever. Write how much conformal time is left from t₀ to the infinite future.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$()$(br2)Matter and antimatter should have annihilated perfectly. They did not: heavy neutrinos decayed out of equilibrium, unequally to leptons and antileptons, and sphalerons turned the excess into baryons; one in a billion. Unlocks the Baryon Asymmetry Crystal.
pages.title: Leptogenesis

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 190$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Reheating, Neutrino Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 8 Sterile Neutrino.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): How rare are baryons? Count the photons: a black-body gas at temperature T has, per unit volume, an integral over energy of E² times the Bose-Einstein occupation 1/(e^{E/k_BT} − 1), times the density of states for two polarisations, 1/π² (units ħ = c = 1). Write the number density of photons.
$(thing)M-Theory$()$(br2)Strings are the edges of membranes in eleven dimensions.
pages.title: M-Theory

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 120$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): String Theory, Brane Cosmology, Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Quantum String.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Eleven-dimensional gravity compactified on a circle of radius g_s·l_s must reproduce ten-dimensional string gravity. The 10-D inverse coupling 1/(2κ²) = 1/((2π)⁷ g_s² l_s⁸) must equal the 11-D one, 1/((2π)⁸ l₁₁⁹), integrated around the circle's circumference in the extra coordinate y.

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$()$(br2)Before inflation, before time: a closed universe can tunnel into existence from no space at all, or begin without a boundary, its time becoming space near the start like the South Pole of a sphere. Quantum cosmology writes the wave function of the whole universe.
pages.title: Creation from Nothing

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 220$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Reheating, Vacuum Stability, Quantum Gravity.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Spin Foam Lattice.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Quantise a closed universe with only one degree of freedom, its radius a, filled with vacuum energy Λ. The Hamiltonian constraint becomes a Schrödinger-like equation with zero energy for the wave function ψ(a) of the whole universe: a kinetic term from the curvature of ψ, minus a potential a² − (Λ/3)a⁴ that forms a barrier between a = 0 and the classical universe (units with the factor 3π/2G absorbed). Write it.

$(thing)Reheating$()$(br2)Inflation leaves space empty and cold. When the inflaton reaches the bottom of its potential it oscillates and decays, and its energy becomes a hot plasma of every particle there is: the hot Big Bang begins here. Unlocks Reheating Plasma.
pages.title: Reheating

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 170$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Inflation, High-Energy Particle Physics.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Strange Matter Pellet.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): At the end of inflation the inflaton decays at a rate λ, and its energy turns into a thermal bath of g relativistic species whose energy density is π²gT⁴/30. The decay completes when the expansion rate has fallen to the decay rate, with H² = ρ/(3M_P²). Write the temperature the universe is reheated to.

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$()$(br2)What could stop a universe from starting at all? A vacuum energy a little larger and it would fly apart before stars formed; a Higgs coupling a little smaller and the vacuum would be unstable. Ours sits, by measurement, at the edge: metastable. Unlocks the Metastable Vacuum Lattice.
pages.title: Vacuum Stability

pages.text: $(thing)Insight$(): 180$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Cosmic Inflation, The Standard Model.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 4 Higgs Field Capacitor.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): The quartic coupling λ of the Higgs field is not a constant: it runs with the energy scale μ. The top quark, with Yukawa coupling y, dominates the running and drives λ down logarithmically from its value λ₀ at the top mass m. Write λ at scale μ in this top-dominated approximation.

A clamp for tears between universes. Graviton crystals pin the edges of the rift, void lattice keeps the Bulk from closing in, and exotic matter props the gap open just long enough to reach through. It vibrates faintly, as if something on the other side were tugging back.
pages.title: Rift Anchor

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every rift I opened closed before I could use it. In the Graviton Condenser I bound a Graviton Crystal to a Void Lattice Shard with Exotic Matter, and the next rift stayed open long enough for me to put my hand through.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Multiverse.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Exotic Matter Crystal, Inflaton Field, Multiverse Rift Stabilizer, Multiverse Shard, Void Lattice Shard.

A casing reinforced against tearing open: void lattice, graviton crystal and chronosteel over a hyperframe. It is built to sit at the edge of a rift between universes, and it feels faintly cold on one side.
pages.title: Rift Frame Casing

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Stabilising a multiverse rift tore through every casing I tried. I layered a void lattice shard, which is rigid even with nothing in it, over a hyperframe with graviton crystal to hold the geometry. It held.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmogenic Casing, Multiverse Rift Stabilizer.

A pylon that pins a patch of spacetime in place, built around a spacetime anchor core and a chronosteel coil. The ground around it feels unusually solid, as if gravity had made its mind up. Compasses near it point steady.
pages.title: Spacetime Anchor Pylon

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Large machines warped the ground they stood on. I built a pylon around an anchor core with a chronosteel coil and hyperframe casing, and the warping stopped at its edge.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.

A lattice of spin networks evolving in time, the loop quantum gravity picture of spacetime as discrete quanta of area and volume. It looks like a soap foam frozen in place, but each bubble is a quantum of space itself. Pressing it does not compress it; space does not come in smaller units.
pages.title: Spin Foam Lattice

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fed Graviton Crystals through the Graviton Condenser together with a qubit to track the states and a condensate to hold them coherent. Spacetime started showing up in discrete chunks, which loop gravity had promised.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Quantum Gravity.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Bounce Core, Coherence Stabiliser, Cosmogenic Casing, Dimensional Residue, No-Boundary Seed, Pocket Universe, Spin Network Loom, Superintelligence Core.

Compactified dimensions woven tight with quantum strings, so they stay rolled up under load. Without it, extra dimensions tend to unroll, and the laws of physics shift. It looks like a tight knot of light, faintly warm.
pages.title: Dimensional Stabiliser Matrix

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)On the String Resonance Loom I wove Quantum Strings through a Calabi-Yau Manifold with a Topological Insulator and Exotic Matter. The compact dimensions held their shape even under pressure.

Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): String Theory.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Adaptive Feedback Core, Anomaly Containment Ward, Contained Anomaly Specimen, Dimensional Stabiliser, Quarantine Field Matrix, Theoretical Notes I.

Turn this crystal and the strength with which strings interact changes. Turn it far enough and a strongly coupled string theory becomes a weakly coupled one of a different type: this is string duality. It is cool and smooth and feels slightly alive.
pages.title: String Coupling Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I fixed a compactified circle's radius with a bulk crystal and varied the coupling in the Compactification Lathe. At strong coupling, Type IIA became M-theory, and the crystal captured the transition.
Made in $(item)Compactification Lathe$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): M-Brane, Theoretical Notes III.

Energy borrowed from the vacuum itself, stored with exotic matter to keep the books balanced. Inside, graviton crystal holds the field taut while a dark matter lens focuses it. It feels heavier when full, though nothing has been added.
pages.title: Vacuum Energy Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The Casimir cell ran out of gap. I needed more vacuum to work with, so I folded in exotic matter for negative energy, graviton crystal for structure and a dark matter lens to concentrate the field.
Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Compactification.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Singularity Energy Cell.

Two branches of physics are about time itself: $(thing)Origin$(), how a universe begins, and $(thing)Finality$(), how it ends. Origin starts with $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$(): run the expansion backwards and everything was once hotter and denser than the core of a star.

The $(thing)Friedmann equation$() says how fast space expands: H² = 8πGρ/3 − kc²/a² + Λc²/3. Matter and radiation slow it, curvature bends it, and the vacuum energy Λ, dark energy, takes over in the end. Exactly flat space has the critical density, about five protons per cubic metre.

$(li)$(thing)Primordial Nucleosynthesis$(): for three minutes the universe fused hydrogen into helium. $(item)Primordial Nucleosynthesis Ash$() comes from quark-gluon plasma (or reheating plasma) in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().$(li)$(thing)Cosmic Inflation$() and $(thing)Reheating$(): see the next chapter.$(li)$(thing)Leptogenesis$(), $(thing)Vacuum Stability$(), $(thing)Creation from Nothing$() and $(thing)Conformal Cyclic Cosmology$() come after.

Where Finality ends, Origin begins. Roger Penrose noticed that at the end of a heat death only massless particles remain, and light has no clock: it cannot tell an infinitely large, cold universe from a tiny, hot one. Rescale the dead universe's infinite future and it is the Big Bang of the next $(thing)aeon$().

In the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(): $(item)Heat Death Embers$(), a $(item)De Sitter Horizon Shard$() and $(fluid)Dark Era Haze$() make an $(item)Aeon Boundary Shard$(); the Shard with a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$() and inflaton condensate makes two $(item)Universe Seeds$(). A $(item)Bounce Core$() from a Big Crunch makes one too.

Origin also feeds what came before it: the $(item)Universe Forge$() can make a $(item)Pocket Universe$() from first principles, a seed, a true-vacuum bubble, the asymmetry, the ash and the plasma, and the Eye of the Horizon's and the Omnilex's universes now want Primordial Ash and a No-Boundary Seed.

The Big Bang alone cannot explain why opposite sides of the sky have the same temperature to one part in 100,000: they were never in contact. $(thing)Inflation$() does: before the hot Big Bang, a scalar field, the inflaton, sat high on its potential and made space grow exponentially, sixty e-folds in 10⁻³² s.

Build the $(item)Inflation Chamber$(). It condenses the $(fluid)Inflaton Field$() and $(fluid)False Vacuum$() into $(item)Inflaton Condensate$(). In its Operation console keep the slow-roll ε = 2/φ² below 1 and N = (φ₀² − 2)/4 above 50, but start the field too high and inflation turns $(thing)eternal$(): quantum jumps outrun the roll, and the bubble never ends (in our universe, other bubbles still may).

$(thing)Reheating$(): at the bottom of its potential the inflaton oscillates and decays. The chamber turns Condensate and a little quark-gluon plasma into $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$(), every particle there is, at 10⁹ GeV and more. That plasma is the raw stuff of every other Origin material.

Reheating makes matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion photons there is one baryon left over. Andrei Sakharov's conditions say what it takes: baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and a moment out of equilibrium.

$(thing)Leptogenesis$() meets all three: heavy right-handed neutrinos decay a little more often into leptons than antileptons, and sphaleron transitions of the electroweak vacuum convert that excess into baryons. In a $(item)Quark-Gluon Collider$(), antimatter and sterile neutrinos in $(fluid)Reheating Plasma$() leave a $(item)Baryon Asymmetry Crystal$(). With the antimatter of the Antiverse, crystals become a $(item)Baryogenesis Seed$() in the $(item)Mirror Foundry$().

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$(): a universe can fail before it starts. A vacuum energy larger by a factor of a hundred and no galaxy forms; the measured one is 10¹²⁰ times smaller than quantum theory's natural guess; the $(thing)cosmological constant problem$(). And the Higgs coupling runs downwards with energy until, near 10¹⁰ GeV, a deeper vacuum opens: ours is $(thing)metastable$(). The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() maps it into a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$().

$(thing)Creation from Nothing$(): quantise a whole closed universe and its wave function obeys the Wheeler-DeWitt equation. Vilenkin's universe tunnels through a barrier from no space at all; Hartle and Hawking's has no boundary; near the start time turns into space, and asking what came before is like asking what is south of the South Pole.
The $(item)Inflation Chamber$() folds spin foam, inflaton condensate and a metastable vacuum into a $(item)No-Boundary Seed$().
Plucks cosmic strings into fundamental quantum strings and weaves them into membranes.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 4$() machine.
pages.title: String Resonance Loom

pages.text: Two very different 'strings'. A $(thing)cosmic string$() is a hypothetical crack in spacetime left by the early universe, light-years long and thinner than a proton. A $(thing)fundamental string$() is string theory's basic object: each vibration mode is a particle. The $(item)String Resonance Loom$() turns one into the other.

Triggers false-vacuum decay and cosmic inflation to grow, and later harvest, a pocket universe. I have never been more nervous.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 5$() machine.

pages.text: 13024 blocks: a broad disc under a dome of glass that steps in as it rises, a coil round every step, and a spire through the crown. The new universe swells inside the dome.

pages.text: Interface Ports either side of the controller, in the rim of the disc.
Its signature material is the $(item)Embryonic Vacuum$(): made here and nowhere else.$(br2)Made in $(item)Universe Forge$().
Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$(); check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

A $(thing)false vacuum$() is a metastable state; if it decays, a bubble of true vacuum expands at nearly light speed. $(thing)Inflation$(), driven by the inflaton field, stretched our universe by a factor of at least 10^26 in a fraction of a second. Combine them and you get a universe in a box.

Procedure: first forge a $(item)Pocket Universe$() from a $(item)Universe Seed$(), $(fluid)False Vacuum$() and $(fluid)Inflaton Field$(). Then feed it back in to harvest it until only a $(item)Heat Death Remnant$() remains.$(br2)Four remnants can be re-inflated into a new seed. Nothing is wasted, not even the end of time.

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 4 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Bubble Universe, Cherenkov Quartz, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dimensional Residue, Distillate of Forces, Distillate of Spacetime, Exotic Matter Crystal, Heat Death Remnant, Logos Thread, Pocket Universe, Quintessence, Stellar Plasma, Universe Seed.
Made in $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$().
Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
An entire cosmos, folded into a bubble you can hold. Please do not drop it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Causality Loop Engine$().
A grain of false vacuum primed to inflate into a cosmos.$(br2)Made in $(item)Universe Forge$().
All that is left of a universe at maximum entropy. Cold, even and perfectly still.$(br2)Made in $(item)Universe Forge$().

Every journey to another dimension, by Brane Shifter, rift, wormhole, falling through the void or the hyperobject, now takes a moment: the travel animation builds up on screen for under two seconds, and only then do you jump. The loading screen of each world is its own.

Wherever you arrive, you arrive standing: never inside blocks, never in mid-air, never on top of a world's ceiling (the Quantum Foam's Relativity Breakdown, the build limit), never in a fluid or on something that burns. The ground nearby is searched for two free blocks over solid ground; open sky first, otherwise the spot nearest the height you left from.
Only when there is nowhere at all is a small platform built for you, with the room above it cleared. Laws of the place still apply: carry its attunement item.

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() is the exception to open sky: it has a bedrock roof, so you arrive under it, on dry rock as near y 100 as the cave allows, with a Mantle Breach beside you for the way back.

Every strange dimension has the item that lets you survive it. Each one was made from what you brought back from the places before it, so it carries their protection too.$(br2)Carry an attunement item and every dimension whose own item comes $(l)earlier$() in this list cannot touch you at all: no debuffs, no strange gravity, no rules.
$(li)$(item)Form of the Self$(): the Platonic Realm$(li)$(item)Penning Harness$(): the Antiverse$(li)$(item)Coherence Stabiliser$(): the Quantum Foam$(li)$(item)Brane Tether$(): the Bulk

$(li)$(item)Geodesic Anchor$(): black and white holes$(li)$(item)Well-Ordering Charm$(): the Transfinite Hierarchy$(li)$(item)Primordial Charter$(): Hyperdimensional Reality$(li)$(item)Identity Kernel$(): the Transcendental$(br2)So the $(item)Primordial Charter$() shields you completely in every place before Hyperdimensional Reality, does its usual job inside Hyperdimensional Reality itself, and only the Transcendental still needs the $(item)Identity Kernel$(). In its own dimension, each item works as it always has.

Brane cosmology says our universe is a membrane adrift in a higher-dimensional $(thing)Bulk$(). The $(item)Brane Shifter$() slips me sideways into it, and back. It requires the Brane Cosmology research.

First crossing. The Bulk is an endless void of floating islands under the shadow of a vast hypercube; a four-dimensional cube, of which I only ever see a 3D shadow. Monoliths hide vaults of exotic materials, and $(item)Void Lattice Ore$() is common here.
Physics aside: in brane-world models only gravity leaks out into the Bulk, which might be why it is so much weaker than the other forces. Standing out here, I believe it.
Slip sideways out of this brane and into the Bulk.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Brane Shifter$(): Cantor Key, Horizon Diver, Planck Diver

$(thing)Dimension data: The Bulk$()$(br2)$(thing)Nature$(): Gravity 0.5 g, 5 spatial dimensions, time x1, ordinary vacuum.$(br2)$(thing)Carry$(): $(item)Brane Tether$(), with it, half gravity, twice the knockback.

$(thing)Natives$(): Brane Strider, Graviton Wisp, Moduli Crawler.$(br2)$(thing)Landmarks$(): Anomaly Vault Graviton Reef, Ore Void Lattice, Ore Kaluza Klein, Ore Dilaton, Graviton Reef, Crystal Spire, Bulk Monolith, Derelict Station.
Log, the Bulk, fifth crossing. It is not uniform. There are regions: the open $(thing)Bulk$(), the crystal $(thing)Graviton Reefs$() and the $(thing)Moduli Wastes$().

$(thing)Derelict Stations$() hold salvage and supplies; someone came here before me. $(thing)Collapsed Calabi-Yau Knots$() hang over the Wastes with caches at their hearts. In string theory, Calabi-Yau shapes are the tiny curled-up extra dimensions; these have come uncurled.

The locals:$(li)$(thing)Graviton Wisps$() pull you toward them and crush you up close.$(li)$(thing)Brane Striders$() slip between branes when hurt and leave you seeing double.$(li)$(thing)Moduli Crawlers$() hunt in packs and climb anything.$(br2)I keep my back to a wall. It does not help with the Crawlers.
$(thing)Graviton Wisp$(). Lives in: Graviton Reef, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Graviton Wisp Core, Graviton Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
$(thing)Brane Strider$(). Lives in: Graviton Reef, Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Brane Tension Fiber, Void Lattice Shard, Kaluza-Klein Shard.
$(thing)Moduli Crawler$(). Lives in: Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.

Ruins and impossible structures keep their treasure in $(item)Containment Caches$(), not chests. Each dimension seals its own kind: the Bulk Cache borrows room from a fifth dimension, the Euclid Reliquary of the Platonic Realm closes on an exact right angle, the Hilbert Locker is always full and always has room for one more.
A cache works like a chest of 27 slots; hoppers and pipes can reach it. Breaking it spills its contents and drops the cache itself. You can make an ordinary $(item)Containment Cache$() of your own.
Sunday. Even a lab deserves some style. Put a block of any high-tech material in a $(item)Stonecutter$() for plating, tiles, bricks and pillars, and back again, so nothing is wasted.

Surround a material block with glowstone dust for four $(item)Lamps$(). Most bricks and tiles also come as stairs, slabs and walls.$(br2)Chronosteel, Spacetime Alloy, Cosmic Neutronium, Dilithium and Void Lattice each have a storage block too, which is how I keep the hoard tidy.
Made in a crafting grid.
Nether expedition, day 2. $(item)Dilithium$() grows down here. Its lattice is porous to antimatter, which makes it the only practical regulator for an annihilation reactor.

Field notes: annihilation turns all the rest mass of matter and antimatter into energy; E = mc², the full amount, against under 1% for fusion. The hard part has always been holding antimatter without it touching anything. A crystal it can pass through gently is exactly what such a reactor needs.
Porous to antimatter. It regulates annihilation reactions.$(br2)Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilithium Ore in the Nether.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Dilithium Crystal$(): Annihilation Core, Block of Dilithium, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Dilithium Crystal, Magnetar Shard and more
Every other place has its own law, and the law is not kind to visitors. Carry the right $(thing)attunement$() anywhere in your inventory and you will live, with a reminder of where you are.

$(li)$(item)Brane Tether$(), the Bulk: without it, $(thing)Dimensional Bleed$(); with it, half gravity and twice the knockback.$(li)$(item)Primordial Charter$(), Hyperdimensional Reality: without it a hostile new law every few seconds; with it, a new law (good or bad) every minute and a half.

$(li)$(item)Form of the Self$(), the Platonic Realm: without it, $(thing)Imperfection$(); with it, only a $(thing)sword$() can dig; pickaxes barely scratch the ideal.$(li)$(item)Coherence Stabiliser$(), the Quantum Foam: without it, constant $(thing)Decoherence$(); with it, you still blink a few blocks now and then.

$(li)$(item)Well-Ordering Charm$(), the Transfinite Hierarchy: without it, $(thing)Infinite Regress$() deepens every ten seconds; with it, Regress I and hunger.$(li)$(item)Geodesic Anchor$(), both holes: without it, death in two seconds. In the white hole gravity points $(thing)up$(); sneak to fall.$(li)$(item)Identity Kernel$(), the Transcendental: without it, $(thing)Dissolution$().
Ties your mass to our brane. Carry it in the Bulk, or in any field of extra dimensions.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Your own ideal form, cut in crystal. Carry it in the Platonic Realm.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Keeps your wavefunction in one piece. Carry it in the Quantum Foam, or in an altered vacuum.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Every descent ends somewhere. Carry it in the Transfinite Hierarchy.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
A copy of the laws as they were first written. Carry it in Hyperdimensional Reality.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().
Keeps your worldline your own. Without one, the inside of a black or white hole kills you in two seconds.$(br2)Made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

None of these places has a bottom you can die on. Fall off the floor of one and you fall into another:$(li)off the $(thing)Bulk$(): back onto our own brane$(li)through the $(thing)Platonic Realm$() (and its upper strata, the Transfinite Hierarchy): into the Quantum Foam$(li)below the $(thing)Transfinite$(): into the Quantum Foam

$(li)through a $(thing)black hole$()'s singularity: out of its white hole$(li)past the top of a $(thing)white hole$(): home$(li)between the branches of $(thing)Hyperdimensional Reality$(): into the Bulk$(li)out of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): into Hyperdimensional Reality$(br2)Carry the right attunement for wherever you land.

One world is different. The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() has a true floor, the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(), solid iron that nothing yet cuts, and a roof of bedrock. There is nothing to fall through: you leave the way you came, by a $(item)Mantle Breach$().

The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C, as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior.

A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up.
Stand inside a structure built in more dimensions than three and your eyes stop agreeing with your feet. The deeper you go, the more space folds to match the object you are in:

$(li)$(thing)Tesseracts$() and Bulk monoliths: nested cubes turning inside one another$(li)$(thing)Fractals$(): the view contains itself, again and again$(li)$(thing)Platonic solids$(): mirrored through their symmetry$(li)$(thing)Hilbert's Hotel$() and the Ordinal Spire: an endless corridor$(li)$(thing)Calabi-Yau knots$() and Hopf rings: space wound round itself

$(li)$(thing)Graviton reefs$(): light bent into an Einstein ring$(li)$(thing)Anomaly vaults$(): the picture tears$(li)the heart of the $(thing)Transcendental$(): all of it at once.$(br2)It is harmless, and fades as you walk out. It can be switched off in the client config (structureDistortion).

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() needs no attunement item, its laws are only the planet's own, and they press harder the deeper you go. You reach it with the $(item)Core Drill$() (research $(thing)Plate Tectonics$()), cutting the Overworld's bedrock floor; you leave by any $(item)Mantle Breach$(); one opens beside you wherever you arrive.

$(li)$(thing)Lithostatic Pressure$(): below y 100, one level for every 25 blocks deeper; you move and mine slower.$(li)$(thing)Tremors$() in the Crustal Caverns: a few seconds of Seismic Vertigo.$(li)$(thing)Mantle plumes$() in the Mantle Convection Zone throw you upwards.$(li)$(thing)Geomagnetic storms$() in the Geodynamo Core leave you Magnetized: compasses spin.

$(li)The $(thing)Natural Reactor$() is radioactive, its background is far above the Overworld's, and Fission Fragment seams are hot. Carry a Geiger Counter.$(li)$(fluid)Basaltic Magma$(), the Interior's sea, does 10 damage a hit and Fire Resistance does not help. $(fluid)Deep Brine$() sets you alight like lava.
The floor is the $(item)Inner Core Boundary$(): solid iron under 330 GPa, which no tool yet made can break. The roof is bedrock, which the Core Drill cuts again from below.

Others have been down here before. In the Crustal Caverns stand $(thing)Deep Boreholes$(): drill holes cased in steel and abandoned two dozen blocks down, a broken drill floor at the top and a cache at the bottom of the hole.

In the Natural Reactor, lead-walled $(thing)Oklo Reactor Ruins$() are dug round the reactor seam itself; fission fragments and uraninite in the floor. Bring a Geiger Counter and radiation-plated armour; their caches hold fuel, graphite and control rods.

A plinth that waits for a conclusion. When the right answer is placed on it, the surrounding proof settles into consistency and the room grows quiet. A wrong answer sits there and does nothing at all.
pages.title: Answer Pedestal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)At the heart of each proof chamber stood this pedestal. I understood it once I realised the whole chamber was a theorem waiting for its final line.
$(item)Anticarbon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anticarbon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Anti-Gold Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anti-Gold Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Antihydrogen Ice$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Antihydrogen Ice

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Anti-Iron Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Anti-Iron Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).
$(item)Antisilicon Ore$(). The Antimatter variant of our own universe variant.
pages.title: Antisilicon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Antiverse (mine it for its drop).

Soil of the Antiverse, made of antiprotons, antineutrons and positrons. It is stable only because everything around it is antimatter too; brought into contact with ordinary matter, a gram of it would release about 180 TJ.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Antiverse.
pages.title: Antisoil

pages.text: Planks cut from the Arbor, pale and fine-grained, with faint branching lines running along their length. The wood smells of rain and seems to grow warmer when people walk across it. Nails go in easily and never split it.
pages.title: Arbor Planks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I split Arbor heartwood into planks for building. The grain branched instead of running straight, and every board I cut was slightly different.
$(thing)Used in$(): Arbor Planks Slab, Arbor Planks Stairs.

A lamp that shines when its axiom is in force. Its light is steady and colourless, and when the axiom is withdrawn it simply goes dark. Rows of them read like a truth table drawn in light. Watching them, I finally understood how much of mathematics is a matter of choice.
pages.title: Axiom Lamp

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)These lit and darkened as I flipped axiom toggles inside the proof. They showed me which postulates I had accepted, and which I had not.

A switch that adopts or rejects an axiom. Flip it and the local truths rearrange; some things become provable, others not. It moves with a satisfying click, like choosing between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry.
pages.title: Axiom Toggle

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Inside the proof I found switches wired to the axiom lamps. Each one admitted or denied a single postulate. Solving the room meant choosing a consistent set.

Two bodies coiled round each other in a tightening spiral, shedding gravitational waves. Each turn is faster than the last, until the chirp ends in a merger.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Chirp Signal Record, Merger Remnant.
pages.title: The Binary

pages.text: A thread pulled from a brane, the membrane on which strings end. It is strong beyond any material, because its tension is a property of spacetime rather than chemistry. It hums faintly and pulls back toward the surface it came from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Brane Tension Fiber

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Brane Striders walk on membranes in the Bulk, and when they fell they left these threads behind. I found more in derelict stations, still taut as if attached to something invisible.
Made in $(item)String Resonance Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): D-Brane Sheet.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 70. Gives Bridgmanite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Bridgmanite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

$(thing)Brine Jelly$(): A clear jelly with a glowing ring in its bell, pulsing up and sinking back on the slow currents, trailing long tentacles. Whatever brushes them is stung. Found drifting in Titan's hidden ocean.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Luminous Mesoglea.
pages.title: Brine Jelly

pages.text: Bigger on the inside: it borrows a little room from a fifth dimension. In brane cosmology our whole universe floats in such a bulk.
pages.title: Bulk Cache

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Transcendent Cache.

A translucent crystal from the Bulk whose facets seem to point in directions I cannot quite name. Light passing through comes out a little out of phase with itself, as if it had taken a short detour through another axis.
pages.title: Bulk Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing in the Bulk where the extra dimensions are most tightly curled. Looking through one, I saw my own hand from an angle I should not have been able to see it from.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Brane Tension Fiber, Bulk Cache, Graviton Wisp Core, Silicon Life Spore, String Coupling Crystal.

The bedrock of the higher-dimensional Bulk: a grey stone that seems to have more surfaces than it shows. Edges blur where the extra dimensions curl back in. It is cool and unremarkable to the touch, which is somehow worse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef).
pages.title: Bulk Stone

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Everything in the Bulk rests on this stone, and I first broke some off to see if the extra dimensions would follow it home. They did, a little; enough to make it useful in crafting.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dilaton Crystal, Hyperdimensional Pearl, Kaluza-Klein Shard, Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.

Rather than order, this ore measures size. Its crystals pair up perfectly with one another, unless they come from a larger infinity, in which case some are always left over. It is heavier than it looks, and denser in every sense.
pages.title: Cardinal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Next to ordinal veins I found a second kind of ore that refused to be sorted, only compared. Diagonal arguments on the samples always left a remainder, the clear mark of a larger cardinal.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).
$(thing)Catalyst Sprite$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Organic Evaporite, Nickel Catalyst.
pages.title: Catalyst Sprite

pages.text: The shell of a chamber where time runs at another rate. Even on Earth, a clock a kilometre higher gains about one part in 10¹³.
pages.title: Time Dilation Chamber Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Tiles laid in no repeating order, each pattern drawn at random. Any stretch that looks designed is a coincidence the dice were always going to throw.
pages.title: Chance Tiles

pages.text: Cherenkov quartz cut into small bricks, each one glowing softly blue along its edges. A wall of them looks like a shallow pool at night. They are smooth and slightly cool to the touch. Every joint carries its own thin line of blue light, so the whole wall seems sketched in glow.
pages.title: Cherenkov Bricks

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I cut Cherenkov quartz into bricks to make glowing walls with more texture than plain blocks. The light catches along every seam.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cherenkov Bricks Slab, Cherenkov Bricks Stairs, Cherenkov Bricks Wall.

A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming. Rows of them along a corridor make it feel like walking beneath a reactor pool.
pages.title: Cherenkov Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Pillars of Cherenkov quartz gave the labs a sense of structure and a little light. They were easy to cut and look better than they have any right to.
A stony meteorite: rock that has not melted since the planets formed. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Chondrite

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
The housing of a column oven, keeping every metre of column at one temperature.
pages.title: Chromatography Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other. Yellow and black on dull metal; a language every lab in every universe seems to share.
pages.title: Chronosteel Hazard Panel

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)After walking into a running time field once, I started marking hazards. Chronosteel panels with stripes were the clearest way to say keep out.

A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room. Its bands are spaced at regular intervals, like the ticks on a clock face.
pages.title: Chronosteel Pillar

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Chronosteel pillars were stronger than I needed and looked better than stone. I used them to frame machine halls. They also make a reliable time reference.

Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look. Rivets mark each corner, set in perfectly even rows.
pages.title: Chronosteel Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had spare chronosteel, so I plated walls with it. The blurred reflections are a side effect of the metal's own clock and I have grown fond of them.
$(thing)Used in$(): Chronosteel Plating Slab, Chronosteel Plating Stairs.

A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still. The slats never collect dust, though I have never cleaned them.
pages.title: Chronosteel Vent

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Labs full of machines get stuffy. Chronosteel vents were the obvious fix, and they look the part. The slats were angled by trial and error until the hum of the machines dropped.
Casing for a climate engine. Earth's climate balances about 340 W/m² of incoming sunlight against heat radiated back to space.
pages.title: Climate Engine Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room. Walking past it, the room behind seems to shift a little too smoothly, like a painted backdrop.
pages.title: Metamaterial Cloaking Glass

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Metamaterials can steer light around an object. I built them into glass to see if I could make a window that vanished, and it nearly did.
A thin glass cell of fine grains in water. Unseen molecules jostle them endlessly; in 1908 Perrin watched that jitter and counted the atoms in a mole.
pages.title: Colloid Cell

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch. The traces brighten when someone stands close, then fade once they walk away, as though the panel had finished noticing them.
pages.title: Computronium Panel
