pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Computronium walls were too warm as solid blocks. Thin panels gave me the look of a working computer without heating the room.

Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it. Patterns chase each other across the joints between tiles, too fast to follow, and settle into stillness when the room empties.
pages.title: Computronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I tiled a floor with computronium offcuts. It flickers gently underfoot, and I am almost sure it is only decorative. It has never miscounted anything.
$(thing)Used in$(): Computronium Tiles Slab, Computronium Tiles Stairs.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 1 and 48. Gives Magnetite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Core Magnetite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing. Running a hand over it feels like touching cold glass, and the lights inside never quite stay still.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Plating

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Plating walls with cosmic neutronium was extravagant, but the effect was worth it. It is the closest thing to a sky I have indoors.

Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid. The tiny lights drift very slowly if I watch them long enough, like stars wheeling over a night.
pages.title: Cosmic Neutronium Tiles

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I had offcuts of cosmic neutronium and laid them as tiles. The faint lights inside them were a surprise, and I left them as they were.
$(thing)Used in$(): Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Slab, Cosmic Neutronium Tiles Stairs.
Alloy steel round a furnace where oil spends half a second at eight hundred degrees.
pages.title: Cracker Casing

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
$(thing)Cryolava Slug$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Cryolava Rock, Organic Evaporite.
pages.title: Cryolava Slug

pages.text: The iron return path of a cyclotron magnet. It carries the flux back from pole to pole, so the field across the gap stays strong and even.
pages.title: Cyclotron Yoke

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Deepslate Pitchblende Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld's deepslate (mine it for its drop).

End stone cracked around knots of matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into the lowest states quantum mechanics permits. Pauli exclusion holds it up, not chemistry. The block is far heavier than it looks, and the pick rings against it.
pages.title: Degenerate Matter Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the End, where dead stars seem to have been scattered, a pickaxe bounced off a seam of end stone that was much too heavy. Under the crust was matter pressed into degeneracy, like a fragment of a white dwarf.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the End (mine it for its drop).
The tall frame over a well that carries the crown block and the whole string of pipe. The word comes from Derrick, a seventeenth-century Tyburn hangman.
pages.title: Derrick Frame

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Deep Borehole Surface chests.

In string theory, the dilaton is a field whose value sets the string coupling: how readily strings split and join. This crystal froze one value of it. Hold it up to the light and everything behind it looks slightly more or less substantial.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Dilaton Ore in the Bulk (Graviton Reef).
pages.title: Dilaton Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I found these growing on the Graviton Reefs of the Bulk and inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Their facets responded to string interactions, and I realised they had frozen the dilaton field in place.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Dilaton Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Singularity, String Coupling Crystal.

Pale, oddly variable mineral whose hardness seems to drift as I handle it. The dilaton is the scalar field in string theory that sets the coupling strength of strings; here it is pinned into crystal, and wherever it sits the rules of interaction loosen or tighten slightly.
pages.title: Dilaton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the bulk stone a seam kept changing how hard my tools struck it. Plotting the variance against depth, I realised the local string coupling was shifting, a frozen dilaton field showing through the rock.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

Scorched nuggets blown out of a white hole. They are rich in elements that should not exist together, flung up from a region that admits no entry. The surfaces are glassy from the violence of their exit.
pages.title: Ejecta Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)The ejecta rock is peppered with dense, blistered lumps. I first took them for meteorites until I traced their trajectories back to a point nothing can enter.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Platonic Realm, between Y 876 and 1044. Gives Epsilon Dust when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Epsilon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Platonic Realm, between Y 318 and 400. Gives Euclidean Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Euclidean Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
$(thing)Euclid's Automaton$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Euclidean Shard, Golden Ratio Glass.
pages.title: Euclid's Automaton

pages.text: Found in Titan, between Y 30 and 200. Gives Organic Evaporite when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Evaporite Deposit

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Creation from nothing, made a machine. It does not convert energy; it simply has it: it gives unlimited FE to every block beside it, and charges the items of every player within 16 blocks.
pages.title: Ex Nihilo Engine

pages.text: A tall brick chimney. The hot gas inside is lighter than the air outside, so the taller the stack, the harder it draws.
pages.title: Exhaust Stack

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Fission Fragment Mix when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Fission Fragment Seam

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

A pocket of space sitting in a higher-energy vacuum than its surroundings, metastable and patient. If it tunnels down to the true vacuum it will expand at nearly light speed and rewrite everything it touches. The surface ripples softly, waiting for an excuse.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Quantum Foam.
pages.title: False Vacuum Bubble

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Drifting through the quantum foam, I noticed bubbles whose interior energy did not match the vacuum outside. Coleman's false vacuum, right there. I have learned to give them a very wide berth.
$(thing)Fourier Wisp$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Epsilon Dust, Fourier Series.
pages.title: Fourier Wisp

pages.text: Photons that fell toward a horizon and appear to have stopped. To any outside observer, their final moments are stretched forever, so the ore glows a deep, slow red that never fades. It is not hot, merely luminous and patient.
pages.title: Frozen Light Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Seen from far away, anything falling into a black hole freezes at the horizon. In infall rock I found veins of that frozen light, caught at the instant it crossed and preserved there indefinitely.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Platonic Realm, between Y 556 and 722. Gives Geodesic Thread when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Geodesic Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
A precision turntable that sets sample and detector at exact angles. The detector swings twice as far as the crystal, keeping θ and 2θ in step.
pages.title: Goniometer

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

The heart of a Graviton Wisp: a closed loop of string vibrating in the mode that makes a graviton. Even out of the Wisp, it pulls gently on everything nearby. It is light, but holding it gives a faint sensation of falling toward it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): dropped by the Graviton Wisp (the Bulk (Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Graviton Wisp Core

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Graviton Wisps drift through the Bulk, and when one dissipated it left this behind. I found more in the Calabi-Yau Knot, still faintly attracting dust.

Made in $(item)Graviton Condenser$().$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Graviton Wisp.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Graviton Crystal.
A small creature forever evaporating. Like a black hole, the smaller it gets the hotter it glows and the faster it radiates itself away.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Hawking Quanta.
pages.title: Hawking Imp

pages.text: A mirror that tracks the Sun on two axes. At Odeillo, sixty-three of them feed one parabolic concentrator whose focus passes 3,000 °C.
pages.title: Heliostat

pages.text: Made in a crafting grid.

An ender pearl wrapped in bulk stone and cosmic neutronium and charged by a nether star. Thrown, an ordinary pearl takes you somewhere; this one would take you everywhere. It shimmers and is never quite in the place it appears to be.
pages.title: Hyperdimensional Pearl

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ender pearls teleport through some hidden dimension. Wrapping one in bulk stone gave it access to all of them, and a nether star kept it from scattering on the Extreme Assembly Table.
Made in $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Omniscience Catalyst.

Spheres in four dimensions leave odd traces when they intersect our three. This ore shows them as nested balls that swell and shrink as I turn the lump. It has no corners anywhere and rolls slightly uphill.
pages.title: Hyperspherical Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Slicing a 4-sphere with a 3-dimensional plane gives a growing then shrinking ball. In the ordinal stone I found ore whose cross-sections did exactly that as I rotated it. Something four-dimensional was buried here.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).

$(thing)Ice Eel$(): A long dark eel with lights down its sides, hunting grazers, and biting whoever comes too close. Three meals and it spawns another; a day with none and it starves. The predator of Titan's hidden ocean. Found in Titan's hidden ocean.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Eel Photophore, Vent Biofilm.
pages.title: Ice Eel

pages.text: Rock shattered and welded back together in the instant of an impact. It lines a meteorite crater's bowl and rim.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Impact Breccia

pages.text: The floor of the Planetary Interior: the edge of the solid inner core, 5,150 km down. Iron here is crystallised under 330 GPa and about 5,400 C, as hot as the Sun's surface, yet solid because the pressure will not let it melt. No tool breaks it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior.
pages.title: Inner Core Boundary

pages.text: The iron-nickel mass of a meteorite, half buried where it struck. Found in craters out in open country.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Meteorite Crater structures in the Overworld.
pages.title: Iron Meteorite

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Kaluza and Klein noticed that general relativity in five dimensions, with one dimension curled up small, produces electromagnetism for free. Momentum around that hidden circle appears as electric charge. The shard has a faint static charge and seems to hum slightly when spun.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Kaluza-Klein Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef); dropped by the Brane Strider (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes, Graviton Reef)).
pages.title: Kaluza-Klein Shard

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I first found these in the Bulk, among Brane Strider remains and derelict stations. Running bulk stone through Maxwell's Demon Sorter with helium, I could separate grains with momentum in the fifth dimension.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Kaluza-Klein Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Brane Strider.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Compactification Lathe, Compactified Circle, Dimensional Singularity.

Bricks of lead shielding. Lead is dense and has many electrons, so it stops gamma rays well, about half of them every 1.3 cm, but it does little against neutrons. Shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.
pages.title: Lead Bricks

pages.text: Lead shielding striped yellow and black to mark a radiation area. It shields as well as the Lead Shielding Block.
pages.title: Lead Hazard Panel

pages.text: Nearly invisible: it is seen only by how it bends the light behind it into arcs and rings, the way unseen dark matter betrays itself to telescopes.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Einstein Ring Lens.
pages.title: Lens Phantom

pages.text: $(thing)Macrophage$(): The big eater: a slow cell that engulfs whatever it catches and digests it. Caught, you are held inside and dissolved until you strike your way out; items and red cells it simply eats (and gives the items back when it dies). It goes for the Tumour Hydra too, as macrophages go for a real tumour. Found in Inner Space's Tissue and Bloodstream.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Matrix Fibre, Lipid Bilayer.
pages.title: Macrophage

pages.text: Bricks of magnetite (Fe3O4), the most magnetic mineral in nature. Iron oxide is dense, so it also shields: it stops gamma rays about two thirds as well as lead, and neutrons three times better.
pages.title: Magnetite Bricks

pages.text: A hole bored through bedrock by the Core Drill. Step into it and you fall to the Planetary Interior; on arrival a second breach opens in the floor beside you, and stepping into that one brings you back up. It cannot be broken or moved.
pages.title: Mantle Breach

pages.text: $(thing)Moduli Crawler$(). Lives in: Moduli Wastes, The Bulk.$(br)Drops: Moduli Crystal, Void Lattice Shard.
pages.title: Moduli Crawler

pages.text: The extra dimensions of string theory have shapes and sizes set by fields called moduli. This crystal is those parameters frozen solid: a record of exactly how the hidden dimensions are curled. It changes shape slightly depending on the angle you view it from.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Moduli Ore in the Bulk (Moduli Wastes); dropped by the Moduli Crawler (the Bulk (Moduli Wastes)).
pages.title: Moduli Crystal

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Moduli Crawlers in the Moduli Wastes of the Bulk dropped these, and more lay inside the Calabi-Yau Knot. Measuring their facets, I found they recorded the shape and size of the compact dimensions.

Made in $(item)Maxwell's Demon Sorter$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Moduli Ore$(), in veins through the Bulk.$(br2)$(thing)Dropped by$(): Moduli Crawler.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Calabi Yau Knot chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Brane Cosmology.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Dimensional Residue, Dimensional Singularity, G₂ Manifold.

Each crystal here is a snapshot of one possible shape for the hidden dimensions. Moduli are the dials that describe the size and shape of compactified space, and this ore holds those dials fixed in mineral form. Different veins, different geometries, all perfectly valid.
pages.title: Moduli Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)String theory admits an enormous landscape of vacua, each set by its moduli. Mining the bulk, I noticed no two lumps of this ore refract light the same way. Each one has settled into a different vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).

Neutronium rolled into flat plates and riveted onto a block face. It is grey, dense and almost reflective, with seams that look as though they were drawn with a ruler. It gives a lab the look of a reactor vault.
pages.title: Neutronium Plating

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Neutronium, Neutronium Plating Slab, Neutronium Plating Stairs, Neutronium Plating Wall.

Host rock of the Natural Reactor, modelled on Oklo in Gabon, where two billion years ago groundwater slowed neutrons enough for uranium ore to run as a fission reactor for hundreds of thousands of years. It is still slightly radioactive.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor), Oklo Reactor Ruin structures in the Planetary Interior (Natural Reactor).
pages.title: Oklo Rock

pages.text: Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 36 and 126. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Oklo Uraninite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

Ore whose crystals arrive in sequence: each one has a definite successor, and even infinite chains of them have a limit crystal waiting beyond. Breaking a lump never disturbs the order of what remains.
pages.title: Ordinal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)In the ordinal stone I found a vein where crystals grew in strict succession, with a larger one capping every infinite run. Von Neumann's construction of the ordinals, rendered in mineral.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Transfinite Hierarchy (mine it for its drop).
$(thing)The Ouroboros$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Kekule Ring, Tholin.
pages.title: The Ouroboros

pages.text: $(thing)Paradox Shade$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tautology Shard, Proof Certificate.
pages.title: Paradox Shade

pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y 0 and 48. Gives Raw Pitchblende when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Pitchblende Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

$(thing)Polymerase$(): An enzyme that works the double helix: it walks to the nearest one, climbs it rung by rung reading the strand and laying down a copy behind it, turns at the top and works back down. Knocked off, it climbs back on. Harmless. Found in the Nucleus of Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Nucleotide, Messenger RNA.
pages.title: Polymerase

pages.text: A spinning wisp that flashes on a perfect beat, like the lighthouse beam of a pulsar. Millisecond pulsars keep time nearly as well as atomic clocks.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Pulsar Timing Crystal, Cosmic Ray Shard.
pages.title: Pulsar Wisp

pages.text: $(thing)Red Cell$(): A disc with a dimple in each face, packed with haemoglobin, carried round and round by the current. Climb on and it carries you too. Found in the Bloodstream of Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Porphyrin Oxygen Carrier, Iron Nugget.
pages.title: Red Cell

pages.text: Ore that knows when it is going to be mined. The vein grows brighter before my pick arrives, and splinters along lines that only make sense once the strike has happened. Holding it feels like being remembered.
pages.title: Retrocausal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)White holes run time backwards. Mining the ejecta rock, I noticed this ore cracking a moment before I struck it. The effect preceded the cause, and the cause still happened.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the white hole interior (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Copper Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Copper Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 12 and 96. Gives Rich Gold Chunk when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Gold Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 50 and 126. Gives Rich Iron Chunk when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Rich Iron Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
Found in the Planetary Interior, between Y 4 and 84. Gives Ringwoodite when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Ringwoodite Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).

A panel of spacetime alloy whose surface seems to bend inward slightly, as if the wall behind it were further away than it is. It is cool, smooth and very faintly disorienting to look at for long. Its edges line up neatly in rows.
pages.title: Spacetime Panel

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Block of Spacetime Alloy.

Ice VI, squeezed by the weight of a hundred kilometres of ice above it into a form denser than liquid water. Below it lies Titan's hidden ocean of ammonia water. Nothing yet made can drill through it. Found at the bottom of Titan.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in Titan.
pages.title: Subsurface Seal

pages.text: $(thing)T Cell$(): A killer lymphocyte on patrol. It leaves you alone, unless you carry an infection: then you glow in the Lymph Node and it hunts you down. It hunts the anomalies that infect, and the Tumour Hydra, too. Found in the Lymph Node of Inner Space.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Memory Cell, Antibody.
pages.title: T Cell

pages.text: Found in the Platonic Realm, between Y -724 and -648. Gives Tautology Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
pages.title: Tautology Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Found$(): in veins through the rock (mine it for its drop).
$(thing)Tessellate$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Geodesic Thread, Symmetry Crystal.
pages.title: Tessellate

pages.text: $(thing)Tholin Drifter$().$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tholin, Tholin Sand.
pages.title: Tholin Drifter

pages.text: A seam of metal pulled thin by gravity gradients. One end of every grain feels a stronger pull than the other, and the ore is threaded with stretch marks. It flexes slightly in the hand, as if still being tugged.
pages.title: Tidal Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Tidal forces are the difference in gravity across an object. Deep in infall rock I found metal that had been stretched rather than crushed, and recognised the signature of a nearby singularity.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the black hole interior (mine it for its drop).

A creature of the tide near a compact mass, where feet are pulled harder than head. It draws everything near it out long and thin, like spaghetti.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Tidal Shear Crystal, Accretion Disk Fragment.
pages.title: Tidal Stretcher

pages.text: $(thing)Vent Crab$(): A yeti crab: pale, hairy-clawed, walking the floor round the vents and waving its claws to feed the bacteria it farms on them. Harmless, unless struck. Near a vent long enough, it broods another. Found round the vents of Titan's hidden ocean.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Crab Chitin, Vent Biofilm.
pages.title: Vent Crab

pages.text: $(thing)Vent Grazer$(): A pale shrimp that circles the hydrothermal chimneys, grazing the bacteria on them. Well fed, it splits off another; it flees any eel. The prey of Titan's hidden ocean. Found in Titan's hidden ocean, round its vents.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Vent Biofilm.
pages.title: Vent Grazer

pages.text: A vein where gravity itself fizzes. The quanta of the gravitational field appear and vanish here so densely that the ore feels slightly heavier one moment and lighter the next. Nearby dust drifts in slow, uneven arcs.
pages.title: Ephemeral Graviton Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)No detector has ever caught a single graviton. Picking through foam substrate, I found a seam where my plumb line twitched in rhythm with bursts of vacuum noise. Borrowed gravitons, pinned in stone.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

A vein that points only one way. Each fleck carries a lone magnetic pole, north without south or the reverse, which classical electromagnetism forbids. A compass held close swings and holds, refusing to recover.
pages.title: Ephemeral Monopole Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dirac showed one monopole anywhere would explain why charge is quantised. In foam substrate my compass locked onto a single seam and would not let go: monopole pairs, flickering up from the vacuum.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Glints of light that do not come from anywhere. Virtual photons, the messengers that carry the electromagnetic force, wink in and out of this vein, so the ore glows without a source. It is cool to the touch despite the sparkle.
pages.title: Ephemeral Photon Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Every electric force is an exchange of virtual photons. Working in foam substrate I saw a seam lit from within, though nothing nearby could be lighting it. The vacuum was lending light and briefly forgetting to take it back.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Quantum Foam (mine it for its drop).

Void lattice cut into bricks; rigid blocks of nothing stacked with careful joints. The wall looks like a pattern of very clean holes in the world. Each brick has crisp, flawless edges, and the joints between them are the only part that looks like ordinary matter. Torchlight seems to fall into them.
pages.title: Void Lattice Bricks

pages.text: Made in a $(item)Stonecutter$().$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Void Lattice Block, Void Lattice Bricks Slab, Void Lattice Bricks Stairs, Void Lattice Bricks Wall.

Bulk stone holding pockets of a crystal made of nothing; a lattice of empty sites that remains rigid even though there is nothing in them. It looks like a gap in the rock that has decided to be solid.
pages.title: Void Lattice Ore

pages.text: $(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Mining in the Bulk, I hit a patch of rock that the pick went through as though it were air but that still dropped something. The lattice was a crystal of vacancies, ordered without anything to order.
$(thing)Found$(): in veins through the Bulk (mine it for its drop).
Survey notes. $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() grows deep in the deepslate layer. $(item)Degenerate Matter$() is found in End stone; smelt or blast it into $(item)Neutronium$().

$(item)Void Lattice$() only forms in the Bulk.$(br2)Names explained: Cherenkov light is the blue glow of particles outrunning light in a medium. Degenerate matter is what remains when atoms are crushed until only quantum exclusion holds them up, as in white dwarfs and neutron stars.
Glows with the blue light of particles outrunning light in a medium.$(br2)Made in $(item)Galton Board$().$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): mined from Deepslate Cherenkov Quartz Ore in the Overworld.
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Cherenkov Quartz$(): Atomic Clock, Block of Cherenkov Quartz, Casimir Plate, Casimir Vacuum Press, Chemical Reactor and more

Out past the edge of the sky, round a black hole feeding on a disk of its own fire, islands of rock and ice drift in the dark. The $(thing)Accretion Frontier$() is reached with a $(item)Light Sail$() (research $(thing)Galactic Dynamics$()): climb to y 200 or higher, stand under open sky, and unfurl it. Unfurled again in the Frontier, it brings you home and slows your fall.

It has five regions. The $(thing)Molecular Cloud Nebula$(), cold ice and dust where stars are born: you cannot see far. The $(thing)Asteroid Belt$(), where you weigh almost nothing, and $(thing)micrometeorites$() strike anyone not wearing a $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter stopped per piece; a full set stops all).

The $(thing)Pulsar Field$(): crust of neutron-star iron, and a pulse of radiation every five seconds, on the beat, for anyone under open sky. Gravity is high and time runs slow (Time Dilation). The $(thing)Accretion Rim$(): slag lakes of disk plasma; it is hot enough to burn, and the disk's tidal pull stretches you. The $(thing)Lensing Void$(): black glass, sight lines bent, and frame-dragging currents that push you sideways.

Its ores: $(item)Interstellar Dust$() in the nebula's ice, $(item)Exoplanet Core Samples$() and $(item)Brown Dwarf Cores$() in the asteroids, $(item)Magnetar Crust$(), $(item)Pulsar Timing Crystals$() and $(item)Cosmic Ray Shards$() in the pulsar crust, $(item)Accretion Disk Fragments$() in the slag, and $(item)Einstein Ring Lenses$() in the void glass. Derelict Stations drift between the islands; Pulsar Beacons stand on the field.

Each of the Frontier's creatures acts out its physics. The $(thing)Nebuloid$() is a drifting knot of gas and dust; inside it you are blind. The $(thing)Pulsar Wisp$() pulses on an exact beat, once every one and a half seconds, and its pulse hurts and irradiates anyone it can see within ten blocks; dodge behind something between pulses.

The $(thing)Tidal Stretcher$() pulls you in harder the closer you are (a tidal force grows as 1/r³) and stretches what it grabs. The $(thing)Lens Phantom$() is never where it appears: its light reaches you bent round the void's mass, so its image stands a block or two from its body. Aim beside it.

The $(thing)Hawking Imp$() is a tiny black hole. It evaporates, and the smaller it gets the hotter and faster it burns (T ∝ 1/M), until it pops. The $(thing)Boltzmann Brain$() fluctuates out of nothing, mutters, and is gone within half a minute unless caught.

$(thing)The Binary$(): play a Binary Black Hole Merger record, or a Gravitational Wave Echo, in the Frontier and two compact stars spiral out of the dark. Their gravitational waves carry off their orbit: they close in (da/dt ∝ −1/a³) and circle ever faster. Kill both before they meet, if they merge, the shockwave hits everything nearby, and nothing is left to loot.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Accretion Disk Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim's slag.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Accretion Disk Fragments.

$(item)Asteroid Rock$(). The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Asteroid Belt).
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph sorts four into two Meteoric Iron and a Chondrite Fragment.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Brown Dwarf Core when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Brown Dwarf Cores (also made in the Tectonic Press, from dust and cloud gas).
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Cosmic Ray Shard when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Cosmic Ray Shards (also made by the Interstellar Scoop, from glass left high up).
$(item)Dust Cloud$(). A cloud of dust grains, too thin to stand on. Now and then, broken, it leaves Interstellar Dust.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Breaks into Interstellar Dust, sometimes.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Interstellar Dust when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Interstellar Dust.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Einstein Ring Lens when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void's glass.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Einstein Ring Lenses.

$(item)Frontier Regolith$(). Rock ground to dust by billions of years of micrometeorites. Assayed in bulk it gives back its interstellar dust and a little rare earth.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The top of every island of the Accretion Frontier (except the Lensing Void).$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The Spectrograph assays eight into four Interstellar Dust and a Rare Earth Oxide.
$(item)Hydrogen Cloud$(). Ionised hydrogen glowing red at 656 nm, the H-alpha line. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Magnetar Crust Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Magnetar Crust Fragments.

$(item)Nebular Ice$(). Water, carbon monoxide and ammonia frozen together on dust grains at about fifteen kelvin. Starlight slowly builds larger molecules within it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Molecular Cloud Nebula).
$(thing)Found$(): Patches in the Molecular Cloud Nebula, among its clouds.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two sublimate into 250 mB of Molecular Cloud in the Electrolytic Cell.
$(item)Oxygen Cloud$(). Doubly ionised oxygen glowing green-blue at 501 nm. You can walk straight through it.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier.
$(thing)Found$(): The Molecular Cloud Nebula: you can pass through it.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Light: it glows. Its gases will be gathered in a later expansion.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Exoplanet Core Sample when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Asteroid Belt's rock.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Exoplanet Core Samples (also made in the Hypervelocity Impact Forge).
$(item)Protostar Fragment$(). Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Protostellar Ember when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): Inside the Nebula's ice.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives a Protostellar Ember: thermoelectric fuel that burns for a long time, or feed for the Accretion Disk Reactor.

$(item)Pulsar Crust$(). Iron from a neutron star's crust: a lattice of nuclei in a sea of electrons, held under a field of some hundred million tesla.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Pulsar Field).
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Two with two Iron-Nickel become a Magnetar Crust Fragment in the Pulsed Magnet Lab, at 80 T.
Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Pulsar Timing Crystal when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): The Pulsar Field's crust.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Gives Pulsar Timing Crystals.

$(item)Rim Slag$(). Cinder flung from the inner edge of an accretion disk, where gas spirals in at a fair fraction of light speed and is heated to millions of degrees.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Accretion Rim).
$(thing)Found$(): The Accretion Rim, round its plasma lakes.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Quenched with Accretion Disk Plasma in the Tectonic Press: Accretion Disk Fragments.
$(item)Station Hull$(). Aluminium skin and stringers from a spacecraft, thin enough to dent by hand. In vacuum, a few millimetres of it is all that separates air from nothing.
$(thing)Found$(): Derelict Stations drifting in the Frontier; or crafted from iron.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): The body of the Whipple Shield and the Frontier Suit.

$(item)Void Glass$(). Glass as dark as the space it came from. Gravity bends light as a lens does, and a well-aligned mass draws a background source into a full Einstein ring.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Accretion Frontier (Lensing Void).
$(thing)Found$(): The Lensing Void.$(br2)$(thing)Used$(): Four with Fused Silica make an Einstein Ring Lens in the Optical Workshop.
Every region of the Accretion Frontier has its hazard, and each has an answer.

$(li)$(thing)Nebula$(), blinding dust: the $(item)Adaptive Optics Visor$().$(li)$(thing)Asteroid Belt$(), micrometeorites: the $(item)Whipple Shield$() (a quarter per piece); low gravity: $(item)Gravity Compensators$().$(li)$(thing)Pulsar Field$(), its radiation pulse: $(item)Radiation Plating$() on your armour; high gravity: Gravity Compensators; Time Dilation: an $(item)Atomic Clock$() in the off hand.

$(li)$(thing)Accretion Rim$(), heat: the $(item)Thermal Shroud$() (or a full Refractory Suit); its tidal pull: the $(item)Tidal Brace$() (or a Precision Gyroscope in the off hand).$(li)$(thing)Lensing Void$(), frame dragging: a $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() in the off hand; warped sight: the Adaptive Optics Visor.

The four pieces of the $(item)Frontier Suit$() are made of Station Hull, each round a piece of the region it answers: an Einstein Ring Lens, an Accretion Disk Fragment, a Tidal Shear Crystal and a Planetary Core Sample (the reference mass the boots weigh gravity against).

Saturn's largest moon is the only other world we know with rain, rivers, lakes and seas on its surface, of methane, at 94 K, under an air half again as thick as Earth's. Reach it with a $(item)Cryogenic Lander$() (research $(thing)Titan$()): stand under open sky in the Overworld and use it. Used again on Titan, it lifts off and brings you home under its parachute.

It has six regions. $(thing)Kraken Mare$(), a sea of liquid methane over a floor of tholin sand. The $(thing)Shangri-La Dunes$(), tholin piled by the wind. The $(thing)Xanadu Uplands$(), bare water-ice bedrock. The $(thing)Ontario Lacus Basin$(), lakes and the bright crust of lakes that have dried up. The $(thing)Sotra Cryovolcanic Field$(), where cryolava, ammonia and water, wells up from below. And $(thing)Selk$(), a plain pocked with impact craters, each a bowl with a raised rim, the big ones with a peak in the middle.

Under everything lies the $(item)Subsurface Seal$(): ice VI, crushed denser than water by the ice above it. Titan's hidden ocean is beneath it, and nothing yet made can get through. Falling out of the bottom of Titan sends you home.

Titan's rock is $(item)Water-Ice Bedrock$(): electrolysed, it gives $(fluid)Oxygen$(). $(item)Tholin Sand$() gives up its $(item)Tholin$() to methanol in the Chemical Reactor, and tholin boiled with water gives $(item)Amino Acids$(); the haze makes the building blocks of life out of methane and sunlight. The haze is so thick that from the ground you cannot see Saturn at all.

$(thing)Cold$(): at 94 K you freeze as in powder snow, then take frost damage. Each piece of a $(item)Heated Pressure Suit$() (a Pressure Suit crafted with two Silica Aerogel and redstone heating wire) keeps out a quarter of it; a full suit, all of it. It is still a pressure suit underneath.

$(thing)Rain$(): out under the sky in a storm, methane rain soaks through a suit's aerogel and chills you as much again. Use a $(item)Hydrophobic Coating$() while wearing armour to coat each piece (one can a piece): each coated piece sheds a quarter of the soaking. Methane wets almost everything; the coating is fluorinated so that it does not.

$(thing)Air$(): Titan's air is nitrogen and methane, and your breath runs out as if you were under water. An $(item)Oxygen Rebreather$() anywhere in your inventory holds twenty minutes of oxygen and spends it a second at a time, even in a lake. Craft a spent one with an Oxygen Gas Cell to refill it.

$(thing)No fire$(): nothing burns without oxygen. Flint and steel and fire charges fail, and anything burning goes out. $(thing)Low gravity$(): a seventh of Earth's; you fall slowly, land softly and jump higher. Liquid methane is less than half as dense as water and too thin to swim in: you sink, and it is 94 K.

In 1865 Kekule dreamt of a snake seizing its own tail, and woke knowing the shape of benzene: a ring of six carbons. Use $(item)Kekule's Dream$() in Titan's $(thing)Selk Crater$() and a serpent of six segments rises, its tail in its mouth.

It is $(thing)aromatic$(): while the ring is closed, its electrons belong to the whole ring, and every blow is shared round all six bonds; it takes a quarter of the damage. Every twenty seconds it lets go of its tail for five (its eyes turn red and its bar goes red): then it takes double damage, but its head lunges at you. Closed, it spits tholin at everyone it can see.

At half health two Catalyst Sprites come to it, and they heal it as they heal everything of Titan: kill them first. It leaves a $(item)Kekule Ring$() and a pile of tholin. The ring never wears: held in a Polymeriser's catalyst slot, it turns Organic Evaporite and ammonia straight into $(item)Aramid Fibre$() (Kevlar is a ring of six carbons, repeated). Kekule's Dream can be crafted again from tholin, evaporites and amino acids, so the Ouroboros can always be called again.

Nothing on Titan is alive the way we are, but its chemistry moves. The $(thing)Tholin Drifter$() is a flake of the haze, carried on the slow wind (which turns with the day). Whoever it settles on is coated in tar: darkness, and heavy steps. It drops Tholin.

The $(thing)Catalyst Sprite$() is a speck of bare metal surface, and a catalyst speeds what is near it: it keeps five blocks off, and every three seconds spends half a minute of the oxygen in your rebreather and heals Titan's other creatures. Hurt, it keeps its distance. It sometimes drops a Nickel Catalyst.

The $(thing)Methane Skater$() stands on liquid methane as a pond skater does on water, skates straight out to whoever is on the shore and knocks them in. Its legs are coated against the methane: it can drop a Hydrophobic Coating. The $(thing)Cryolava Slug$() crawls the Sotra field, armoured and slow; it freezes what it touches and spits cryolava from twelve blocks.

Ruins: $(thing)Abandoned Refineries$() by the basin and the sea, $(thing)Lander Wrecks$() in the dunes and uplands, and $(thing)Cryolabs$() on the cryovolcanic plain. Each has a cache; a Cryolab's may hold Kekule's Dream.

High above the Platonic Realm's own islands (the Number Line), across a gap of empty air, and far below Curved Space lies the $(thing)Elements$(): islands of $(item)Euclidean Marble$() from Y 320 to 400, laid out as if with compass and straightedge.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.
In the Realm, sneak and use the $(item)Platonic Compass$() to climb a layer (sneak and look down to go down one). This is the safe layer: none of the Realm's hunters come up here.

$(thing)Compass Towers$() rise fourteen to twenty-five blocks and carry a circle and the hexagon stepped round it with the same opening (Book IV, Proposition 15). $(thing)Geometer's Ruins$() have Euclid's proof of Pythagoras inlaid in the floor: squares of 144 and 256 on the legs of a right triangle (12 and 16 long), and one of 400 on its long side (20). A cache waits at the right angle. The Platonic solids float here too, in marble.

$(item)Euclid's Automaton$() walks only in straight lines and turns on the spot through angles it can construct. Now and then it makes a construction the way surveyors always have: it drives a pin into the ground, walks once round it with the cord taut (a circle), then walks the six sides of the hexagon inside it, each as long as the cord, its straightedge on the ground. The lines glow for half a minute. Leave it to its work: it fights only whoever hurts it. Struck, it rouses: its eyes burn red and follow you, and steam pours from its shoulders.

$(item)Euclidean Ore$() gives $(item)Euclidean Shards$() (the Automaton drops them too). The Geometer's Table draws a stack of Golden Ratio Glass from plain glass and a single shard (or a bigger stack from eight glass and eight Euclidean Marble), and lays out eight marble from eight cobblestone and a shard; a shard mends a Platonic Compass at an anvil; and the later machines of Mathematics are built with them.
At the foot of the Realm, some 650 blocks below the Number Line, a broad plain of $(item)Postulate Slate$(): what every proof stands on.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.

$(thing)Liar's Vaults$() are sealed halls floored in light and dark, true and false, with two doors: one of them is only glass. $(thing)Proof Stairs$() wind up thirty to fifty steps round a pillar, each step standing on the one before it (induction). Both hold caches.

$(item)Paradox Shades$() are true, then false, then true again every few seconds. True, they are solid and hunt you; false, they are dark outlines that nothing can touch. Strike them while they are true.
$(thing)Contradiction$(): every half minute or so, two opposite effects at once (fast and slow, strong and weak). A $(item)Proof Certificate$() carried keeps you consistent.

$(item)Tautology Ore$() gives $(item)Tautology Shards$(). On the Formal Proof Assistant: two Proof Certificates from two shards and two paper; two Axiom Schemas from two shards, two lattices and a book; two Proof Fragments from 32 Postulate Slate and two shards; and eight Postulate Slate from eight cobblestone and a shard.

Above Curved Space and far below the Infinite, islands of $(item)Dense Stone$() in three bands, the same shapes at three sizes: between any two points, another.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.

$(thing)Fourier Harps$() are rows of 33 rods whose heights add up the first few harmonics of a square wave, overshoot and all. Near one you meet $(thing)Limits$(): the closer you get, the slower you go. You can reach it, but only just.
$(item)Fourier Wisps$() are chains of turning circles drawing a square wave in the air. They keep their distance.

$(item)Epsilon Ore$() gives $(item)Epsilon Dust$(). On the Analytic Continuator: two Real Continua from eight Rational Fields and four dust; four Infinitesimals from a Real Continuum and two dust; a Transcendental Crystal from 32 Dense Stone and four Rational Fields; and eight Dense Stone from eight cobblestone and a dust.
High above the Elements, islands of $(item)Hyperbolic Stone$(), warped like saddles: geometry where parallel lines spread apart.$(br2)$(thing)Found$(): in the Platonic Realm.

$(thing)Möbius Arches$() are broad bands with a half twist from one foot to the other. Walk through one and you come out $(thing)mirrored$(): left and right swapped for ten seconds. $(thing)Hyperbolic Floors$() are the Poincaré disc in stone, nearly forty blocks across, their tiles crowding ever smaller toward the rim.
$(item)Tessellates$() are creatures of hyperbolic tiles. Broken, each falls into two smaller ones, twice; only the smallest carry anything.

$(item)Geodesic Ore$() gives $(item)Geodesic Threads$(). On the Topology Kiln: a Differential Manifold from two threads and a Derivative Operator; a Möbius Strip from 16 Hyperbolic Stone and a Function Graph; and eight Hyperbolic Stone from eight cobblestone and a thread (fired as a surface with two handles, χ = −2).

The Platonic Realm is six layers, one for each part of mathematics, from Y −768 at the bottom to 1536 at the top. Between each layer and the next lies a wide gap of empty air, a hundred blocks and more: too far to climb, and too far to fall.

$(li)$(thing)The Infinite$() (Y 1280 to 1536): the Transfinite Hierarchy's strata, set theory.$(li)$(thing)The Continuum$() (islands at Y 880 to 1040): analysis.$(li)$(thing)Curved Space$() (Y 560 to 720): topology.$(li)$(thing)The Elements$() (Y 320 to 400): Euclid, the safe layer.$(li)$(thing)The Number Line$() (Y 10 to 194): the Realm's own islands.$(li)$(thing)The Axioms$() (Y −720 to −650): logic, far below the rest.

The $(item)Platonic Compass$() brings you to the Number Line. In the Realm, sneak and use it to climb one layer, or sneak, look down and use it to go down one; it lands you on the next layer's islands. It climbs no higher than the Continuum.

The widest gap of all, 240 blocks of nothing, lies under the $(thing)Infinite$(), and only the $(item)Cantor Key$() opens it: fly or climb up to it and you are turned back just below. From the Infinite, the Compass (sneaking, looking down) takes you back to the Continuum. Fall out of the bottom of the Axioms and you land in the Quantum Foam.

Each layer has its own stone, ore, landmarks, creature and music, and something it does to visitors (only ever an effect: nothing there changes a block). Each stone is also its field's raw feedstock, and each can be made again from cobblestone and a little of its layer's material, so building with it never runs out. Snow never settles here: the Realm is warm all the way up.

The $(thing)Macrophage$() is slow, but it engulfs whatever it catches. Caught, you are held inside it and digested: strike it to break free. It eats items and red cells too, and gives the items back when it dies.

The $(thing)T Cell$() leaves you alone unless you are infected, or strike it. It hunts the anomalies that infect as well. The $(thing)Polymerase$() climbs the Nucleus's double helices rung by rung, copying the strand, and harms no one. Macrophages and T Cells both go for the Tumour Hydra, and it bites them back: fight it beside them.

The $(thing)Tumour Hydra$(), called with a $(item)Metastatic Spore$() on open ground in the Tumour, starts with three heads. Strike a head or its neck: every 30 damage cuts that head off, and its stump, left in the same place, is open for five seconds. Seal it with fire, or strike it with a $(item)CAR-T Cell Culture$() or an $(item)Apoptosis Trigger$(), and the head is gone for good; leave it, and it grows back with another beside it. With no heads left, its body takes blows in full and it can be killed. Its bite carries $(thing)Metastasis$().

Landmarks with caches: $(thing)Germinal Centres$() in the Lymph Node, $(thing)Nuclear Pores$() in the Nucleus and $(thing)Ribosome Workshops$() in Tissue. In the Overworld, abandoned $(thing)BSL-4 Field Stations$() hold the branch's first samples: sterile packs and cultures.

A body, seen from the inside at the scale of its cells. Reach it with the $(item)Miniaturiser$() (research $(thing)Inner Space$(), after Circulation): use it in the Overworld and you shrink until a cell is the size of a house. Used again inside, it brings you back out. Falling out of the bottom brings you home too.

It has five regions. The $(thing)Bloodstream$(): seas and channels of $(fluid)Blood Plasma$(), whose current carries you along, and $(thing)Red Cells$() drifting in it that you can ride. $(thing)Tissue$(): walls of cells, the commonest region, where a fight sets off $(thing)inflammation$() (you slow, and the heat hurts). The $(thing)Lymph Node$(): if you carry an infection here you glow, and the $(thing)T Cells$() hunt you down.

The $(thing)Nucleus$(): chromatin, the double helix in spires, and $(thing)mutation$(): now and then one of your effects swaps for its opposite. The $(thing)Tumour$(): overgrown tissue where an anomaly has taken hold. Its oncogenic field weakens you more the longer you stay, and it is where the $(thing)Tumour Hydra$() is called.

Each region has its material, each useful and each renewable: $(fluid)Blood Plasma$() (the Lake Pump draws it from the Bloodstream; it makes broth and antibodies), $(item)Matrix Fibre$() (collagen seams in Tissue; a cheaper Grown Organ), $(item)Memory Cells$() (T Cells and Germinal Centres; antibodies from plasma), $(item)Nucleotides$() (the Nucleus; cheap Messenger RNA) and $(item)Tumour Specimens$() (the Tumour; a cheaper CAR-T Cell Culture).

Under Titan's Subsurface Seal lies an ocean of salty water, larger than all of Earth's. The $(item)Cryobot$() (research $(thing)Titan's Hidden Ocean$()) melts down into it: stand on the Seal at the bottom of Titan and use it. You come out just under the ice, with the probe's own air for half a minute. An $(item)Oxygen Rebreather$() keeps you breathing after that, and it is as cold as Titan above. Use the Cryobot again to climb back; sinking through the floor brings you up through the ice too.

The ocean is dark water between a $(item)Water-Ice$() ceiling, hung with $(item)Brinicles$(), and a floor of $(item)Abyssal Silicate$(). In the $(thing)Hydrothermal Vents$() mounds of rock rise into glowing chimneys, each crowned by a $(item)Black Smoker$(): water at 400 C pouring out black with sulfides, roaring and bubbling. Its plume lifts and scalds whoever swims into it. $(item)Giant Tube Worms$() ring the mounds, and spread by themselves near a smoker.

Its life, from the bottom of the food chain up: bacteria on the chimneys and in the worms; $(thing)Vent Crabs$() (yeti crabs that farm bacteria on their hairy claws, and brood near a vent) and $(thing)Vent Grazers$() feeding round the vents; $(thing)Brine Jellies$() drifting in open water, stinging what brushes their tentacles; and the $(thing)Ice Eels$() that hunt the grazers.

Its ecosystem is the first for the Ecosphere: $(thing)Vent Grazers$() feed on the chimneys' bacteria and, well fed, multiply; $(thing)Ice Eels$() hunt them, multiply after three meals, and starve after a day without one. So where eels are few the grazers boom, the eels follow, and their feast ends in famine: Lotka-Volterra, with no numbers written in.

Grazers drop $(item)Vent Biofilm$() (cheap Bacterial Cultures in the Fermenter), eels $(item)Eel Photophores$(), jellies $(item)Luminous Mesoglea$() and crabs $(item)Crab Chitin$() (polymer sheet). Together with algae, the $(item)Ecosphere$() builds Stable Ecosystems from them at half the old cost. Abyssal Silicate and water give hydrogen in the Chemical Reactor, as rock does at Earth's vents.

Found a crashed research observatory, its containment dome cracked, a supply cache still inside. They dot the Overworld. Who built them, I don't yet know.$(br2)A good source of early Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium; worth a detour before I can make either myself.

A cache the Transcendental keeps for itself, and the one you can build: 243 kinds of item, and up to $(thing)2,147,483,647$() of each. Whatever you put in joins the pile of the same item. Scroll to move through its 27 rows; a click or shift-click takes one normal stack at a time.
Pipes put into it and take out of it (one stack at a time). Broken, it keeps everything inside. It is made on the $(item)Extreme Assembly Table$().

A tumour is not one enemy but a population of competing clones, each with its own mutations and its own fitness f_i. A clone gains share only when it beats the average: dx_i/dt = x_i(f_i − Σx_j f_j). Every treatment changes the fitnesses, and so it selects whichever clones it happens not to kill.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Containment is not destruction: you must keep the anomaly alive to study it. A unit that makes new ones at rate β, and is cleared naturally (γ) or by quarantine (q), makes R_e = ∫β e^{−(γ+q)τ}dτ = β/(γ + q) in its life. Quarantine works by pushing R_e below 1, every outbreak then dies out, and the minimum field is q = β − γ.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Between hosts, an infection is bookkeeping. Split a population into susceptible S, infected I and recovered: dI/dt = βSI/N − (γ + μ)I. At the start everyone is susceptible, and the infection grows only if each case makes more than one more: $(thing)R₀ = β/(γ + μ) > 1$(). Once a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ is immune, it can no longer spread.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The body destroys anomalous cells all the time. A tumour exists because it escaped. $(thing)Immune evasion$(): it sheds the markers T cells look for, shows PD-L1 to switch them off, and recruits cells that suppress inflammation. $(thing)Immortality$(): every division shortens the telomeres at the chromosome ends until a cell must stop, unless it switches $(thing)telomerase$() back on.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

What can an anomaly do? The catalogue so far:$(li)break a symmetry and stay broken (defects)$(li)make itself from its surroundings (autocatalysis, prions)$(li)override the rules of its host (oncogenesis)$(li)defy prediction (chaos, undecidability)$(li)copy itself and escape (replicators, metastasis)$(li)evolve resistance$(li)spread through a population$(li)break a conservation law locally$(li)turn partner.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Every science keeps a drawer of things that should not happen. Physics has defects and law violations, chemistry has molecules that make themselves, biology has cancer, mathematics has monsters. $(thing)Abnormality & Infection$() studies them together, because they behave alike: they $(thing)arise$() from a broken rule, $(thing)replicate$(), $(thing)escape$() what should destroy them, and $(thing)change$() the normal world they live in.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In quantum field theory an $(thing)anomaly$() is a technical word: a symmetry that holds in the classical theory and fails in the quantum one. The chiral charge of massless fermions should be conserved; in parallel electric and magnetic fields it is created from the vacuum at the rate e²E·B/2π² per unit volume. This $(thing)anomaly$() is real; it makes the neutral pion decay into two photons, and it is measured in crystals today.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

anomaly/intro__anomaly_origin_autocataly.title: Origins II: Molecules That Copy Themselves

pages.text: In chemistry an anomaly begins as $(thing)autocatalysis$(): a product that speeds up its own making. Its concentration does not rise steadily but explodes, and with feedback it can oscillate, a chemical clock, or spread as a wave through a still dish. The classic model feeds A and B into dX/dt = A − (B + 1)X + X²Y; past B = 1 + A² the steady state breaks and the colours start to pulse.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

How does an anomaly begin in physics? With a choice. A field whose potential has two equal valleys must fall into one as the universe cools, and regions too far apart to agree fall into different ones. Where they meet, the field is stuck on the hill between: a $(thing)domain wall$(). With more dimensions of choice you get strings, monopoles and textures; $(thing)topological defects$(), which no smooth change can remove.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Cancer is the model anomaly: a part of the body that stops obeying the body. It is not one mistake but several. An $(thing)oncogene$() gets stuck on (RAS, MYC) and the cell is told to divide; a $(thing)tumour suppressor$() is lost, $(thing)p53$(), the guardian of the genome, which should stop a damaged cell or make it die, and nothing tells it to stop. Each mutation gives one clone an edge over its neighbours.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Mathematics breeds anomalies from perfectly good rules. In 1872 a sum of cosines, W(x) = Σaⁿcos(bⁿπx), turned out to be continuous everywhere and differentiable nowhere: a $(thing)monster$(), as Poincaré called such things. Its graph is a fractal of dimension 2 + ln a/ln b. Then came sets with no measure, space-filling curves, a sphere cut into a few pieces that reassemble into two.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The end of an anomaly is understanding it. Physics has done this before: infinities in quantum field theory looked like a disaster until $(thing)renormalisation$() showed they only meant the constants depend on the scale you measure at. A measured quantity G then obeys [μ∂/∂μ + β(g)∂/∂g + nγ]G = 0, and at a fixed point it scales as μ^{−nγ}: the anomaly is just an $(thing)anomalous dimension$(), a number in a deeper law.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A $(thing)quine$() is a program that prints its own source code. It needs two parts: a description of itself, and instructions to copy the description and build from it. Von Neumann found the same two parts in any machine that can build itself; years before DNA showed life does it that way. A computer virus, a gene and a $(thing)meme$() (an idea that spreads because it is good at spreading) are the same trick.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

An anomaly that lives inside a normal system is in a relationship with it. Write both as populations: dN₁/dt = r₁N₁(1 − (N₁ + αN₂)/K₁), and the mirror equation for N₂ with β. With α and β positive they compete; they coexist at N₁* = (K₁ − αK₂)/(1 − αβ) only if neither crowds the other out. Flip the sign of α and the invader helps its host instead.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

An anomaly is a system, not a cell. A tumour builds a $(thing)microenvironment$(): blood vessels, fibroblasts, a stiffened matrix, immune cells talked into helping. Signalling networks, growth factors, cytokines, feedback loops, decide which cells divide, move or die, and a mutation in one hub rewires them all.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Kill the anomaly, spare the normal. $(thing)CRISPR$() cuts DNA where a guide RNA matches, so it can write a trigger only the anomalous genome will read; restoring $(thing)apoptosis$(), the death a damaged cell was always meant to accept. $(thing)CAR-T$() cells are a patient's own T cells given a receptor for the anomaly's marker: living drugs that multiply as they find their target.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
An antiproton and a positron make $(item)antihydrogen$(), and its spectral lines sit exactly where hydrogen's do; measured to twelve decimal places, and still CPT holds.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Its creatures are made of antimatter like everything else there. $(thing)Annihilators$() are shells around a core of $(item)antihelium$(); $(thing)Positronium Skitterers$() eat antisilicon; $(thing)Antihydrogen Wisps$() drift over the sea and drop frozen antihydrogen.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Big Bang should have made matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion antibaryons there was one extra baryon, and everything we are is made of that one.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Notebook, antimatter. Swap every particle for its antiparticle (C), reflect the world in a mirror (P), and run the film backwards (T). Do all three at once and the laws of physics come out exactly the same: CPT symmetry, as solid as anything we know.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A metal that may never touch a crucible, a mould or the air. The $(item)Mirror Matter Foundry$() is a stack of Penning traps: the anti-ore floats, melts, refines and cools in fields alone.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Split light into its colours and it tells you what made it. A hot body glows brightest at a wavelength set by its temperature alone: $(thing)λ = b/T$(), with b = 2.898 mm·K. The Sun, at 5,778 K, peaks in green light.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Astronomy begins with gathering light. A $(item)Telescope Mirror Blank$(), glass, ground and silvered, collects a star's light over its whole face and brings it to one point. The wider the mirror, the fainter the stars it shows.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Everything falls the same way: a feather and a hammer land together on the Moon. That is the $(thing)equivalence principle$(), and a $(item)Proof Mass$(), shielded so that nothing but gravity touches it, follows free fall exactly.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Measure the Doppler shift of the hydrogen line along the Galaxy and you have how fast its gas circles at each distance from the centre. If the stars were all its mass, the speed would fall off far out, as the planets' does: v = √(GM/r).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Sometimes a $(thing)crater$() lies in open country: a bowl of $(item)Impact Breccia$() with a raised rim, and in the middle, half buried, what made it. An $(item)Iron Meteorite$() is the core of a small planet that shattered billions of years ago; a $(item)Chondrite$() is stone that has not melted since the planets formed.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Radio Telescope$() is a dish on an alt-azimuth mount with a $(item)Feed Horn$() at its focus. Radio passes through cloud and daylight: it works at any hour, rain or shine, but it needs a view of the sky, and every machine running within 24 blocks is $(thing)noise$() in its receiver.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

After the furnace at Odeillo in the Pyrenees: $(item)Heliostats$() turn with the Sun and throw its light onto a parabolic wall of $(item)Concentrator Mirrors$(), which brings it to a point on the $(item)Solar Receiver$(). It works only by day, under open sky and without rain.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Reflecting Telescope$() is a mirror under a dome. It works only at $(thing)night$(), with $(thing)open sky$() above its slit and no rain, and every plate it exposes teaches you something: each run gives $(thing)Insight$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Optics from the workshop make the Reflecting Telescope a better instrument. Each sits in it as a catalyst and is never used up.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Matter falling onto a black hole gives up energy as it spirals in; η of its rest energy, from 6% for a hole that does not spin to a third for one spinning at the limit. Fusion manages 0.7%.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Cepheid variables pulse with a period that gives their true brightness: the first rung of the distance ladder. A Spectrograph sets a $(item)Cepheid Standard Candle$() against a spectral plate: a $(item)Redshift Lens$(), every galaxy is receding, faster the farther.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A planet crossing its star blocks a fraction $(thing)δ = (r/R)²$() of its light: a Jupiter dims the Sun by one per cent, an Earth by one part in twelve thousand. The Reflecting Telescope records a $(item)Transit Light Curve$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Interstellar Scoop$() gathers what lies between the stars, but only where the air will not swamp it: at y 200 or above in the Overworld, or anywhere in the Accretion Frontier or the End. It gathers $(fluid)Molecular Cloud$() gas, $(fluid)Interstellar Medium$() (into glass bottles) and $(item)Interstellar Dust$() (onto paper).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A neutron-star merger heard by the Laser Interferometer can be found in the sky: point the telescope with its record and photograph the $(thing)kilonova$(); the glow of freshly made gold and platinum, peaking after days: $(item)Kilonova Ash$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The engines found in ruins pull creatures out of nothing at random. One you build yourself (on the $(item)Convergence Altar$()) grows the creature you choose; once you have studied $(thing)Synthetic Biology$(); before that it will not open for you.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Evolution needs generations, and generations need time. The $(item)Evolution Engine$() only runs where time runs at least ten times as fast; inside a $(item)Chronal Field Projector$() field. Bring a Chronal Anchor.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Notebook, biology. Life is chemistry that makes copies of itself, with mistakes. The $(item)Bioreactor$() grows cultures in $(fluid)Nutrient Broth$(); the $(item)Gene Sampler$() takes a genome from any creature you can reach.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Photosynthesis moves energy through its antenna with near-perfect efficiency by trying every path at once, coherently. A robin feels north through a pair of electrons entangled in a protein in its eye.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Biology from the bottom up: the cell, its skin, its chemistry and its protein factory. Everything alive is made of these.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Life too small to see: bacteria, the viruses that eat them, and the fungi that feel their way through the ground.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The body is attacked all the time, and answers: first the same for every invader, then learned, and remembered. The Anomaly is an invader like any other, and now you can be ready for it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Life at the scale of organs: how the body feeds itself, grows itself, and keeps time.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Life above the single creature: whole populations, their evolution, life built to a plan, and life built backwards. And the keystone that ties the branch together.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Each chapter of the Anomaly storyline now has something to meet, not only to read. $(thing)Abnormality & Infection$(): the containment-failure creatures infect (Fracture, Grey Goo, Rewind, Hollowing). $(thing)Broken Symmetry$(): the Destabilised Husk's Fracture. $(thing)Molecules That Copy Themselves$() and $(thing)Self-Reference$(): the Nanite Swarm's Grey Goo. $(thing)Pathological Objects$(): the Paradox Echo's Rewind.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Late anomalies learn to hide, as tumours do: they shed the markers a ward is made against. The $(thing)Tumour Hydra$()'s bite carries $(thing)Metastasis$(): every ten seconds the growth spreads somewhere new (weakness, hunger or slowness), and no plain Anomaly Ward holds it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Synthetic biology writes genomes from scratch: the $(item)Minimal Synthetic Cell$(), $(item)Stem Cell Cultures$(), and $(item)Xenobots$(); living machines of cells. $(item)Neural Organoids$() are brains grown in a dish; Boltzmann Brains and superintelligence cores now need them.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Biology$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Notebook, chemistry, day one. A bond is not a stick between balls. Two atoms share an electron because the shared $(thing)wavefunction$() spread over both has lower energy than either alone; the same quantum mechanics as everything else in this book.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

$(item)Graphene$() is a single sheet of carbon atoms in hexagons. Roll it and you have $(item)Carbon Nanotubes$(); fold sixty atoms into a ball and you have a $(item)Buckyball$(); hollow, with room for one guest atom inside.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Every reaction is electrons moving from where they are to where they would rather be. The $(item)Electrolytic Cell$() pushes them with a voltage instead of waiting.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Pleroma is everything at once, and that includes every fluid of every mod installed. First, every mod's fluids are distilled together in the $(item)Essence Distillery$() into that mod's $(fluid)Essence$(): one fluid that stands for all of them.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Replace the electron and chemistry changes. A $(thing)positron$() makes positronium, an atom of matter and antimatter, and $(item)Positronium Hydride$() is a molecule of it. A $(thing)muon$() is 200 times heavier than an electron, so a $(item)Muonic Catalyst$() squeezes atoms close enough to fuse cold.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Past uranium, elements get heavier and shorter-lived, until, theory says, an island: nuclei with $(thing)magic numbers$() of protons and neutrons, closed shells that hold them together.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Every machine has a $(thing)catalyst slot$(), the gold slot under its progress arrow. It holds one catalyst at a time, and is filled by hand (shift-click puts a catalyst there first); pipes and ME networks do not reach it.$(br2)A catalyst that wears or decays only works from the catalyst slot, so it is always the one there that wears. A catalyst that never wears still works from an input slot too, as it always did.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Chemistry grew into fourteen branches in 1.2. These are the ones built so far, and their machines; each has its own entries in this chapter.$(li)$(thing)Kinetics & Equilibrium$(): $(item)Haber-Bosch Reactor$(), $(item)Ostwald Converter$(), $(item)Contact Process Tower$(), $(item)Air Separation Unit$()$(li)$(thing)Acids, Bases & Solutions$(): $(item)Titration Bench$(), $(item)Buffer Tank$(), $(item)Brine Evaporator$(), $(item)Reverse Osmosis Cell$()$(li)$(thing)Thermochemistry$(): $(item)Bomb Calorimeter$(), $(item)Heat-Pack Reactor$()
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Chemical Reactor$() has an $(thing)Operation$() console now, like the big physics machines. Set two things: the $(thing)heater temperature$() and the $(thing)residence time$(); how long each batch is held.$(br2)A reaction goes at the rate constant k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT) (Arrhenius): hotter is faster, and the higher its activation energy Eₐ, the more heat it needs.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Technetium-99m loses half of itself every six hours, on the scaled clock, every 15 seconds. Carried loose, or dropped on the ground, a vial is spent within a minute.$(br2)Anywhere it is stored it waits instead: in a machine, an ME network, a chest or a $(item)Chronostatic Vault$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Nothing a machine holds on to lasts for ever. A $(thing)catalyst$() speeds a reaction and is not used up by it, but its pores clog and its surface is poisoned, a little each time. Lenses scratch, magnets lose their field, crystals crack and chips burn out.$(br2)Each time one of these serves as a recipe's catalyst it uses a run of its life: ten runs when the machine is pushed past a $(thing)wear$() limit of its physics. Its tooltip and the bar under it show what is left.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Burn sulfur (or gunpowder) in oxygen for $(fluid)Sulfur Dioxide$(). Over vanadium, 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃; exothermic again, so the equilibrium falls back as it heats, but the $(item)Vanadium Bed$() only lights off near 670 K.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ gives out heat, and turns four volumes of gas into two. So $(thing)ΔG° = ΔH − TΔS$() climbs as it gets hotter and the equilibrium constant $(thing)K = e^(−ΔG°/RT)$() falls: cold and pressed makes the most ammonia. But the iron catalyst is sluggish when cold.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
