A reaction goes at the rate constant $(thing)k = A·e^(−Eₐ/RT)$() (Arrhenius): ten degrees warmer and many go twice as fast. The Chemical Reactor's console runs on it.$(br2)The feeds for heavy chemistry: the $(item)Air Separation Unit$() boils liquid air apart into $(fluid)Nitrogen$() and $(fluid)Oxygen$(); coal and steam in the Chemical Reactor give $(fluid)Hydrogen$() (C + H₂O → CO + H₂), as does water in the Electrolytic Cell.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

On white-hot platinum, ammonia burns to nitric oxide: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O. Too cool, or too long on the gauze, and it burns to plain nitrogen instead. The $(item)Ostwald Converter$() sets the gauze temperature and the contact time: hot (about 1100-1200 K) and brief (a millisecond or two) for 90% selectivity. The nitric oxide is absorbed into $(fluid)Nitric Acid$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

chemistry/intro__r60_acids.title: Acids, Bases and the Purity Tag

pages.text: An acid gives up a proton, a base takes one; $(thing)pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]$(). On the $(item)Titration Bench$() a standard runs into the sample until the indicator turns: at the endpoint the pH jumps six units in a drop. Set the titrant so the pH sits between 4 and 10 and the reagent comes out $(thing)assayed$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A weak acid and its salt hold a pH set by their ratio: $(thing)pH = pKa + log₁₀([A⁻]/[HA])$(). The $(item)Buffer Tank$() mixes them: $(fluid)Phosphate Buffer$() at the pH of blood, 7.4, from bone meal and sulfuric acid; $(fluid)Ammonia Buffer$() at 9. Too far from a ratio of 1 and there is nothing left to buffer with.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Water crosses a membrane toward the saltier side, pulled with the osmotic pressure $(thing)π = iMRT$(): about 30 bar for a brine. The $(item)Reverse Osmosis Cell$() pushes harder; water comes through fresh, and what stays behind is $(fluid)Concentrated Brine$(), which dries to halite sooner. The membrane is rated to 80 bar.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A salt dissolves until its ions' product reaches the $(thing)solubility product K_sp$(). Drive the water off a brine and its salts come out in order: in the $(item)Brine Evaporator$(), $(item)Gypsum$() at four times the strength, $(item)Halite$() at ten to twenty, and $(item)Lithium Carbonate$() from the bittern beyond thirty.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In the $(item)Bomb Calorimeter$() a weighed sample burns in pure oxygen inside a steel bomb, under water. The heat q = m·ΔH_c warms the water by $(thing)ΔT = q/C$(). Size the sample so the rise is readable (1.5 to 3 K) and give it oxygen enough to burn it all: each burn writes a $(item)Thermochemical Data Card$() and gives Insight.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Heat is a state function, so the heat of any reaction can be added up from steps already measured (Hess). The $(item)Heat-Pack Reactor$() runs reactions for their heat: ammonia and nitric acid neutralise to $(item)Ammonium Nitrate$(), giving heat out; mixed too fast it runs away. Dissolving it again takes heat in: $(fluid)Cold Pack Solution$() at 268 K. Salt and ice make $(fluid)Eutectic Brine$() at 252 K.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Split a reaction in two and make its electrons go round by a wire, and its free energy comes out as a voltage: $(thing)ΔG = −nFE$(). The Nernst equation says how the voltage moves with the reactants: $(thing)E = E° − (RT/nF)·ln Q$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A current through a metal salt lays the metal down on the cathode: $(thing)m = MIt/(nF)$() (Faraday). Nitric acid takes the nickel out of meteoric iron as $(fluid)Nickel Sulfate Solution$(); the $(item)Electroplating Bath$() puts it back on iron. Set the current and time for a coat 20 to 50 µm thick; above 8 A/dm² it burns. $(item)Nickel-Plated Iron$() makes $(item)Corrosion-Proof Casings$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A mixture carried down a packed column comes apart: each part sticks to the packing for its own time. The bands spread as they go, the $(thing)plate height H = A + B/u + C·u$() (van Deemter) is smallest at a middling flow, and two parts come out clean when the resolution $(thing)Rs$() reaches 1.5.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

An ion accelerated through V and bent by a field B moves on $(thing)r = √(2mV/q)/B$(). The $(item)Mass Spectrometer$()'s detector sits at 0.5 m: set the field for the mass you want. Cold clouds concentrate deuterium in their molecules thousands of times; a cheaper deuterium than heavy water. Lithium-6 can be picked out of lithium the same way.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Frontier's clouds are a gas field Earth's air cannot match. A $(item)Cloud Siphon$() touching a Hydrogen, Oxygen or Dust Cloud draws its gas for ever; the cloud is not used up. The Fractionation Spire, run cold, parts out $(fluid)Hydrogen$() and $(fluid)Carbon Monoxide$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A catalyst holds a molecule on its surface just long enough to change it. Too weakly and nothing sticks, too tightly and nothing leaves: plotted against the binding energy, the activity is a $(thing)volcano$() (Sabatier). The coverage of a surface follows $(thing)θ = KP/(1 + KP)$() (Langmuir).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A framework is a crystal of nodes and struts, mostly empty. On the $(item)Framework Assembler$() the linker sets the pore: it must fit the target molecule, and the solvent must be dried out slowly or the pores collapse. $(item)MOF Gas Sorbent$() fills a $(item)MOF Gas Storage Cell$(), which holds 256,000 mB of one gas; sixteen tanks' worth, because the framework holds gas on its inner surface (Langmuir). $(item)Silica Aerogel$() is ninety-nine parts air.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Coal and hydrogen under pressure make $(fluid)Synthetic Crude$() (Bergius); the pack's crude oil will do as well. In the $(item)Cracking Tower$() its long chains break into short ones: hotter gives more $(fluid)Ethylene$() (about 1100 K), cooler more $(fluid)Propylene$() (1000 K). Each needs a 60% share. Above 1150 K coke fouls the Zeolite Catalyst; steam keeps it down.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

When a fraction p of the ends have reacted, chains average $(thing)1/(1 − p)$() units (Carothers): a thousand-unit polyethylene needs p = 0.999. The $(item)Polymeriser$() makes $(item)Polymer Sheet$() from ethylene, $(item)Nylon Fibre$() from propylene, ammonia and nitric acid, and $(item)Aramid Fibre$() from PAH soot spun out of sulfuric acid. Above 420 K it runs away.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A route of n steps keeps $(thing)yⁿ$() of its material: every step costs. On the $(item)Synthesis Bench$(), choose the shortest route the target allows; it has a least number of steps, and no route is shorter. $(item)Fine Reagents$() are what later recipes ask for by name.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Ligands split a metal's d orbitals by $(thing)Δ$(); against the pairing energy $(thing)P$(), that decides high spin or low. The $(item)Coordination Reactor$() sets the ligand field: $(item)Prussian Blue$() and the $(item)Porphyrin Oxygen Carrier$() are low spin, the $(item)Copper Ammine Complex$() high. The porphyrin is haem: it holds oxygen and lets it go.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

At its $(thing)eutectic$() an alloy melts all at once: the $(item)Phase Diagram Kiln$() makes Superconducting Solder from lead and copper more cheaply. The $(item)Doping Furnace$() diffuses a dopant into a wafer for a working junction (10¹⁶ to 10¹⁸ carriers); a $(item)Doped Wafer$() goes through the Lithographer at twice the yield.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Each bond absorbs infrared at its own vibration, $(thing)ν = √(k/μ)/2π$(). The $(item)Infrared Spectrometer$() must scan across the band, narrowly enough to resolve it: a $(item)Structure Card$(). With one in its catalyst slot, the Synthesis Bench knows its target and takes a shorter route.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

On Titan, methane does what water does on Earth: it rains, runs in rivers, pools in seas and evaporates again. At 94 K its vapour pressure is about a sixth of an atmosphere (Clausius-Clapeyron); enough to make clouds and rain.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A photon absorbed breaks one bond; what follows can make several molecules of product; the quantum yield Φ. How much of the light is absorbed is the $(thing)Beer-Lambert law$(): the absorbance is A = εcl, and the cell takes a fraction 1 − 10^(−A).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The alchemists searched for the $(thing)alkahest$(), a universal solvent that would dissolve anything. It is distilled here from all of Chemistry at once, in the $(item)Alkahest Still$(), in four stages, each with its own boiling point. Purity must reach 95% (a reflux ratio of 5 or more); hotter is faster, but 150 K over the boiling point boils over.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Many molecules come in two mirror-image forms, like hands. Living things use only one: the wrong hand of a drug can be useless, or a poison. A $(thing)chiral catalyst$() lowers the barrier to one hand by ΔΔG‡ more than to the other, so that one forms $(thing)s = e^(ΔΔG‡/RT)$() times faster; the enantiomeric excess is ee = (s − 1)/(s + 1).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In 1951 Boris Belousov found a mixture that turned from yellow to clear and back, again and again. Nobody believed him. The $(thing)Brusselator$() shows how: one species makes more of itself from another and is used up again, and past a threshold $(thing)B > 1 + A²$() the steady mixture can no longer stay still.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A current makes a magnetic field. Around a long straight wire it circles the wire, and its strength falls with distance: B = μ₀I/(2πr). Ten amps give 40 µT five centimetres away, about the strength of the planet's own field.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A changing field drives a current: spin a coil of N turns in a field B and it gives ε = NBAω·sin ωt. Every generator works this way. The iron core that guides the field is built from thin $(item)Electrical Steel Laminations$(), so the changing field cannot stir currents inside it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Spin a coil in a magnet's field and it drives a current: ε = NBAω. With the same coil and load, the power goes as ε², so a magnet three times stronger gives about ten times the power.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A permanent magnet is set by a field stronger than its $(thing)coercivity$(), and keeps what it was given. Ferrite needs about 0.35 T, neodymium-iron-boron 1.2 T, samarium-cobalt 2 T.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Push a conducting fluid across a magnetic field and it becomes the armature of a generator: the field drives current across the flow, into $(item)MHD Electrodes$() on the channel walls. No turbine, no moving parts.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A proton crossing a magnetic field circles, and how often it circles, $(thing)f = qB/2πm$(), does not depend on how fast it goes. Lawrence saw what that meant: put an RF voltage at that frequency across a gap, and the proton is kicked every half turn, spiralling out faster and faster in step.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Two circuits, each a capacitor and a coil, each ringing at its own frequency. Tune the primary to the secondary and energy sloshes across, and appears at a voltage higher by $(thing)√(C₁/C₂)$(): kilovolts in, megavolts out.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Maxwell's equations put electricity, magnetism and light into one theory: changing fields make each other, and a wave of field carries itself across empty space at $(thing)c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀)$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Steady magnets top out near 45 tesla. For more, dump a room of capacitors into a coil for a few milliseconds: $(thing)B = μ₀NI/L$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In a strong field and the cold, the Hall resistance of a sheet of electrons sits on plateaus at $(thing)h/(νe²)$(); 25 812.807 Ω for ν = 1, exact to a part in a billion, because it counts a topological number. The Laser Cutter cuts $(item)Hall Bar Chips$() from silicon and gold.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Two rails and an armature between them: current up one rail, across, down the other. The field between the rails pushes the armature out with $(thing)F = ½L′I²$(), a railgun.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
I threw the Omnilex into the Quantum Foam. It shattered into everything I had ever made, and the pieces became a shape with too many directions. It asked me whether I understood.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The Reality Compiler showed that the universe runs on source code. Beneath the code are $(thing)axioms$(); the rules that decide what can be true at all. Physics is just their consequence.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Log, first descent. Outside every universe there is a single, endless space. A $(thing)World Tree$() of an unknown material towers over it, more than four hundred blocks high.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Particle Spectrometer$() splits quark-gluon plasma into $(item)quark flavours$(), $(item)leptons$() and $(item)gauge bosons$(). The heaviest quarks and the $(item)Higgs$() need the Synchrotron.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Landscapes are written by water. A river carries grains as fast as it flows, and drops them as it slows, the heaviest first. A small grain of radius r sinks at a steady speed v = (2/9)(ρ_s − ρ_f)g r²/μ: sand settles in minutes, clay in days.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A map flattens a round planet, and no flat map keeps everything true. Keep every angle true, so a compass course is a straight line, and the map must stretch towards the poles: a point at latitude φ is drawn at R·ln tan(π/4 + φ/2).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

An earthquake sends out two kinds of wave. $(thing)Pressure waves$() push and pull the rock along their path and travel fastest, about 6 km/s in the crust. $(thing)Shear waves$() shake it sideways and travel at about 3.5 km/s. The farther the source, the larger the gap between them: d = Δt·v_p·v_s/(v_p − v_s).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Scientists worked across the Overworld before you, and their field sites still stand; built, like the old observatory ruins, from the mod's own materials, with Containment Caches of what they left behind.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Bedrock is not the bottom of the world; it is only as far as any tool could cut. The $(item)Core Drill$() cuts it: hold it against bedrock and keep holding. At the floor of the Overworld the bit breaks through into a $(item)Mantle Breach$(). Step in.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Interior is richer than the Overworld. Its ores run in bigger veins: $(item)Rich Iron$() and $(item)Rich Copper$() in the crust, $(item)Rich Gold$() in the basalt of the Magma Chambers. Their chunks smelt to two ingots; assayed in the $(item)Spectrograph$() they give three each, and what rides with them in nature; magnetite with iron, gold with copper, uraninite with reef gold.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Deep Drilling Rig$() is a derrick: four leaning legs, a crown block, and a string of pipe hanging into the hole. Set the depth, the weight on the bit and its speed, and the density of the mud that fills the well.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Rock buried deep recrystallises into whatever is stable down there. The $(item)Tectonic Press$() does it on purpose: a multi-anvil vessel over a firebox, under a hydraulic ram. You set two things, the anvil pressure and the furnace temperature, and the phase diagram does the rest.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The $(thing)Magma Crawler$() lives in the Magma Chambers' sea. Basaltic Magma is its water: it swims through it as fast as you walk, and its bite sets you alight. On dry rock it is slower.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Every hazard below has its suit, crafted like ordinary armour.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Carbon dioxide traps the heat the ground gives off: a forcing $(thing)ΔF = 5.35 ln(C/280 ppm)$() W/m² - 3.7 W/m² for each doubling. Aerosols reflect sunlight back out. The world warms by about $(thing)0.8 K per W/m²$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A $(item)Survey Satellite$() sits in the Interstellar Scoop as a catalyst, the Scoop works only high up or in space, which is where a satellite flies, and photographs the ground: a $(item)Satellite Image Plate$(). From 700 km, a 1.1 m mirror sees 40 cm.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Water seeps through rock by $(thing)Darcy's law$(): Q = kAΔP/(μL); permeability times the pressure gradient. The $(item)Aquifer Pump$() draws it up: Water anywhere; in the Planetary Interior, an $(item)Aquifer Sample$() with Deep Brine from a confined aquifer.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Night 9. A tesseract is a 4D cube: take a cube and drag it along a fourth axis, $(thing)W$(), at right angles to the other three. What you see in the assembler is its 3D shadow, rotating through the W axis; the way a cube's shadow on a wall seems to turn inside out.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In 1867 Maxwell imagined a tiny being that opens a door only for fast molecules, sorting hot from cold for free; breaking the second law. The catch took a century to find: the demon must record each molecule, and erasing a bit of memory costs at least kT ln 2 of heat.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Calculus is the art of the infinitely small. $(item)Infinitesimals$() come from the reals. With a $(item)Function Graph$() they become $(item)Derivative$() and $(item)Integral Operators$(); rates of change and sums of slices.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The Platonic Realm is self-similar: big islands low down, smaller ones above them, smaller still at the top. Its landmarks are mathematical objects built exactly to their definitions.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Start from nothing, literally. Start from $(item)Axiom Schemas$() and the $(item)Empty Set$() (Void Essence, or plenty of Void Lattice). Von Neumann built every number out of empty sets nested inside each other; I am doing the same.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Absolute Infinity is no longer a shortcut. To build it I have to build mathematics itself, one branch at a time.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Each number system is built from the one before it. Every step patches a hole: you cannot subtract 5 from 3 in the naturals, or halve 1 in the integers, or square-root 2 in the rationals. So each time, I build something bigger.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Mathematical objects have to exist somewhere. The $(item)Platonic Compass$() takes you there: a bright realm of floating axiom stone where the five Platonic solids hang in the sky.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Mathematics starts from almost nothing: a few rules of logic, the empty set, and counting.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Mathematics can start almost at once. After $(thing)Number Systems$() the $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$() is made from quartz, iron, a comparator, a block of redstone and Quantum Dots, and it counts $(item)Natural Number Lattices$() from Cherenkov Quartz and redstone.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Geometry, symmetry and shape: the mathematics of space, and of the extra dimensions Physics needs.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The mathematics of things that change: rate equations, where they settle, and whether they stay there.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Statistics, information and computation: how sure, how much, and how long.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Transfinite Hierarchy is no longer a world of its own. It is the $(thing)Platonic Realm$()'s top layer, the Infinite: above Y 1280, across a wide gap of empty air over the Continuum, ordinal stone begins, and the Hierarchy's four strata rise one above another as they always did, with Hilbert's Hotel, the tesseract frames, the Hopf rings and the ordinal spires.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The best choice, and the shape of a network.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Feedback: measure, compare, correct.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
When the best choice depends on what others choose.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
How an even mixture paints itself into stripes.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Wherever something changes in proportion to how much of it there is, e appears. Some of the places it turns up in the mod:
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

e^(iπ) + 1 = 0. Five constants, each made in its own phase: $(item)Zero$() and $(item)Unity$() (Foundations), the $(item)π Crystal$() (the Geometer's Table), the $(item)e Crystal$() and the $(item)Imaginary Unit$() (the Integrator).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
The $(item)Analytic Continuator$() is a console now, and built from early parts (Rational Fields, glass, clocks, iron and redstone).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A reading room for a machine: error-corrected cores in a ring around a well of light, under a glass dome. Give it power and Research Dossiers; it shortens whatever its owner is studying.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Infinity comes in kinds. The $(item)Cantor Key$() opens a dimension built in strata, each layer of islands higher and sparser than the last, where the ordinals and cardinals are mined.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Weigh a helium nucleus and it is lighter than its two protons and two neutrons were apart, by about 0.03 atomic mass units. That missing mass is the $(thing)binding energy$(): B = Δm·c², 28.3 MeV for helium-4; several million times what a chemical bond holds.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

$(item)Pitchblende Ore$() lies in stone and, more often, in deepslate. It is uranium ore, and it is radioactive: its nuclei fall apart on their own, at random, but at a fixed rate. Of N₀ nuclei, N = N₀·e^(−λt) remain; half of them after each half-life.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Radium-226 decays into $(item)Radon-222$(), a gas with a half-life of 3.8 days. The $(item)Decay Chamber$() draws it off a piece of Radium Salt, which, with a 1,600-year half-life, is never used up.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

From 1.2, radiation in the mod follows the physics. Every source is an $(thing)isotope$() with its real half-life and its own kind of radiation, and what reaches you falls with the $(thing)square of the distance$(): a source two blocks away gives a quarter of the dose it gives at one.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Natural uranium is 0.72% uranium-235. A reactor needs a few per cent. Roast $(item)Raw Pitchblende$() into $(item)Yellowcake$(), combine it with $(item)Fluorspar$() (the Spectrograph finds it in calcite and in geode shells) and you have $(fluid)Uranium Hexafluoride$(), a gas.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
In a $(item)Molten Salt Reactor$() the fuel is liquid: uranium fluoride dissolved in a lithium salt, pumped through a core of graphite. Graphite slows the neutrons; the salt carries the heat out.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Electrolysing water leaves the heavy molecules behind: a thousand millibuckets of $(fluid)Water$() give ten of $(fluid)Heavy Water$(), and electrolysing that gives $(fluid)Deuterium$(). $(item)Lithium$() is won from Deep Brine; the Gas Centrifuge Cascade enriches it to $(item)Lithium-6$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Hafnium-178m2 holds 2.4 MeV in each nucleus, locked in by its spin, for thirty-one years: $(thing)1.3 TJ$() a kilogram. The Cyclotron makes it from rare earths (hafnium travels with them) above 6 MeV.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Deuterium and tritium fuse into helium-4 and a neutron, giving $(thing)17.6 MeV$(). They must be hot (10-20 keV, over a hundred million kelvin), dense, and held long enough: Lawson's $(thing)nTτ ≥ 3×10²¹ keV·s/m³$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

X-rays are about as long as the gaps between atoms. Scattered by a crystal's planes, they reinforce only where the extra path between neighbouring planes is a whole number of wavelengths: $(thing)nλ = 2d·sin θ$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$() a seed crystal is dipped into the melt and drawn slowly up, turning, the Czochralski method. The melt freezes onto it as one crystal. Its $(item)Iridium Crucible$() is made of Iron-Nickel: a planet's core, and the iron meteorites, hoard the iridium the crust lacks.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Every lens is made the same way: study the crystal, grow it pure, cut it true. Three machines do it, the $(item)X-ray Diffractometer$(), the $(item)Crystal Growth Furnace$() and the $(item)Optical Workshop$(), and what they make goes into the telescopes and more.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Optical Workshop$() turns blanks into optics. A lens's power is set by its two surfaces: $(thing)P = (n − 1)(C₁ − C₂)$(), with C the curvature of each; one over its radius. A 1-dioptre lens focuses at a metre.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

An excited atom struck by a photon of just the right energy gives off a second, identical photon: $(thing)stimulated emission$(). Fill a crystal with excited atoms, put it between two mirrors, and the light builds on itself.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Chemistry$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Chance has laws. Repeat an experiment n times, each a success with probability p, and exactly k successes happen with probability C(n,k)·p^k·(1 − p)^(n−k). Three heads in ten tosses: 11.7%.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A curve made of many small chances is the $(thing)normal distribution$(): f(x) = e^(−(x−μ)²/2σ²)/(σ√2π). 68% of it lies within one width of its centre, 95% within two.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Drop a ball through rows of pegs. At each it goes left or right with even odds, so after n rows it has gone right k times with probability C(n,k)/2ⁿ. Pile up enough balls and the binomial heap becomes a bell curve: $(thing)the central limit theorem$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Grains of clay in water never keep still: molecules too small to see strike them from every side, unevenly, and they wander. Einstein worked out how far: the mean square displacement grows as $(thing)⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt$(), with D = kT/(6πηr).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Some sums are too hard to work out. Throw dice instead: average N random samples and the answer is off by only $(thing)σ/√N$(). To halve the error, sample four times as much. The $(item)Monte Carlo Engine$() draws up to a trillion samples a run.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

At night, in the open, something drifts that has no will of its own: a cloud of particles taking an honest random walk. Near prey its steps lean toward it; a drift on top of the diffusion, the way a charged grain wanders in a field.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The largest of n draws from a bell curve is about $(thing)√(2 ln n)$() standard deviations: five for a million draws. Rare events are rarer than average ones, but not as rare as a bell curve alone says. A Galton Board now and then sorts an Entropy Die into a $(item)Large Deviation Shard$(); the Monte Carlo Engine, tilting its samples toward the tail and weighing them back, makes one every time, slowly. A $(item)Black Swan Feather$(), proof the improbable happens, is a shortcut: with it the Pulsed Magnet Lab finds a monopole every time, and an Ergodic Mixer Core becomes a Boltzmann Brain in a tenth of the time.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A fluctuation that costs entropy ΔS happens with odds $(thing)e^(−ΔS/k)$(). A lone brain that only thinks it remembers a world is far cheaper than a whole low-entropy universe, so in an eternal universe, which observers are likely? That is the measure problem.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Three vats in a ring, A → B → C → A, the feed hopping on by chances p, q and r. However it starts, it settles into the steady state: time in each vat ∝ $(thing)1/(its chance of leaving)$(). Give a vat three fifths of the time and monazite sand comes out as that vat's product: rare earths, thorium, or phosphate. Make all three equal and warm helium thermalises into $(fluid)Maxwell-Boltzmann Gas$(). The slowest hop sets how fast it mixes.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A state of energy E is found $(thing)e^(−E/kT)$() times as often as one of zero: the Boltzmann factor. Summed over every state, the factors make the partition function, and everything else, energy, entropy, pressure, is a derivative of it. The Monte Carlo Engine samples one into a $(item)Partition Function Matrix$(); a billion sorted samples make a $(item)Monte Carlo Sample Pack$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A drunkard's walk of N steps of length l ends about $(thing)l√N$() from where it began; the reason Brownian grains wander as they do. A $(item)Markov Chain Link$() remembers only the one before it; a $(item)Poisson Clock$() ticks at random, each tick a decay in its radium. Clay stirred into water makes a $(fluid)Brownian Suspension$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Third dive. The Quantum Foam has a floor and a ceiling I cannot pass. Below lies $(item)Schrödinger's Limit$(), where every possibility is still undecided.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
First dive. Below the Planck length, spacetime is not smooth. The $(item)Planck Diver$() takes me there.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Final pages. Every computation the universe will ever perform, converging on a single point at the end of time: the $(item)Omega Point$(). It is the last thing you can make.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Mathematics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Observation log. A running singularity bends light around its horizon: the room behind it is smeared into an $(thing)Einstein ring$(), with a bright $(thing)photon ring$() at the edge of the shadow.$(br2)White holes do the opposite.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Horizon Diver$() takes me through an event horizon. Rule one: $(thing)carry a Geodesic Anchor$(). Without one, tidal forces kill within two seconds, in the black hole and the white hole alike.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() and $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Is a dead universe dead forever? Statistical mechanics says no. In a finite system every state recurs (Poincaré recurrence), for a de Sitter universe after about e^{10¹²²} years. Long before that, fluctuations happen by chance: P ∝ exp(−(Δ_E − TΔ_S)/k_BT). A single brain is far more likely than a whole world; the $(thing)Boltzmann brain$() problem.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The second branch of time is $(thing)Finality$(). $(thing)Cosmic Eschatology$() starts from the acceleration equation, ä/a = −4πG(ρ + 3p/c²)/3 + Λc²/3: matter and radiation decelerate the expansion, dark energy accelerates it, and ours is accelerating (q₀ ≈ −0.53).
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

spacetime/intro__finality_eras.title: The Long Dark: Protons and Black Holes

pages.text: If the universe expands forever, its history after the stars falls into eras. The last red dwarfs die after 10¹⁴ years; then the $(thing)Degenerate Era$() of white dwarfs, neutron stars and planets, until, if grand unification is right, $(thing)Proton Decay$() dissolves them: p → e⁺ + π⁰, with a lifetime above 10³⁴ years.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The likeliest end: maximum entropy. After the black holes, an empty de Sitter space is left, with a horizon c/H away that glows at ħH/(2πk_B) ≈ 3×10⁻³⁰ K and holds S = πc⁵k_B/(GħH²) ≈ 2×10¹²²; the most entropy there can ever be. Nothing more can happen, because nothing can get colder than its surroundings.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

$(thing)The Big Rip$(): phantom dark energy (w < −1) grows denser as space grows. With w = −1.5 the Rip comes 22 billion years from now: clusters go a billion years before, the Solar System three months before, atoms in the last instant. The $(item)Dark Energy Siphon$() bottles it in a $(item)Phantom Energy Cell$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it. Near the Earth the effect is tiny; near a spinning black hole, inside its ergosphere, nothing can stand still.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Light climbing out of gravity loses energy. Over a height H the fraction lost is $(thing)gH/c²$(), about 2.5×10⁻¹⁵ up a 22.5-metre tower. In 1959 Pound and Rebka measured it with the gamma ray of iron-57, whose line is so sharp that even this shows.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Two black holes spiralling together shake spacetime: a wave passes, stretching space one way and squeezing it the other, by a strain h of 10⁻²¹ when it reaches us. The $(item)Laser Interferometer$() is an L of two long arms with a $(item)Test Mass$() at each end: a laser split between the arms comes back to interfere, and a wave changes the pattern.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In 1975 Colella, Overhauser and Werner split single neutrons with a perfect silicon crystal and joined them again, and tilted the whole thing. One path ran a few centimetres higher than the other; gravity slowed the neutron on it; the two waves came back out of step. Gravity, acting on a quantum wave: $(thing)Δφ = 2πm²gλA·sin α/h²$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Sound in a fluid flowing faster than sound cannot make headway upstream. Where the flow crosses its own speed of sound there is a horizon for sound, and the mathematics of sound near it is the mathematics of light near a black hole. Hawking radiation included.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Two experiments have put quantum theory and gravity into one equation: gravity bending a neutron's phase, and a horizon glowing with quantum pairs. Both are $(thing)semiclassical$(): the quantum world on a smooth, classical spacetime.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Clocks deep in a gravity well run slow: by $(thing)1/√(1 − r_s/r)$() at a distance r from a mass with Schwarzschild radius r_s.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A spinning mass drags spacetime round with it: a gyroscope near the Earth turns by $(thing)Ω = 2GJ/(c²r³)$(). A $(item)Precision Gyroscope$() carried in the off hand holds you steady: no Frame Drag, no Tidal Strain.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A falling body follows a $(thing)geodesic$(): the straightest path through curved spacetime. The $(item)Geodesic Compass$() points along one. A mass squeezed inside $(thing)r_s = 2GM/c²$() lets no light out.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Two compact stars spiral in as gravitational waves carry off their orbit; how fast the pitch rises depends only on the $(thing)chirp mass$() (m₁m₂)^(3/5)/(m₁ + m₂)^(1/5). The Binary of the Accretion Frontier drops Chirp Signal Records and Merger Remnants.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Alcubierre found a solution of general relativity that moves a bubble of flat space at any speed: space contracts ahead of it and expands behind. Its wall must be made of $(thing)negative energy$(), from $(item)Negative Energy Lattices$() of Casimir plates.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Maldacena and Susskind: two entangled particles are joined by a wormhole too small to cross. The $(item)ER=EPR Weaver$() makes pairs and sends their halves to two mouths. Fidelity falls with the distance and with the weaver's own heat, and every pair heats it. Cold, and close, it weaves an $(item)ER Bridge Thread$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A black hole of mass M glows at $(thing)T = ħc³/(8πGMk)$(), radiates power ∝ 1/M², and evaporates in a time ∝ M³. A stellar hole is colder than the sky; one of a billion kilograms, hotter than any star.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A black hole has entropy $(thing)S = Ac³/(4Għ)$(), its area in Planck units over four, the most any region can hold: the $(item)Bekenstein Crystal$(). It evaporates; if what comes out is purely thermal, what fell in is gone, and quantum mechanics forbids that.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Loop quantum gravity quantises space: areas come in steps of $(thing)8πγℓₚ²√(j(j+1))$(). The $(item)Spin Network Loom$() weaves Planck Shards into $(item)Planck Area Tiles$(), tiles into $(item)Spin Network Nodes$(), and nodes with liquid spacetime into $(fluid)Quantum Spacetime Condensate$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Empty space looks empty only if you are not accelerating. Accelerate at a, and the vacuum glows at $(thing)T = ħa/(2πck)$(); one kelvin needs 2.5×10²⁰ m/s².
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Tensor Calculus Engine$() works up from $(item)Lorentz Transforms$() and the $(item)Minkowski Lattice$() to the $(item)Metric$() and $(item)Riemann Curvature Tensors$() and finally the $(item)Einstein Field Core$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(item)Chrono Loom$() reverses the $(item)Arrow of Time$(), ties $(item)Temporal Knots$() (a Möbius strip helps; a surface with only one side seemed fitting) and crystallises the $(item)Novikov$() self-consistency principle.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
A star begins as a cloud. I harvest $(fluid)Nebular Gas$() with the Dark Matter Halo Collector and collapse it into a $(item)Protostar$() in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Field notes, the Bulk. The extra dimensions are mined here: $(item)Kaluza-Klein$() everywhere, $(item)Dilaton$() on the Graviton Reefs, $(item)Moduli$() in the Moduli Wastes.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Two branches of physics are about time itself: $(thing)Origin$(), how a universe begins, and $(thing)Finality$(), how it ends. Origin starts with $(thing)The Hot Big Bang$(): run the expansion backwards and everything was once hotter and denser than the core of a star.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Where Finality ends, Origin begins. Roger Penrose noticed that at the end of a heat death only massless particles remain, and light has no clock: it cannot tell an infinitely large, cold universe from a tiny, hot one. Rescale the dead universe's infinite future and it is the Big Bang of the next $(thing)aeon$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Big Bang alone cannot explain why opposite sides of the sky have the same temperature to one part in 100,000: they were never in contact. $(thing)Inflation$() does: before the hot Big Bang, a scalar field, the inflaton, sat high on its potential and made space grow exponentially, sixty e-folds in 10⁻³² s.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Reheating makes matter and antimatter in equal amounts, and they should have annihilated into light. For every billion photons there is one baryon left over. Andrei Sakharov's conditions say what it takes: baryon number violation, C and CP violation, and a moment out of equilibrium.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

$(thing)Vacuum Stability$(): a universe can fail before it starts. A vacuum energy larger by a factor of a hundred and no galaxy forms; the measured one is 10¹²⁰ times smaller than quantum theory's natural guess; the $(thing)cosmological constant problem$(). And the Higgs coupling runs downwards with energy until, near 10¹⁰ GeV, a deeper vacuum opens: ours is $(thing)metastable$(). The $(item)Higgs Field Modulator$() maps it into a $(item)Metastable Vacuum Lattice$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Physics$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Every journey to another dimension, by Brane Shifter, rift, wormhole, falling through the void or the hyperobject, now takes a moment: the travel animation builds up on screen for under two seconds, and only then do you jump. The loading screen of each world is its own.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Every strange dimension has the item that lets you survive it. Each one was made from what you brought back from the places before it, so it carries their protection too.$(br2)Carry an attunement item and every dimension whose own item comes $(l)earlier$() in this list cannot touch you at all: no debuffs, no strange gravity, no rules.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Brane cosmology says our universe is a membrane adrift in a higher-dimensional $(thing)Bulk$(). The $(item)Brane Shifter$() slips me sideways into it, and back. It requires the Brane Cosmology research.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Log, the Bulk, fifth crossing. It is not uniform. There are regions: the open $(thing)Bulk$(), the crystal $(thing)Graviton Reefs$() and the $(thing)Moduli Wastes$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Ruins and impossible structures keep their treasure in $(item)Containment Caches$(), not chests. Each dimension seals its own kind: the Bulk Cache borrows room from a fifth dimension, the Euclid Reliquary of the Platonic Realm closes on an exact right angle, the Hilbert Locker is always full and always has room for one more.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Sunday. Even a lab deserves some style. Put a block of any high-tech material in a $(item)Stonecutter$() for plating, tiles, bricks and pillars, and back again, so nothing is wasted.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Nether expedition, day 2. $(item)Dilithium$() grows down here. Its lattice is porous to antimatter, which makes it the only practical regulator for an annihilation reactor.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Every other place has its own law, and the law is not kind to visitors. Carry the right $(thing)attunement$() anywhere in your inventory and you will live, with a reminder of where you are.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

None of these places has a bottom you can die on. Fall off the floor of one and you fall into another:$(li)off the $(thing)Bulk$(): back onto our own brane$(li)through the $(thing)Platonic Realm$() (and its upper strata, the Transfinite Hierarchy): into the Quantum Foam$(li)below the $(thing)Transfinite$(): into the Quantum Foam
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Stand inside a structure built in more dimensions than three and your eyes stop agreeing with your feet. The deeper you go, the more space folds to match the object you are in:
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(thing)Planetary Interior$() needs no attunement item, its laws are only the planet's own, and they press harder the deeper you go. You reach it with the $(item)Core Drill$() (research $(thing)Plate Tectonics$()), cutting the Overworld's bedrock floor; you leave by any $(item)Mantle Breach$(); one opens beside you wherever you arrive.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Others have been down here before. In the Crustal Caverns stand $(thing)Deep Boreholes$(): drill holes cased in steel and abandoned two dozen blocks down, a broken drill floor at the top and a cache at the bottom of the hole.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Survey notes. $(item)Cherenkov Quartz$() grows deep in the deepslate layer. $(item)Degenerate Matter$() is found in End stone; smelt or blast it into $(item)Neutronium$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Out past the edge of the sky, round a black hole feeding on a disk of its own fire, islands of rock and ice drift in the dark. The $(thing)Accretion Frontier$() is reached with a $(item)Light Sail$() (research $(thing)Galactic Dynamics$()): climb to y 200 or higher, stand under open sky, and unfurl it. Unfurled again in the Frontier, it brings you home and slows your fall.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Each of the Frontier's creatures acts out its physics. The $(thing)Nebuloid$() is a drifting knot of gas and dust; inside it you are blind. The $(thing)Pulsar Wisp$() pulses on an exact beat, once every one and a half seconds, and its pulse hurts and irradiates anyone it can see within ten blocks; dodge behind something between pulses.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Accretion Slag Ore$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Asteroid Rock$(). The rubble of planetesimals that never became planets. Its chondrules are frozen droplets from the Solar System's first few million years.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Brown Dwarf Remnant$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Cosmic Ray Ore$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Dust Cloud$(). A cloud of dust grains, too thin to stand on. Now and then, broken, it leaves Interstellar Dust.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Dusty Ice$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Einstein Ring Cluster$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Frontier Regolith$(). Rock ground to dust by billions of years of micrometeorites. Assayed in bulk it gives back its interstellar dust and a little rare earth.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Hydrogen Cloud$(). Ionised hydrogen glowing red at 656 nm, the H-alpha line. You can walk straight through it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Magnetar Crust Ore$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Nebular Ice$(). Water, carbon monoxide and ammonia frozen together on dust grains at about fifteen kelvin. Starlight slowly builds larger molecules within it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Oxygen Cloud$(). Doubly ionised oxygen glowing green-blue at 501 nm. You can walk straight through it.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Planetesimal Core Ore$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Protostar Fragment$(). Found in the Accretion Frontier, between Y 0 and 255. Gives Protostellar Ember when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Pulsar Crust$(). Iron from a neutron star's crust: a lattice of nuclei in a sea of electrons, held under a field of some hundred million tesla.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Pulsar Timing Ore$().
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Rim Slag$(). Cinder flung from the inner edge of an accretion disk, where gas spirals in at a fair fraction of light speed and is heated to millions of degrees.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Station Hull$(). Aluminium skin and stringers from a spacecraft, thin enough to dent by hand. In vacuum, a few millimetres of it is all that separates air from nothing.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
$(item)Void Glass$(). Glass as dark as the space it came from. Gravity bends light as a lens does, and a well-aligned mass draws a background source into a full Einstein ring.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Every region of the Accretion Frontier has its hazard, and each has an answer.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Saturn's largest moon is the only other world we know with rain, rivers, lakes and seas on its surface, of methane, at 94 K, under an air half again as thick as Earth's. Reach it with a $(item)Cryogenic Lander$() (research $(thing)Titan$()): stand under open sky in the Overworld and use it. Used again on Titan, it lifts off and brings you home under its parachute.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

$(thing)Cold$(): at 94 K you freeze as in powder snow, then take frost damage. Each piece of a $(item)Heated Pressure Suit$() (a Pressure Suit crafted with two Silica Aerogel and redstone heating wire) keeps out a quarter of it; a full suit, all of it. It is still a pressure suit underneath.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

In 1865 Kekule dreamt of a snake seizing its own tail, and woke knowing the shape of benzene: a ring of six carbons. Use $(item)Kekule's Dream$() in Titan's $(thing)Selk Crater$() and a serpent of six segments rises, its tail in its mouth.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Nothing on Titan is alive the way we are, but its chemistry moves. The $(thing)Tholin Drifter$() is a flake of the haze, carried on the slow wind (which turns with the day). Whoever it settles on is coated in tar: darkness, and heavy steps. It drops Tholin.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

High above the Platonic Realm's own islands (the Number Line), across a gap of empty air, and far below Curved Space lies the $(thing)Elements$(): islands of $(item)Euclidean Marble$() from Y 320 to 400, laid out as if with compass and straightedge.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
At the foot of the Realm, some 650 blocks below the Number Line, a broad plain of $(item)Postulate Slate$(): what every proof stands on.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
Above Curved Space and far below the Infinite, islands of $(item)Dense Stone$() in three bands, the same shapes at three sizes: between any two points, another.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.
High above the Elements, islands of $(item)Hyperbolic Stone$(), warped like saddles: geometry where parallel lines spread apart.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The Platonic Realm is six layers, one for each part of mathematics, from Y −768 at the bottom to 1536 at the top. Between each layer and the next lies a wide gap of empty air, a hundred blocks and more: too far to climb, and too far to fall.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

The $(thing)Macrophage$() is slow, but it engulfs whatever it catches. Caught, you are held inside it and digested: strike it to break free. It eats items and red cells too, and gives the items back when it dies.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

A body, seen from the inside at the scale of its cells. Reach it with the $(item)Miniaturiser$() (research $(thing)Inner Space$(), after Circulation): use it in the Overworld and you shrink until a cell is the size of a house. Used again inside, it brings you back out. Falling out of the bottom brings you home too.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Under Titan's Subsurface Seal lies an ocean of salty water, larger than all of Earth's. The $(item)Cryobot$() (research $(thing)Titan's Hidden Ocean$()) melts down into it: stand on the Seal at the bottom of Titan and use it. You come out just under the ice, with the probe's own air for half a minute. An $(item)Oxygen Rebreather$() keeps you breathing after that, and it is as cold as Titan above. Use the Cryobot again to climb back; sinking through the floor brings you up through the ice too.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Found one: a crashed research observatory, its containment dome cracked, a supply cache still inside. They dot the Overworld. Who built them, I don't yet know.$(br2)A good source of early Cherenkov Quartz and Neutronium; worth a detour before I can make either myself.
$(thing)More$(): the $(thing)Dimensions$() tab has the rest of this study: its machines, materials, recipes and how they connect.

Many multiblocks take $(thing)coils$(), in one of 5 tiers. The structure counts as the $(thing)lowest$() tier among all its coils, so build them all of one kind. Each tier above the first makes a coiled machine faster (by a quarter of its base speed a tier, unless the machine says otherwise), and some recipes only run at or above a given tier: the machine's screen and JEI show which.$(br2)Every coil's tooltip names its tier.

The $(item)Structure Assembler$() builds a structure's coils in one tier: the highest you carry enough of for the whole structure (your inventory and a bound ME network together), or failing that the highest you have any of. In creative it uses the highest tier, or the one in your off-hand.$(br2)To $(thing)change the coils$() of a built structure, sneak-use the assembler in the air until it says $(thing)coils mode$(). Then use it on the controller: every coil is swapped for the best tier you have enough of, and the old coils come back to you. Sneak-use on the controller first to pick a tier yourself (it cycles through them, showing how many you need and have); the machine runs at the new tier at once.

pages.title: Tier 1: Superconducting Coil Block
pages.text: Tier 1 of 5. Made in a crafting table.

pages.title: Tier 2: Chronosteel Coil Block
pages.text: Tier 2 of 5. Made in a crafting table. First needed for: Bottom & Top Quarks, Glueball Core, Quark Star Core, Spacetime Alloy Ingot.

pages.title: Tier 3: Spacetime Alloy Coil Block
pages.text: Tier 3 of 5. Made in the Femtoscale Assembly Line. First needed for: Cosmic Neutronium Ingot, Higgs Boson Crystal, Hypernova Alloy Ingot, Hyperon Crystal.

pages.title: Tier 4: Cosmic Neutronium Coil Block
pages.text: Tier 4 of 5. Made in the Femtoscale Assembly Line. First needed for: Neutronium Ingot, Omnium Ingot.

pages.title: Tier 5: Transfinite Coil Block
pages.text: Tier 5 of 5. Made in the Femtoscale Assembly Line. First needed for: Omnium Ingot, Pocket Universe, Transcendent Metal Ingot, White Hole Fragment.
Every fluid flow has a Reynolds number, Re = ρvL/μ: inertia against viscosity. Below about 2300 a pipe flows in smooth layers; above it, eddies form and the pressure drop climbs.

The $(item)Laminar Flow Conduit$() puts that to work. Point a line of them the way the fluid should go: the first segment draws from the block behind it, the last fills the block in front of it, and nothing in between holds any fluid.
A smooth line of up to 16 segments passes 2,000 mB a tick. Longer lines pass less, in proportion to their length, as Poiseuille's law says: the flow through a pipe falls as 1/L.
Lift is L = ½ρv²SCₗ: the dynamic pressure of the air, times the wing's area, times its lift coefficient. A thin wing makes Cₗ = 2πα, until about 14°, where the flow tears off its top and it stalls.

The $(thing)Wind Tunnel$() lays up $(item)Aerofoil Composite$() and proves it: hold the lift coefficient between 0.9 and 1.3, the Reynolds number between two and eight million, and stay below Mach 0.6.
Above the speed of sound a duct must widen to speed a gas up. A $(item)De Laval Nozzle$() narrows to a throat, where the flow reaches Mach 1, and then flares.

Test one in the Wind Tunnel between Mach 1.6 and 3 with a small lift coefficient. Crossing Mach 1 on the way shakes the tunnel (transonic buffet): go through it quickly.$(br2)In the $(thing)MHD Generator$(), a nozzle as catalyst gives 20% more power from $(fluid)Stellar Plasma$().
Blows air past a model at a set speed, angle and pressure, and measures what it does.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 2$() machine.
pages.title: Wind Tunnel

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry, and JEI, show the pattern.

pages.name: Wind Tunnel
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports in the floor at either end). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Makes$(): Aerofoil Composite, De Laval Nozzle.

Air at density ρ and speed v flows past a model of chord c. The Reynolds number ρvc/μ decides how the boundary layer behaves, the Mach number v/a how the air compresses, and the angle of attack how much lift the model makes.
$(thing)Set$(): Airspeed v, Angle of attack α, Tunnel pressure p.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Fan gusting: the airspeed varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Transonic buffet within 0.12 of Mach 1 wears the tunnel; a lift load above 90 kPa tears the model from its mount.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): one test per run.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Effective airspeed: v·(1 + 0.02·d)$(br)Density: ρ = p/(RₛT)$(br)Reynolds number: Re = ρvc/μ$(br)Mach number: M = v/a$(br)Lift coefficient: 2πα/√(1 − M²), above Mach 1 4α/√(M² − 1)$(br)Dynamic pressure: q = ½ρv²

A rocket gains Δv = u·ln(m₀/m_f): its exhaust speed times the logarithm of its mass ratio. Low orbit needs about 9,400 m/s, more than any single stage can give, so a rocket drops its empty tanks on the way up.

Propellant is $(fluid)Liquid Oxygen$() with a fuel: Titan's $(fluid)Liquid Methane$() (methalox) or $(fluid)Liquid Hydrogen$() (hydrolox). Both liquids are made in the $(thing)Bose-Einstein Condenser$(). Hydrogen gives more exhaust speed and lifts a heavier payload, but costs twice the superfluid helium.
Fuels a two-stage rocket, counts down and flies a payload to orbit.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
pages.title: Rocket Assembly

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry, and JEI, show the pattern.

pages.name: Rocket Assembly
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports along the pad's edges). Leave the air round the rocket clear. Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Makes$(): Microgravity Crystal (from a Microgravity Lab, flown to orbit and back).

Two stages, each a hundred tonnes of propellant in twenty of tank and engine, with the payload on top. Exhaust speed comes from the specific impulse; Δv from Tsiolkovsky's equation; losses from gravity and drag on the climb.
$(thing)Set$(): Mixture ratio r, Chamber pressure P_c, Pitch-over speed.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Valve drift: the mixture ratio varies by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Chamber temperature above 3,550 K wears the engines; combustion instability above 250 bar wears them; max-Q above 45 kPa breaks the airframe up.$(br2)$(thing)Recipe window$(): a margin to orbit of zero or more.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Exhaust speed: vₑ = Iₛₚ·g₀$(br)Ideal Δv: 2·vₑ·ln((120 + m_p)/(20 + m_p))$(br)Losses: 1300 + 0.08·(v_pitch − 60)²$(br)Chamber temperature: 3700 − 180·(r − r_s)²$(br)Max-Q: 12 + 1400/v_pitch

Speed on an orbit follows vis-viva, v² = GM(2/r − 1/a). Low orbit takes about 7.7 km/s; climbing to the station's higher orbit takes a little more, and its heavy modules need hydrogen fuel to get there.

Fly four $(item)Station Modules$() on the $(thing)Rocket Assembly$() (each launch docks one, whoever flies it). Then fly a $(item)Crew Capsule$(): it comes back fuelled, and used beside the pad it takes you up.

A pressurised hub four hundred kilometres up, with the Earth turning below its windows. Inside, the air holds; outside is vacuum, and only a full pressure suit (Pressure, Heated or Frontier) keeps you breathing. Everything weighs a tenth of what it does at home, and nothing falls hard.

Its $(thing)Transfer Consoles$() send you on: home, to Titan, to the Accretion Frontier, and, with Ad Astra installed, to its planets. Sneak and use a console to choose; use it to go. Drift off the station and you fall home through re-entry.$(br2)Background radiation here is about 20 µSv/h.

Above Y 200 the Accretion Frontier's gas streams past the islands: a steady wind from the west pushes whoever is off the ground towards the east, harder the higher they go. Glide with it and it carries you; against it, it holds you back.

$(thing)Kármán Wraiths$() ride it: ribbons of wake that ripple from side to side and throw gusts at whoever comes near (mind the edges).$(br2)The $(thing)Bussard Ramscoop$() only works up here.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Vortex Filament.

$(thing)Kármán Wraith$(): a ribbon of wake in the Jet Stream. Flow past any body sheds eddies on alternate sides at a steady beat (St = fd/v ≈ 0.2): this one is nothing but the street of eddies. It sings the Aeolian tone of a wire in the wind and throws gusts at its prey.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Vortex Filament.

A ramscoop gathers ṁ = χρvA: the ionised share of the gas it sweeps through. The capture area grows with the square of the field, so the coils matter most; speed helps too, but the caught gas brings its energy in as heat.

The $(thing)Bussard Ramscoop$() only runs high in the Accretion Frontier (Y 200 or more). It makes $(fluid)Molecular Cloud$() by the bucketful, far cheaper than the Interstellar Scoop, and with a strong enough flow a trickle of $(fluid)Deuterium$().
Nine shrinking rings of Funnel Coil, a lattice frame and an ion collector at the throat.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 3$() machine.
pages.title: Bussard Ramscoop

pages.text: $(thing)Made on the Extreme Assembly Table$() (it is also a crafting table). The recipe pages at the end of this entry, and JEI, show the pattern.

pages.name: Bussard Ramscoop
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports under the collector). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().
$(thing)Makes$(): Molecular Cloud, Deuterium. Only in the Accretion Frontier, at Y 200 or more.

Ionised gas follows the field lines; the funnel coils bend them into a cone and the ions with them. The capture radius grows with the field, the caught mass with the ionised fraction, the gas density, the speed and the area.
$(thing)Set$(): Coil field B, Ioniser power P, Ram speed v.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Coil ripple: the field varies by ±1%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): above 12 T the coils quench; above 80 MW the ionisers arc (wear); more than 400 W of caught kinetic energy overheats the throat (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): output follows the mass flow, up to four times a full run.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Capture radius: R_c = 40·B m$(br)Ionised fraction: χ = P/(P + 20 MW)$(br)Mass flow: ṁ = χρvπR_c²$(br)Funnel heating: ½ṁv²

The deepest sea floor there is, eleven kilometres down: basins and trenches of $(item)Oceanic Basalt$() under a blanket of $(item)Hadal Ooze$(), pillows of lava heaped along the old fissures,, and fields of hot vents where life gathers. Dive from under water in a deep ocean, below Y 40, in a $(item)Bathyscaphe$(); use it again to surface.

A thousand atmospheres: without a full pressure suit (Pressure, Heated Pressure or Frontier) the water crushes you. You need air too: the sphere's lasts half a minute; an $(item)Oxygen Rebreather$() keeps you breathing.$(br2)Background radiation is almost nothing: eleven kilometres of water stop the cosmic rays.

$(thing)No light$() has ever reached the trench. Your eyes see nothing; a torch or lantern lights only the few blocks round it. $(thing)Night Vision$() lifts the dark, but the water is thick with marine snow and you see only a dozen blocks. What you see from far off is the glow of the things that live here.$(br2)Swim up through the surface and the current carries you home; fall through the floor and you go down with the plate into the $(thing)Planetary Interior$().
$(thing)Hadal Anglerfish$(): hangs still over the trench floor with its lure lit, and lunges at whatever comes close to the light.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Anglerfish Lure.

$(thing)Siphonophore Colony$(): a float, swimming bells and a long stinging stem, drifting slowly through the trench. Whatever brushes the stem is poisoned and slowed.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Nematocyst Cluster.
Pressure under water grows by ρgh: about one atmosphere every ten metres. At the bottom of the Challenger Deep, 10,935 m down, that is more than a thousand.

A deep-water swell carries ρg²H²T/64π watts per metre of front. The $(thing)Wave Energy Converter$() rides it in any ocean biome: set the float's diameter, the take-off's damping (half is best) and its natural period (match the swell's).
