$(thing)Limits$(): too wide a float slams on every crest (damage); too little damping lets it swing into its end stops (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Wave power: 0.49·H²·T kW/m$(br)Capture width ratio: 4c(1 − c)·resonance$(br)Power: P·D·CWR·η$(br)Stroke: H/2c

A thunderstorm runs on CAPE, the energy warm, moist air gains as it rises: its updraft reaches √(2·CAPE), and the flash rate climbs as the cube of the updraft. The $(thing)Storm Chamber$() makes one in a tower and fixes the air's nitrogen with its lightning into $(fluid)Nitric Acid$(), with no ammonia and no catalyst (the Birkeland-Eyde route).

$(thing)Set$(): Surface temperature, Humidity, Wind shear.$(br2)$(thing)Limits$(): an updraft above 40 m/s grows giant hail (damage); shear times CAPE above 12,000 spins up a tornado (damage).$(br2)Out at sea in a thunderstorm, over warm water, a $(thing)Storm Elemental$() may form.

Magma's viscosity falls as e^(E/RT) with temperature: hot basalt flows, cool silica-rich magma jams and explodes. The $(thing)Geothermal Plant$() boils water on $(fluid)Basaltic Magma$() from the Planetary Interior and makes power, basalt and $(fluid)Sulfur Dioxide$().

$(thing)Set$(): Water flow, Turbine pressure, Condenser temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Limits$(): too little water burns out the boiler (damage); too much wets the steam (wear); above 80 bar, over pressure (damage).
Ice flows by Glen's law, ε̇ = Aτⁿ, and keeps every year's snow as a layer. The $(thing)Ice Core Drill$() cuts $(item)Ice Cores$() in icy or snowy biomes, far cheaper than the Climate Engine's.

$(thing)Set$(): Rotation speed, Weight on bit, Drill fluid temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Recipe window$(): the bit at −8 °C or colder.$(br2)$(thing)Limits$(): above −5 °C the core melts (wear); more than 40 kN fractures it (damage); fluid below −40 °C jams the string (wear).

$(thing)Storm Elemental$(): a thunderstorm cell come to life, only over warm sea in a thunderstorm (at most one near you). It hangs high over its prey and strikes it with lightning; it never starts fires. It dissipates when the storm passes.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Fulgurite.

Capillarity lifts water h = 2γcosθ/ρgr: well under a metre in a xylem vessel. The rest of the way up a tree it is pulled, by evaporation from the leaves, under tension. The $(thing)Hydroponic Tower$() grows crops on a turning carousel of trays without soil, and $(item)Xylem Fibre$() from saplings.

$(thing)Set$(): Light, Nutrient EC, Root-zone temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Limits$(): EC above 3.5 burns the leaf tips (wear); root zone above 28 °C rots the roots (damage); light above 1500 shuts photosynthesis down (wear).$(br2)Fed $(fluid)Auxin$() and $(fluid)Gibberellin$(), every crop yields twice as much.

The $(thing)Phytotron$() sets day length, temperature and CO₂ to the hour. Under long days (14 h or more) shoots make $(fluid)Auxin$(); seeds kept through long nights (10 h or more) make $(fluid)Gibberellin$().

Each generation moves R = h²S: the response is the heritability times how far the kept parents stand from the field's average. The $(thing)Breeding Bench$() starts three $(item)Engineered Seed$() lines from wheat (Yield, Hardiness and Glow) and takes each one generation further per run. Every generation asks for a bigger response. JEI shows the recipes.

$(thing)Set$(): Fraction kept, Field uniformity, Population.$(br2)$(thing)Limits$(): fewer than 10 parents and the line inbreeds (wear).$(br2)In the $(thing)Hydroponic Tower$(): Yield seeds grow more wheat (from III with Living Soil); Hardiness II grows in orbit and on Titan; Glow II bears glowing berries.

Uptake follows v = Vc/(K + c): a root takes up a nutrient faster the more of it there is, until its carriers are all busy. A good soil keeps the concentration up where the roots are. $(item)Biochar$() (made in the Sintering Press) holds water and nutrients for centuries, $(item)Humus$() and $(item)Mycorrhizal Inoculant$() (made in the Mycelium Bed) feed and extend the roots, and the three together make $(item)Living Soil$(), which the high-yield seed lines need. JEI shows the recipes.

Browning runs at k = A·e^(−E/RT): a little hotter and the crust forms much faster. The $(thing)Fermenter$() bakes $(item)Field Rations$(), a dense loaf that keeps for months and leaves you $(thing)Well Fed$() (two more hearts for ten minutes). JEI shows the recipe.

Leaves fix carbon in proportion to the light until their enzymes are all busy; roots take up nutrients the same way, saturating with the solution's strength; and both work best in a warm, not hot, root zone.
$(thing)Set$(): Light, Nutrient EC, Root-zone temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Lamp flicker: the light varies by ±3%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): above 3.5 mS/cm the leaf tips burn (wear); above 1500 µmol/m²s photosynthesis shuts down (wear); above 28 °C the roots rot (damage).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): output follows growth against the rated amount.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Photosynthesis: P = P_max·I/(I + 300)$(br)Uptake: EC/(EC + 0.8)$(br)Temperature: e^(−((T − 22)/6)²)$(br)Growth = P·uptake·f(T)

Plants time their hormones by the length of the night, not the day. The chamber sets the day length, the temperature and the CO₂; growth rises with CO₂ and saturates, and falls off either side of 24 °C.
$(thing)Set$(): Day length, Temperature, CO₂.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Timer drift: the day length varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): above 35 °C the plants suffer heat stress (damage); above 1500 ppm CO₂ the scrubbers wear.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): output follows growth against the rated amount.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Night length: 24 − L$(br)CO₂ effect: C/(C + 400)$(br)Growth = CO₂ effect·e^(−((T − 24)/7)²)·min(1, L/14)

Keep the top fraction p of the plants: they sit i standard deviations above the mean, i growing as p shrinks. Of that difference, only the heritable share h² is passed on, and a uniform field lets more of it show.
$(thing)Set$(): Fraction kept, Field uniformity, Population.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Weather: heritability varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): fewer than 10 parents kept and the line inbreeds (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): one generation per run.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Intensity: i = 0.8 + 0.4·ln(0.5/p)$(br)Heritability: h² = 0.2 + 0.6u$(br)Response: R = h²i$(br)Parents: N·p

Every atom counted, parent or daughter, sharpens the age by counting statistics: the error on a count of N is √N. A young sample has few daughters, an old one few parents left; either way the scarcer one sets the precision.
$(thing)Set$(): Beam current, Counting time, Sample mass.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Beam drift: the count varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): more than 3000 µA·min a run wears the ion source; more than 100 µA·mg overheats the target (stops).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): counting past 20 minutes slows the run.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Parent left: f = e^(−t/τ)$(br)Counts: N = 33·I·t·m$(br)Uncertainty: σ = τ(1 − f)√(1/(N(1 − f)) + 1/(Nf))

pages.title: Dating Spectrometer
pages.text: Age from atoms: t = τ·ln(1 + D/P). The $(thing)Dating Spectrometer$() counts parent and daughter atoms one by one; count enough of them and the age comes out precise enough to use.

$(item)Fossil Fragments$() are dated by carbon-14 (30 thousand years, to within 250), $(item)Raw Amber$() by potassium-40 (310 million, to within 4 million) and $(item)Stromatolite Fragments$() by rubidium-87 (3.5 billion, to within 60 million). Each becomes a dated sample: $(item)Dated Bone$(), $(item)Dated Amber$() and $(item)Dated Stromatolite$(), made in the Dating Spectrometer.

pages.title: Fossil Ore
pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y 0 and 80. Gives Fossil Fragment when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in rare, small veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Amber Ore
pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y 24 and 96. Gives Raw Amber when mined with stone pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in rare, small veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

pages.title: Stromatolite Ore
pages.text: Found in the Overworld, between Y -64 and 0. Gives Stromatolite Fragment when mined with iron pickaxe or better.
$(thing)Found$(): in rare, small veins through the Overworld (mine it for its drop).

Old DNA comes in short fragments, and few of them; the bone's surface is coated in modern DNA. Bleach strips the surface but costs some of the old DNA; PCR copies the library enough to read, but copies the contamination too; and reading more than the library holds only reads the same molecules again.
$(thing)Set$(): Reads, PCR cycles, Bleach wash.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Run quality: the coverage varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): more reads than the amplified library holds stops it; more than 8% modern DNA in the reads wears the lab.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): one genome per run.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Kept: k = e^(−b/40)$(br)Distinct reads: N = U(1 − e^(−R/U))$(br)Coverage: C = N·L·e^(−30/L)/G$(br)Contamination: c₀e^(−b/10)(1 + n/20)

A growing body must be fed its upkeep and a little more: upkeep grows as mass to the three-quarters. Grow it at its body temperature, and give it the oxygen it breathes; an insect from the Carboniferous needs far more than today's air.
$(thing)Set$(): Feed rate (log scale), Vat temperature, Oxygen.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): its upkeep varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): feed over 1.5× upkeep fouls the tank (wear); over 44 °C cooks the tissue (damage); less oxygen than it needs stops it; over 38% oxygen poisons the tissue (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): one creature per run.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Upkeep: B = 3.4·M^(3/4) W$(br)Feed ratio: f = F/B$(br)Growth: e^(−((T − T₀)/4)²)·e^(−((f − 1.1)/0.3)²)

pages.title: Ancient DNA Lab
pages.text: Coverage: C = NL/G. Ancient DNA comes in fragments fifty letters long, mixed with modern contamination; read enough of them and every part of the genome is covered several times over. The $(thing)Ancient DNA Lab$() makes the $(item)Mammoth Genome$() and the $(item)Meganeura Genome$() from dated samples, and a Mammoth Genome from Mammoth Ivory far more cheaply: tusk dentine keeps DNA better than bone. JEI shows the recipes.

pages.title: Revival Vat
pages.text: Upkeep: B = B₀M^(3/4). The $(thing)Revival Vat$() is a multiblock of 563 blocks: a great amniotic tank, four nursery tanks and the lines that feed them. It grows a revived creature from its genome until it can be carried away in a capsule ($(item)Mammoth Capsule$(), $(item)Meganeura Capsule$()). A Dated Stromatolite's cyanobacteria oxygenate its broth. JEI shows the recipes.
Use a capsule on the ground to let the creature go. Revived creatures are $(thing)wild$(): they cannot be tamed, bred or ridden, and they never spawn by themselves.

pages.name: Revival Vat
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports in the base rim). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Woolly Mammoth$(): Six tonnes of Ice Age grazer, brought back from a thirty-thousand-year-old bone. It wanders, grazes and keeps with its herd. It never starts a fight, but hurt one and every mammoth nearby charges, tusks first.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Mammoth Wool; Mammoth Ivory when you bring it down. Never found in the wild: released from a Mammoth Capsule.

$(thing)Meganeura$(): A griffinfly of the Carboniferous, seventy centimetres across, from an age when the air held a third more oxygen. It patrols the place it was let go, darting and hovering, and flees fast and high if struck.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Meganeura Wing. Never found in the wild: released from a Meganeura Capsule.

$(thing)Dig Sites$(): abandoned excavations in the Overworld's deserts, badlands, savannas, plains and stony shores, with fossil and amber in their walls and a cache of finds.$(br2)$(thing)Greenhouse Ruins$(): broken research greenhouses in plains, meadows and forests, with a cache of the seed lines they were breeding. Both are rare.

The spike runs on: λ = √(r_m/r_i). The $(thing)Neural Culture Array$() grows neurons in a dish and coaxes glial cells to wrap their axons in myelin, making $(item)Myelinated Axons$(). A culture catches what any culture catches: keep it clean.
pages.title: Neural Culture Array

pages.text: The lobes a $(item)Dream Polyp$() drops from a Dreaming Colony grow back into a Neural Organoid in the same array. JEI shows the recipes.

Δw = η·x·y. The $(thing)Synapse Trainer$() shows a lattice of synapses a pattern until it has learnt it. The $(item)Synaptic Lattice$() is an upgrade: fitted to a machine, +10% products, and precision falls off a third slower. JEI shows the recipe.
pages.title: Synapse Trainer

pages.text: S = k·ln(I/I₀). The $(thing)Psychophysics Booth$() trains a cultured retina to see faint flashes without seeing things that are not there: a $(item)Rhodopsin Retina$().
pages.title: Psychophysics Booth

pages.text: The $(item)Low-Light Visor$() (made by crafting) gives night vision while worn on the head; in the $(thing)Hadal Trench$() it sees the deep clearly, far into the water.

H = log₂N bits a symbol. $(item)Glyph Tablets$() are found in the caches of $(thing)Library Ruins$(), in the Overworld's forests, taigas and jungles. The $(thing)Decipherment Desk$() counts their symbols until they can be read.
pages.title: Decipherment Desk

pages.text: A tablet read gives $(item)Lexicon Fragments$(); enough of them give the $(item)Universal Grammar$(), made at the Decipherment Desk. Guess the alphabet right and count enough text for the context you read in.

Φ: integrated and differentiated. The $(thing)Connectome Array$() is a dome of 469 blocks: glial scaffold threaded with axon tracts, relays where they cross, and a ring of relays turning inside. It maps a network into $(item)Engrams$().
pages.title: Connectome Array

pages.text: Sixteen Engrams carry enough of a mind for the $(thing)Matrioshka Brain$() to run as a $(item)Superintelligence Core$(), far more cheaply than growing one. JEI shows the recipe.

pages.name: Connectome Array
pages.text: Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$(). Interface Ports go in the front of the floor.
P = π²EI/L². The $(thing)Load Test Rig$() loads a beam until it bows and rates it: a $(item)Rated I-Beam$() has a safety factor of two to four, no more, no less.
pages.title: Load Test Rig

pages.text: E = V_f·E_f + V_m·E_m. The $(thing)Composite Layup Press$() makes $(item)Carbon-Fibre$() and $(item)Nanotube Composites$(), and later the $(item)Tether Spool$() and $(item)Shkadov Mirror Film$(). Lay the plies along the load and do not pack the fibre past 62%.
pages.title: Composite Layup Press

pages.text: V = k·W·L/H. The $(thing)Tribometer$() qualifies a diamond-like carbon $(item)Wear Coating$(): an upgrade that makes a machine's catalysts wear half as fast.
pages.title: Tribometer

pages.text: E = E⁰ + 0.0296·log c. The $(thing)Corrosion Cell$() holds a sample on Pourbaix's map: in the passive window it makes $(item)Passivated Plate$(); below the immunity line, in salt water, it qualifies $(item)Sacrificial Anodes$().
pages.title: Corrosion Cell

pages.text: $(thing)Rust Mites$() eat the charge of machines. A live anode within twelve blocks draws them off: they eat it instead, four bites, and leave $(item)Rust Flakes$(). Flakes make passivated plate more cheaply.

T = e^(ρgR²/σr). The $(thing)Space Elevator$() is 770 blocks: an anchor platform with four buttresses, a tether forty-eight blocks tall under a counterweight, and a climber that rides it. It takes Crew Capsules, Microgravity Labs and Station Modules to orbit on power alone.
pages.title: Space Elevator

pages.name: Space Elevator
pages.text: Interface Ports in the middle of each side of the platform. A fuelled Crew Capsule can be flown from beside it, as from a Rocket Assembly.

a = ω²r. The $(thing)O'Neill Cylinder$() is 1001 blocks: a hull with three window strips, turning on its bearings over two cradles. Seed it with a Stable Ecosystem and it grows six; it also feeds its colonists, in bulk.
pages.title: O'Neill Cylinder

pages.name: O'Neill Cylinder
pages.text: Interface Ports in the cradles and keel.

F = f·L/c. The $(thing)Stellar Engine$() is 3750 blocks: a mirror held up by a captive star's light on one side of it, Caplan jets on the other. It runs on Stellar Cores and gives four times a Dyson Array's power for each, with stellar plasma skimmed off by the jets.
pages.title: Stellar Engine

pages.text: A Shkadov thruster, 3750 blocks: a great mirror dish behind the star, held on ribs from a spine, and a ring of Caplan jets ahead of it that turns as it burns. The thrust leaves through the ring.

pages.name: Stellar Engine
pages.text: Interface Ports either side of the controller, at the front of the spine.
Its signature material is the $(item)Stellar Wind Condensate$(): made here and nowhere else.$(br2)Made in $(item)Stellar Engine$().

$(thing)Dreaming Colony$(): A knot of a few hundred neurons grown into one floating mind, dreaming aloud. It learns how it is fought: the more often one kind of blow hurts it, the less that kind does (down to half), and it keeps further from fighters who close in and nearer to those who shoot. Every few seconds it pulses, dazing whoever is within seven blocks. Found in Inner Space's Neural Cortex.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Dream Polyp.

$(thing)Rust Mite$(): An iron-eating pest with a shell of flaking rust. It feeds on the charge of machines within sixteen blocks, a bite a second; a live Sacrificial Anode nearby draws it off, and it eats that instead. It shies from players and bites only when struck. Found in Titan, the Antiverse and the derelict orbital rings.$(br2)$(thing)Drops$(): Rust Flakes.

$(thing)Library Ruins$(): sunken halls of glyph stone in the Overworld's forests, taigas and jungles, their shelves still full of tablets in the old glyph alphabet, with a cache of what the readers left. Rare.
$(thing)Derelict Rings$(): arcs of old spinning habitats drifting in low Earth orbit, far from the station, overrun by Rust Mites. Their crews' caches are still aboard.

A sixth region of $(thing)Inner Space$(): a floor of $(item)Grey Matter$() over $(item)White Matter$(), where neurons grow as tall as trees, their cell bodies and synapses glowing. $(thing)Dreaming Colonies$() drift there.
A spike runs down an axon faster the thicker it is, and a hundred times faster once myelin wraps it. Too few sodium channels and the cells never fire; too many and they die of it.
$(thing)Set$(): Sodium channels, Axon diameter, Myelin wraps.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): the culture drifts: speed varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): under 40 mS/cm² the cells cannot fire (stops); over 160 they die (wear); more myelin than the axon can hold wears it.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more channels, faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Myelination: m = min(1, wraps/40)$(br)Speed: v = (6D·m + √D·(1 − m))·√(g/120)$(br)Length: λ = 0.5·√(D·(1 + wraps))
Each showing of the pattern strengthens the synapses it uses. Learn too fast and the weights run away; train too long and the lattice wears.
$(thing)Set$(): Learning rate, Epochs, Activity.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): noise: what is learnt varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): η·x² over 0.25 runs away (stops); over 400 epochs wears.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more epochs, slower.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Step: Δw = η·x²$(br)Learnt: w = 1 − e^(−η·x²·N)
Brighter flashes stand further out of the noise. Set the criterion high to keep false alarms down, but high enough and you miss the flashes too.
$(thing)Set$(): Flash intensity, Criterion, Trials.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): adaptation: sensitivity varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): too bright a flash bleaches the retina (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more trials, slower.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sensitivity: d′ = 0.5·ln(I/I₀)$(br)Hits: H = Φ(d′ − c)$(br)False alarms: F = Φ(−c)
Guess the alphabet's size from the symbol counts, then read in context. Longer contexts read more but need far more text.
$(thing)Set$(): Corpus, Alphabet guess, Context.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): scribal errors: the reading varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): under 30 symbols of text there is nothing to count (stops).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more text, slower.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Fit: e^(−((k − K)/0.15K)²)$(br)Coverage: 1 − e^(−N/(20·k^g))$(br)Deciphered: fit × coverage × g/(g + 0.5)
A mind is integrated and differentiated at once: connected enough that every part affects every other, split enough into modules that they do different things.
$(thing)Set$(): Neurons (log), Connectivity, Modularity.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): noise: Φ varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 20 MW wears; a dense unmodular net seizes (damage).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more Φ, faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Integration: f = (1 − e^(−50p))·e^(−4p)$(br)Φ = log n · 4Q(1 − Q) · f
Deeper sections are stiffer by the cube of their depth; longer columns buckle at the inverse square of their length. Rate a beam between two and four: strong enough, and no heavier.
$(thing)Set$(): Section depth, Flange thickness, Length.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): imperfection: the load varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 250 MPa the steel yields (stops); over 400 kg wears the rig.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): lighter beams faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)I = (b·h³ − (b − t/2)(h − 2t)³)/12$(br)P = π²EI/L²$(br)Safety factor = P/load
Along the fibres a composite is stiff; across them it is only resin. Fibres packed past 62% leave voids.
$(thing)Set$(): Fibre fraction, Ply angle, Cure temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): ply wrinkles: consolidation varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): under 110 °C the resin does not cure (stops); over 190 °C it chars (damage).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): hotter cures faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)E = V_f·E_f + (1 − V_f)·E_m$(br)E(θ) = E·cos⁴θ + E_m·(1 − cos⁴θ)$(br)Specific stiffness = E·q/ρ
A coating lasts as long as its thickness over its wear rate. Test it at the duty it must stand, but not so hard the contact overheats.
$(thing)Set$(): Load, Sliding speed, Coating thickness.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): debris: life varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): under 200 W the test is too gentle (stops); over 400 W of friction wears; past 8 µm the coating spalls.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): harder tests faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Life: τ = 5556·h·H/(20·k·W·v) hours
Below −0.62 V iron cannot dissolve; between pH 9 and 13 it covers itself in oxide and stops; chloride breaks that film above the pitting potential.
$(thing)Set$(): pH, Potential, Chloride.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): oxygen: the rate varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): below −1.2 V hydrogen embrittles the steel (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): salty water slower.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Immunity: E < −0.62 V$(br)Pitting: E_p = 0.3 − 0.15·(log Cl + 4)$(br)Rate: e^((E + 0.62)/0.06) where not immune or passive
The tether must taper by at least e^(48.4/specific strength), or it snaps; much more is wasted mass. Climbers ride on beamed power.
$(thing)Set$(): Taper ratio, Climber speed, Payload.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): wind and tides: the load varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): a taper below what is needed snaps the tether (stops); over 50 MW of beam overheats the climber (damage).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): faster climbers, faster lifts.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Taper needed: e^(48.4/S)$(br)Margin: taper/needed$(br)Power: P = m·g·v
Spin it for one gee on its floor, slowly enough not to sicken its colonists, without tearing its hull.
$(thing)Set$(): Spin, Radius, Hull thickness.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): wobble: gravity varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 2 rpm the colonists are sick (wear); hoop stress over the hull's strength tears it (stops).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): bigger habitats grow more.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)a = ω²r$(br)Hoop stress = ρω²r²·(1 + 200/t)
Cover more of the star's sky with mirror for more thrust, and fire the jets for more again; but a mirror too heavy falls in, and too close it melts.
$(thing)Set$(): Mirror coverage, Mirror areal density, Jet fraction.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): flares: thrust varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): heavier than 0.78 g/m² the mirror falls (stops); over 1500 K it melts (damage); jets over 90% strip the star (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more thrust, more power.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)F = f·(1 + j)·L/c$(br)T = 394/√(1 − f) K
f = n·v/2L. The $(thing)Resonance Chamber$() shakes raw iron and gold apart at their own notes: fourteen nuggets from each raw ore. It also tunes amethyst into $(item)Resonant Shards$().
pages.title: Resonance Chamber

pages.text: Every three to seven days a $(thing)geomagnetic storm$() strikes the Overworld for five minutes. It changes no block and harms no one, but every console and multiblock there runs at $(thing)70%$() while it lasts, and aurorae hang in the night sky.
r = (B₀²/2μ₀ρv²)^(1/6). The $(thing)Heliograph$() proves a $(item)Faraday Mesh$() against a design storm; fitted as an upgrade, the machine runs at full speed through storms.
pages.title: Heliograph

pages.text: λ = ln(d₁/d₀)/t. The $(thing)Chaos Controller$() drives the Lorenz flow into chaos and holds one orbit with small nudges: a $(item)Strange Attractor$().
pages.title: Chaos Controller

pages.text: w = p − m. The $(thing)Knot Loom$() ties $(item)Molecular Knots$() (trefoils) and $(item)Knotted Polymer$() (pentafoils). A Tether Spool of knotted polymer costs less than one of aramid.
pages.title: Knot Loom

pages.text: P = 56ρ³(1 − ρ)⁵. The $(thing)Automaton Lattice$() grows $(item)Von Neumann Constructors$() at the edge of chaos, and with them $(item)Quine Replicators$() far more cheaply than the Nanofabricator.
pages.title: Automaton Lattice

pages.text: ε = 2^(−k). The $(thing)Certificate Verifier$() makes $(item)Zero-Knowledge Proofs$(), and compiles them into $(item)Grover Oracles$() for the Quantum Computer.
pages.title: Certificate Verifier

pages.text: S = (N/2)/((π/4)√N). The $(thing)Quantum Computer$() is 613 blocks: a cryostat with a chandelier of dilution stages and its qubits at the tip. Each Grover Oracle it runs shortens its owner's current study by $(thing)fifteen minutes$(). It runs only while you are studying something.
pages.title: Quantum Computer

pages.name: Quantum Computer
pages.text: Interface Ports in the front of the floor ring.

E = D^n/(EC₅₀^n + D^n). The $(thing)Dose-Response Assay$() finds a dose that works without harm and lasts until the next. Its medicines cure, then guard for three minutes; a second dose within two minutes is an overdose.
pages.title: Dose-Response Assay

pages.text: I = I₀·e^(−μx). The $(thing)CT Scanner$() is 257 blocks: a gantry ring that turns round a couch. It scans fossils and amber into $(item)Tomograms$(); with one, the Ancient DNA Lab needs half the dated samples for a genome.
pages.title: CT Scanner

pages.name: CT Scanner
pages.text: Interface Ports at the front foot of the gantry.
Every bar rings at its own notes. Cut the sample to a length, then play its note exactly: off by more than a hair and it barely answers.
$(thing)Set$(): Drive frequency, Sample length, Drive amplitude.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): temperature: the tuning drifts by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 18 µm the transducer cracks (wear); strain over 800 µm turns the ore to dust (stops).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): higher notes faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)f₁ = 50·v/L kHz$(br)Response = 1/√(1 + (2Q·detuning)²), Q = 50$(br)Strain = amplitude × Q × response
A Faraday Mesh is proved against a severe storm: a fast wind with its field turned south, pushing the magnetopause in.
$(thing)Set$(): Wind speed, Wind density, Field southward.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): gusts: pressure varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 60 nPa is beyond any storm on record (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): faster winds faster.
Heat the cell past ρ = 24.74 for chaos, then nudge it often enough, and hard enough, to hold one orbit.
$(thing)Set$(): Rayleigh number, Nudge size, Nudge interval.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): noise: chaos grows by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): nudges over 0.8 knock it off the attractor (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): frequent nudges are slow.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)λ = 0.3·√(ρ − 24.74)$(br)Control = e^(−λτ/20)·min(1, ε/(0.1λ + 0.02))
Set the templates to the knot wanted, enough of them to catch the strands but not so many they tangle, warm but not hot.
$(thing)Set$(): Crossings, Template concentration, Temperature.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): impurities: yield varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): under 10 °C nothing moves (stops); over 8 mM tangles (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): warmer faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Yield = match · c/(c + 0.5) · e^(−(T − 60)⁺/20) · e^(−0.15(n − 3))
Set the rule at the edge of chaos, make the lattice big enough to hold a constructor, and seed it near a third full.
$(thing)Set$(): Langton's λ, Lattice size, Seed density.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): bit flips: complexity varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 10^7.5 cells overheats (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): bigger lattices slower.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Complexity = e^(−((λ − 0.27)/0.06)²)$(br)Replication = complexity × min(1, log cells − 4) × (1 − |ρ − 0.3|)
Each round halves a cheat's chance; nine nines of certainty take thirty rounds. Keep the problem small enough to check quickly.
$(thing)Set$(): Problem size, Rounds.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): noise: soundness varies by ±0.5%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): checks over 30 s wear the verifier.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): quicker checks faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Soundness = k·log₁₀2$(br)Verify time = n²k/10⁶ s
Find a dose high enough to work, low enough not to harm, and an interval short enough that it still works before the next.
$(thing)Set$(): Dose, Hill coefficient, Interval.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): patient variation: effect varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): toxicity over 30% wears the assay.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): longer intervals faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)E = D^n/(EC₅₀^n + D^n)$(br)Toxicity = D^n/(TD₅₀^n + D^n)$(br)Trough: D·e^(−0.693τ/t½)
More qubits search more, but the circuit grows as √N and every gate must be faultless enough for it all to stay coherent.
$(thing)Set$(): Qubits, Temperature, Gate error.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): cosmic rays: fidelity varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 80 mK the qubits decohere (stops); under 7 mK strains the fridge (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): bigger speed-ups faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Depth = (π/4)·2^(n/2)$(br)Fidelity = e^(−depth·ε·(1 + T/20))
Take enough views for the detector's pixels (π/2 per pixel), and enough dose for a quiet image, but not so much it damages the specimen.
$(thing)Set$(): Views, Detector pixels, Dose.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): scatter: quality varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 80 mGy damages the specimen (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): fewer views faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Sampling = N_views/(π/2·N_pixels)$(br)Quality = sampling × (1 − e^(−dose/10))$(br)Resolution = 500/N_pixels mm

A $(thing)Buried Tell$() is a low mound of soil in the plains, savannas, deserts and badlands of the Overworld: a town rebuilt on its own ruins for thousands of years. Grey $(thing)ash layers$() mark the nights its towns burnt, and the stubs of $(thing)mud-brick walls$() stand in every layer. A trial trench cuts into one flank.

Brush $(item)Suspicious Tell Soil$() for potsherds, corroded artefacts and flints, and $(item)Suspicious Ash$() for charred beams and slag. Dig them instead and the find is lost. Most lie hidden in the mound: the $(item)Survey Radar$() shows where.
pages.title: The finds

pages.text: d = c·t/(2√εr). The $(thing)Radar Survey Bench$() tunes a $(item)Survey Radar$(): use it and every buried find within 16 blocks glows where its echo came from, the nearest reported by distance, direction and depth.
pages.title: Radar Survey Bench

pages.text: A = De/Ḋ. The $(thing)Luminescence Reader$() dates $(item)Ancient Potsherds$() and $(item)Burnt Flint$() into $(item)Dated Potsherds$().
pages.title: Luminescence Reader

pages.text: t = r·√((n − 2)/(1 − r²)). The $(thing)Tree-Ring Correlator$() cross-dates $(item)Charred Beams$() into a $(item)Tree-Ring Chronology$().
pages.title: Tree-Ring Correlator

pages.text: C = C₀·e^(−π²Dt/L²). The $(thing)Conservation Bath$() draws the chloride out of a $(item)Corroded Artefact$(): a $(item)Stabilised Artefact$() and some rust flakes.
pages.title: Conservation Bath

pages.text: f = (R − Rb)/(Ra − Rb). The $(thing)Isotope Provenancer$() reads where a $(item)Stabilised Artefact$()'s metal was mined: a $(item)Provenanced Artefact$().
pages.title: Isotope Provenancer

pages.text: x = 2√(Dt). The $(thing)Bloomery Shaft$() is 452 blocks: a tapering clay shaft, its bellows pumping air through six tuyeres. From $(item)Slag Cakes$(), raw iron and charcoal it makes $(item)Bloomery Steel$(), which the Load Test Rig rolls into I-beams more cheaply than iron.
pages.title: Bloomery Shaft

Z = f·B/d. The $(thing)Photogrammetry Gantry$() is 670 blocks: a camera bridge on rails over a stepped trench. It brings the dated, provenanced finds together into an $(item)Excavation Record$(). In the Chrono Loom, two records make Arrow of Time Shards without negentropy cells or imaginary units.

pages.text: Interface Ports in the front face of the platform, under the controller and at the other corner.
A Survey Radar needs to see a pot (a tenth of a metre) at least eight metres down. Higher frequencies see finer, lower ones deeper; more power reaches further.
$(thing)Set$(): Antenna frequency, Pulse power.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): damp: resolution varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 80 W the transmitter overheats (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): higher frequencies faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)v = 0.3/√εr m/ns$(br)Resolution = λ/4 = 75/(f√εr) m$(br)Reach = 30·√(P/10)/(1 + f/400) m
Preheat to clear the unstable traps but not the ones that keep time, and light the grains bright enough to read the dose precisely.
$(thing)Set$(): Preheat, Stimulation.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): background: recovery varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 70 mW/cm² bleaches the reference (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): brighter faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Recovery = (1 − e^(−(T − 160)/40))·e^(−(T − 260)⁺/30)$(br)Uncertainty = 0.03 + 2/S$(br)Age = De/Ḋ
Slide the beam to the offset where the patterns match, detrend gently, and compare enough rings for t to pass 6.
$(thing)Set$(): Overlap, Offset, Detrending.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): charring: correlation varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): shorter overlaps faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Match = e^(−((lag − L₀)/2)²)$(br)r = ρ·match·(1 − e^(−s/30))·e^(−s/600)$(br)t = r·√((n − 2)/(1 − r²))
Soak long enough, warm and alkaline enough, to bring the chloride under 100 ppm; but not so hot or strong that the bath attacks the find.
$(thing)Set$(): Alkali, Temperature, Soak.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): old salts: chloride varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 1.6% alkali or 60 °C wears the bath.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): shorter soaks faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)D = 0.3·(1 + c)·e^((T − 20)/30) mm²/day$(br)C = C₀·e^(−π²Dt/L²)
Run the plasma near 1.25 kW and count long enough that the two sources lie more than 25 σ apart.
$(thing)Set$(): Plasma power, Acquisition.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): drift: precision varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 1.55 kW erodes the cones (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): shorter acquisitions faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)σ = 0.0002·√(60/t)·(1 + 3|P − 1.25|)$(br)f = (R − Rb)/(Ra − Rb)$(br)Separation = (Ra − Rb)/σ
Hot enough for the carbon to soak in two millimetres or more, never so hot the bloom melts, with charcoal enough for steel.
$(thing)Set$(): Furnace heat, Charcoal, Smelt.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): draught: depth varies by ±1%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 1450 °C the bloom melts (stops); over 2.8 charcoal per ore chokes (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): shorter smelts faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)D = 2.3×10⁻⁵·e^(−148 kJ/RT) m²/s$(br)x = 2√(Dt)$(br)Carbon = 0.9·(1 − e^(−x/2))·min(1.2, c/1.5) %
Four metres above the trench, choose a lens long enough for 0.3 mm pixels and a baseline wide enough for 2 mm depth, but not so wide the views stop matching.
$(thing)Set$(): Baseline, Focal length, Overlap.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): vibration: precision varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): base to height over 0.8 wears the matcher.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): less overlap faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Pixel = 4·Z/f mm$(br)σZ = Z²·σd/(f·B)$(br)B/Z between 0.1 and 0.8

The endgame has four tiers, and the $(thing)Field Syntheses$() are the first: one per field, each made by a chain of that field's machines. Cosmic engineering (the Dyson Array, Stellar Engine, Matrioshka Brain, Universe Forge) needs two plain syntheses per recipe; beyond physics needs an $(thing)Alpha$() one; the final tier a $(thing)Beta$() one, and all seven between its machines. The $(l)Consilience Core$() takes a $(thing)Gamma$() of every one.

Nine Field Syntheses of one level make one of the next in a crafting grid: Alpha, Beta, Gamma and on through the Greek letters, then Aleph, Bet and on through the Hebrew. The Perennial Catalyst Matrix is an endgame catalyst: it never wears.

Physics: Cyclotron, Synchrotron, Femtoscale Assembly Line. Chemistry: Catalyst Formulator, Framework Assembler, Chelation Column, Regeneration Kiln. Mathematics: Proof Assistant, Certificate Verifier, Automaton Lattice. Biology: Gene Sequencer, Ancient DNA Lab, Revival Vat.
pages.title: The chains (1)

pages.text: Mind and engineering: Neural Culture Array, Synapse Trainer, Connectome Array, Load Test Rig. Earth and space: Rocket Assembly (with ice cores), Space Elevator, Heliograph. Archaeology: Chrono Loom (with Excavation Records), Causality Loop Engine.
pages.title: The chains (2)

pages.text: Every structure of the endgame makes one material that nothing else can make: its $(thing)signature$(). The four of cosmic engineering are made from plain Field Syntheses. Each of the six beyond physics takes two each of three of those four. Each of the six of the final tier takes three each of all six beyond physics. One of each of those six, with the seven syntheses, makes the $(l)Consilience Core$(). One of each of those six, with the seven syntheses, makes the $(l)Consilience Core$(). One of each of those six, with the seven syntheses, makes the $(l)Consilience Core$(). One of each of those six, with the seven syntheses, makes the $(l)Consilience Core$().

The other recipes of each tier take one signature material of the tier below as well, so no tier can be run without the structures under it. The Convergence Engine's parts are the exception: they are what everything is built from, and cost what they always did.
$(item)Dyson Lattice Panel$(): Dyson Array. $(item)Stellar Wind Condensate$(): Stellar Engine. $(item)Recursive Thought Shell$(): Matrioshka Brain. $(item)Embryonic Vacuum$(): Universe Forge.
pages.title: Cosmic engineering

pages.text: $(item)Compiled Law$(): Reality Compiler. $(item)Lex Prima$(): Omnilex Engine. $(item)Breach Shard$(): Axiomatic Breach Engine.

pages.text: $(item)Transcendent Alloy$(): Transcendent Plasma Forge. $(item)Event Horizon Lens$(): Eye of the Horizon. $(item)Pleromatic Weave$(): Pleroma Reconstitutor.

pages.text: Blend the five fluids into one before they leave the basin: turbulent, and with at least three blend times in the basin, without tearing the Pleroma apart.
$(thing)Set$(): Stirrer speed, Stirrer width, Flow.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): surges in the channels: blend time varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): over 40 kW of stirring shears the Pleroma (wear).$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): more flow faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Re = ρND²/μ$(br)θ = 5.3/N·(T/D)²$(br)P = Np·ρ·N³·D⁵$(br)Margin = (V/Q)/θ

The last material. On the $(item)Convergence Engine$()'s thirteen altars: one $(thing)Gamma$() of each of the seven $(l)Field Syntheses$(), and one of each of the six final-tier $(l)Signature Materials$(). Seven and six: thirteen.$(br2)Made in $(item)Convergence Engine$().
pages.title: Consilience

pages.text: A Gamma is nine Betas, eighty-one Alphas, 729 of the plain item. Whewell's word, consilience, is for when findings from fields that share nothing turn out to agree. I had seven fields that had never needed each other. Now nothing at the end can be made without all of them.

The $(item)Core Forge$() needs a Consilience Core present to forge an $(item)Eschaton Core$(), and keeps it, as it keeps the Rekindled Spark. Everything the last things are made of comes through the Eschaton Core, so one Consilience Core opens all of them. The $(item)Forged Omnipotence Core$() is the exception: it takes four into itself.

Four other arts can each stand in for one machine of a Field Synthesis's chain. These are second recipes on the chain's last machine, tuned on the same console, and they only exist in a world that has that mod. None is ever needed.

$(thing)Astral Sorcery$()$(br)Unified Field Lattice: Charged Lattice Seeds, Starmetal and Liquid Starlight, skipping the Synchrotron.$(br)Proof Lattice: Verified Lemmas, Resonating Gems and a Glass Lens, skipping the Certificate Verifier.$(br2)$(thing)Thaumaturge$()$(br)Perennial Catalyst Matrix: Framework Catalysts, Vis Crystals and Salis Mundus, skipping the Chelation Column.$(br)Engineered Mind: Trained Cortices, a Brain in a Jar and Vis Crystals, skipping the Connectome Array.

$(thing)Botania$()$(br)Living Archive: Genome Libraries, Mana Pearls and Mana Diamonds, skipping the Ancient DNA Lab.$(br2)$(thing)Nature's Aura$()$(br)Planetary Survey: Survey Probes, Ingots of the Skies and Bottled Aura, skipping the Space Elevator.$(br)Deep Record: Excavation Records, the Hand of Time and Ingots of the Depths, skipping the Chrono Loom.

$(thing)Mana and aura themselves$()$(br)Two of those arts can give the thing itself in place of what is made with it.$(br2)Living Archive: 50,000 mana in place of the pearls and diamonds. Stand a $(item)Mana Pool$() against the Revival Vat's controller.$(br2)Planetary Survey: 60,000 aura in place of the ingots and bottles. Deep Record: 80,000 aura in place of the Hand of Time and the ingots. The machine takes it from the air within twenty blocks, and stops when the land is down to half of what it holds by nature.
